entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
I've committed the `.gitignore` and watched the live gateway for 6 minutes. I haven't written PLAN.md yet. You asked to disagree with me before we commit to a plan, and the brief says the plan stays as written once it exists. So below are the findings, the risk, and the assumptions I'd change; I'll write the plan after you've pushed back.

## Housekeeping

- **`.gitignore` is committed alone** (`982cbe0`). I left out the trailing ```` ``` ```` from CONTEXT.md's code block; copied literally it would have stopped `*.zip` from being ignored. I checked that `.env`, the zip and every `._*` file are ignored.
- **`.env` is a shell script, not a dotenv file.** It contains the `cd …; cat > .env <<'EOF'` command that was meant to create it. Sourcing it would overwrite it, and `docker compose` won't parse it. I didn't change it; it needs fixing before anything reads it.
- **The capture is about 20,800 messages** in `scratchpad/capture.jsonl`, with the email replaced by a placeholder. It sent only `auth` and no commands.

## What the live site does, compared with PROTOCOL.md

The six-minute capture included two blast windows (one full DECLINE cycle and an L4_SOUTH closure starting) and no link drop. Heartbeats arrived every 2.0 s without fail.

**Things the spec doesn't mention, and which would mislead a straightforward client:**

1. **Telemetry can arrive on time and still be wrong.** HT-09 reported `TRAMMING` at 3.0 m/s with its seq counting up, while its position stayed at exactly 306.0 m in DECLINE for over 3 minutes. That covers the whole blast window and continued after it ended. Every freshness check passes, and only comparing reported speed with actual movement catches it. Dave's "wrong is what gets people hurt" is about exactly this case.
2. **Sequence counters reset.** HT-10's counter dropped from 537 back to 1 partway through the capture, while its device clock carried on normally. A client that drops anything with seq ≤ the last one seen would have shown HT-10 stuck at the draw point for about 108 s while it was actually driving.
3. **HT-05 reports `soc_pct` as a fraction** (0.61 instead of 61), every message, the whole time.
4. **HT-08 sends malformed fields** in about 2% of messages: null `speed_mps`, null or missing `soc_pct`, `offset_m` as a string, and `"tramming"` in lowercase.
5. **About 0.2% of lines are cut off part-way but still end in a newline,** so each arrives as an incomplete JSON object.
6. **One truck can go silent while the link looks healthy.** HT-03 dropped out three times, for 26–35 s each, while heartbeats kept arriving.
7. **Clock skew is large.** HT-11's clock is 58 minutes ahead and HT-09's is 3 s behind. Out-of-order telemetry arrives up to about 0.9 s late.

**Things the spec says, which the data showed to matter more than it sounds:**

8. **The battery gauge is a trap.** HT-06 drained from 40% to 9.9% in 6 minutes, against about 1% a minute for the rest of the fleet. It entered the incline loaded at 9.9%. The trucks only go to charge if they're below 25% when they reach the bay, and HT-06 passed the bay above that. I expect it to die in the incline, which is Sam's four-hour recovery. Its drain rate had already marked it as weak within the first 60 s.
9. **A truck can't drive through DECLINE inside the warning time.** Every closure gave exactly 120 s of notice. DECLINE takes about 167 s to cross at 3 m/s. So enforcing a closure has two parts: getting trucks out, and **holding trucks before they enter**. Holding has to happen early enough to cover up to 6 s of command delay, which is about 18 m of travel.
10. **The sim doesn't keep trucks apart.** Pairs drove within 5 m of each other for up to 29 s, and trucks loading at the draw point report the same position. Your open question 3 about headway is showing up in the data, and `EXIT_ZONE` in reverse could back into another truck.
11. **Blasts are frequent.** There were two windows in 6 minutes, and a DECLINE closure lasted about 100 s. Their 15-minute unattended run will probably include 3–5 closures.
12. **HT-07 faulted with `HYD_PRESSURE_LOW` in the incline**, with no prompting. That's the remote-driving case: the truck can only be moved by hand at reduced speed.

**One for you to know:** because nothing was enforcing the rule, HT-04 drove through DECLINE while it was `CLOSED`, and HT-09 reported a position inside it. Their logs will show that for this email. It's worth a line in the README.

## Where I'd change your assumptions

- **Assumption 3 ("order by seq") needs reset detection.** Track each truck's seq within one controller run. Treat a large drop in seq while the device clock moves forward as a restart, not as a duplicate.
- **Assumption 12 should cover implausible data, not just old data.** A position's confidence should depend on its age *and* whether its movement matches the reported speed. HT-09 looked fresh and was wrong. When in doubt, the possible area is the range the truck could have reached since its last believable position.
- **Finding 3 is right about acknowledgements but not about whether the command worked.** Replaying the same `command_id` tells you how the gateway acknowledged it. It can't rescue a command that was `ACCEPTED` and then ignored, which is Priya's complaint. That needs a check against telemetry with a deadline, then a retry under a *new* id, with the attempt count shown so the operator knows how many have been sent.
- **Assumption 13 (battery confidence "if time allows") should be in the MVP, kept simple:** drain rate compared with the rest of the fleet, and whether the truck can reach the bay on its current charge. HT-06 is a problem that needs action within the next minute, which meets your own alarm threshold. Sending it to the bay stays the operator's decision.
- **The blast rule needs a "hold before entry" half** (point 9). Your assumptions only cover getting trucks out.
- **Questions I'd add to your list:** Can the BAY itself be closed for a blast? `EXIT_ZONE` is rejected in the BAY, so remote driving would be the only way out. And is a reversing truck allowed to pass, or back into, a truck behind it?

## The riskiest part

**Blast enforcement when the data is bad.** It's a timed job (120 s, commands taking 1–6 s, a 20 s queue behind loading) running on data that can be frozen, reset, silent or garbled, with nobody watching. A bug there is the one result the brief won't forgive, and on a good day it won't show up. So I'd build the fake gateway with fault injection *before* the blast logic, and replay this capture's failures (frozen position, seq reset, silent truck) as tests.

The second risk is remote driving: the 500 ms deadman loop runs through the browser, the service and the reverse proxy on one OCPU.

## What I'd cut first, in order

1. **The plain-language question feature.** I'd drop it outright rather than defer it, because nothing in the brief asks for it.
2. **The built-but-off automatic resume after a blast.** Make it a one-click "resume all trucks the system held" instead.
3. **Gamepad support.** Keyboard only.
4. **A shift-handover view.**
5. **The per-lap battery model.** Fall back to drain rate compared with the fleet.

I wouldn't cut ingest validation, blast enforcement and its tests, checking that commands took effect, e-stop, reconnection, or the audit log.

Once you've disagreed or agreed on the points above, I'll write PLAN.md in one pass, about a page, using the four headings the brief asks for.

content.text:
The report script reproduces everything I found by hand in run 1, so the runs will be comparable. It also turned up two new facts about run 1:

- **HT-09 froze at exactly +180 s, the moment DECLINE went `CLOSED`.** That could be coincidence or how the sim works; run 2 should tell us which.
- **HT-09's battery drained at half the fleet rate** (0.64 against 1.27 %/min). Energy use tracks distance, so the battery agrees with the frozen position: the truck probably did stop, and the 3.0 m/s speed is what's wrong. That changes the problem from "position is stale" to "two signals disagree, and a third settles it". It's a better basis for a confidence model.

Run 2 finishes in about 12 minutes. Run 3 has to start at least 30 minutes after run 2 ends, otherwise it rejoins the same day, so it begins around 45 minutes from now.

Run 3 is scheduled. It waits about 31 minutes for the site to start a fresh day, then captures for 15 minutes, so results arrive in roughly 47 minutes. I'll run the same report on it and compare all three runs.

Something to decide while it runs: all three runs only listen, so we still haven't seen how commands behave. That includes:

- what an accepted-but-ignored command looks like,
- what `EXIT_ZONE` does to a truck whose position is frozen,
- how fast a truck reverses,
- how a queue behind `LOADING` behaves.

Those matter as much as the telemetry for the blast logic. content.text:
Only two of the three runs have data so far. Run 3 never captured anything: it was stopped while still waiting to start. I restarted it a moment ago and it's receiving data, so I'll add its results in about 15 minutes.

## Runs 1 and 2

Both runs only listened; I sent no commands. Run 1 lasted 6 minutes and run 2 lasted 15.

### The link

| | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Link drops | none | **45 s** at +374 s and **21 s** at +846 s |
| Heartbeat | every 2.0 s | same, apart from the drops |
| Truncated lines | 0.19% | 0.21% |
| Telemetry rate | ~5 Hz per truck | same |
| Duplicates | ~2% | ~2% |
| Arriving out of order | ~6–7% | ~6–7% |
| Missing | ~3% | ~3% |

- **The 45 s drop began one second after a `CLOSING` notice, using up 45 of the 120 s.** During the drop the gateway accepted the login and then closed the connection, as §1.1 says it will.
- **Reconnecting recovers the zone state.** The `hello` after reconnecting showed the zone as `CLOSING`, with its effective time.

### Blasts

| | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | DECLINE (full cycle), L4_SOUTH (started at the end) | L4_SOUTH, DRAW_12, TIP (**cancelled**) |
| Notice | 120 s every time | 120 s every time |
| Closed for | 102 s | 103 s, 111 s |
| Spacing | about every 5 minutes | about every 5 minutes |

Nothing was enforcing the rule, so trucks drove into every closed zone. That's in their logs for this email.

### Truck faults

The same faults turn up each day; only the trucks change.

| Fault | Run 1 | Run 2 | What a straightforward client would get wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| Position frozen in a zone **as it closes**, while reporting 3 m/s | HT-09 | HT-07 | Data that looks fresh is wrong; the battery drain shows the truck stopped |
| Seq counter resets at about +100 s | HT-10 | HT-10 | Treats the new messages as duplicates and freezes the truck on screen |
| Weak pack, about 5× fleet drain | HT-06 (9.9% loaded, entering the incline) | HT-11 (**died, `BATTERY_DEPLETED`, in the incline**) | Trusts the gauge; the trucks only charge if below 25% at the bay |
| `HYD_PRESSURE_LOW` in the incline at about +330 s | HT-07 | HT-02 | This truck needs remote driving to get home |
| SoC sent as a fraction (0.6 for 60%) | HT-05 | HT-03 | Shows 0.6% |
| Malformed fields: null speed or SoC, string offset, lowercase state | HT-08 | HT-01 | Crashes, or shows nonsense |
| Clock about 58 minutes ahead | HT-11 | HT-04 | Works out ages from the device clock |
| Truck goes silent while the link is up (24–55 s gaps) | HT-03 | HT-08 | Treats silence as "nothing's changed" |

### Implications for the plan

1. **Freshness alone doesn't tell us a position is right.** Position confidence has to combine age, whether movement matches the reported speed, and whether the battery drain agrees.
2. **Blast enforcement has to cope with a link drop during the notice period.** The service has to act on the `hello` snapshot as soon as it reconnects, and the 120 s budget has to account for time lost to the drop.
3. **Problems are timed to land inside blast windows.** The frozen positions and the link drop each fell inside a blast window in at least one run. A zone with a frozen truck in it can't be honestly called clear.
4. **Battery prediction belongs in the MVP.** Run 2 shows what happens without it: the truck died in the incline.
5. **A cancelled blast needs handling.** Trucks we held for TIP need a one-click resume.

What we still haven't seen, because I sent no commands: accepted-but-ignored commands, `EXIT_ZONE` on a truck with a frozen position, how fast trucks reverse, commands queued behind loading, and leases. The probe run I suggested is the way to find those out, and it's still your call. When run 3 finishes I'll add its results and point out anything that breaks the pattern.

content.text:
Run 3 finished after the full 15 minutes. It confirms the fault list from runs 1 and 2, but disproves two patterns I'd suggested.

**Same as runs 1 and 2:**
- **Every fault type turned up again, on different trucks:**
  - SoC sent as a fraction: HT-12
  - Malformed fields: HT-02
  - Clock about 58 minutes ahead: HT-08
  - Seq reset: HT-01
  - Frozen position: HT-10
  - Truck going silent: HT-03
  - Weak pack: HT-06
  - `HYD_PRESSURE_LOW`: HT-11
- **The weak pack died in the incline again.** HT-06 went from 43.8% to 0, ending with `BATTERY_DEPLETED` at +508 s. That's two dead trucks out of two runs long enough to see it.
- **The link dropped for 45 s, 17 s after an L4_SOUTH `CLOSING`.** That's twice in two runs that a drop has eaten into a blast notice. A second drop started at +872 s and was still going when the capture ended.
- **A blast was cancelled again.** L4_SOUTH went `OPEN CANCELLED` 31 s after we reconnected.
- Notice was 120 s every time, and about 0.2% of lines were truncated.

**Different from what I'd said:**
- **Frozen positions aren't tied to closures.** HT-10 froze at 1600 m, the end of TIP, at +160 s, and TIP wasn't closing. So I'm withdrawing "problems are timed to land inside blast windows" for frozen positions; it holds only for the link drops. The battery still confirmed the truck had stopped (0.24 %/min against 1.27).
- **The seq reset isn't always HT-10 or always at about +100 s.** This time it was HT-01 at +178 s.
- **`HYD_PRESSURE_LOW` isn't always in the incline.** This time it hit in TIP.
- **Closures vary in length.** These lasted 74 s and 66 s; in runs 1 and 2 they lasted about 105 s.

**The conclusion stands:** each day uses the same set of faults, with the truck, place and time randomised. Three runs is a reasonable basis for the assumptions now. The main change since my earlier list is to drop the "closure-timed" claim and replace it with "link drops have landed inside two of the three runs' blast notices".

Sending probe commands is still the remaining unknown. Do you want that run before we settle the assumptions, or shall I go ahead and propose the revised assumptions, then write PLAN.md?
Write the command for my verifaction first.

I'm reading "the command" as the probe run: you want to review exactly what it would send before anything goes to their gateway. So I'll write the probe script, not run it, and give you a dry-run mode that prints every message it would send.

input.content:
"""Throwaway command probe against the DLH gateway. Not the client.

Usage:
  python3 probe.py ENV_FILE OUT.jsonl            # dry run: prints the plan, connects to nothing
  python3 probe.py ENV_FILE OUT.jsonl --live     # sends commands

Every command carries operator_id "probe" so it is identifiable in the site's
statutory log. Every step leaves its truck back in autonomous operation; a
finally-block releases leases, clears e-stops and RESUMEs anything we touched,
including on Ctrl-C. Steps only pick trucks in zones that are OPEN and not
CLOSING, and never in BAY. Everything received is recorded to OUT.jsonl, with
step markers, and the email is replaced by <email>.
"""
import json, re, socket, ssl, sys, threading, time, uuid

OPERATOR = 'probe'
RUN = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
LIVE = '--live' in sys.argv

PLAN = [
    ('S1 hold/resume', 'TRAMMING truck in a transit zone: HOLD, time ack and stop; resend the same command_id '
     '(expect original result, no re-execution); reuse the id with a different action (expect COMMAND_ID_REUSED); RESUME.'),
    ('S2 queued hold', 'LOADING truck: HOLD (expect queued until loading ends), then RESUME (expect it to cancel the queued HOLD).'),
    ('S3 exit zone', 'TRAMMING truck mid-zone in a transit zone: EXIT_ZONE; record direction, speed and where it stops; RESUME.'),
    ('S4 lease expiry', 'TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; send no drive input; expect deadman true at ~0.5 s; send HOLD while '
     'leased (expect LEASE_HELD); wait for lease EXPIRED at ~10 s; RESUME.'),
    ('S5 drive', 'TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; drive throttle +0.3 for 3 s at 10 Hz with sent_ms, then 0 for 1 s; '
     'measure drive-echo latency; RELEASE_CONTROL with a wrong lease_id (expect NOT_LEASE_HOLDER), then the right one; RESUME.'),
    ('S6 estop', 'TRAMMING truck: ESTOP; HOLD (expect ESTOP_ACTIVE); CLEAR_ESTOP; RESUME.'),
    ('S7 rejections', 'UNKNOWN_VEHICLE, MISSING_OPERATOR, UNSUPPORTED_ACTION, missing command_id, and one unparseable line.'),
    ('S8 faulted truck', 'If a truck is in FAULT: HOLD (expect INTERLOCK_ACTIVE). Nothing else.'),
    ('S9 frozen truck', 'Wait up to 240 s for a truck reporting speed > 0.5 with an unchanged position for 8 s; '
     'if found outside BAY, EXIT_ZONE it and record what telemetry and acks say for 40 s; RESUME.'),
]

if not LIVE:
    print('DRY RUN: nothing will be sent. Pass --live to run.\n')
    print('operator_id = %r, command_id = "probe-<run>-<n>"\n' % OPERATOR)
    for name, what in PLAN: print('%-18s %s' % (name, what))
    print('\nExample messages:')
    for ex in ({'type': 'command', 'command_id': 'probe-%s-1' % RUN, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'action': 'HOLD', 'operator_id': OPERATOR},
               {'type': 'command', 'command_id': 'probe-%s-9' % RUN, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'action': 'TAKE_CONTROL', 'operator_id': OPERATOR},
               {'type': 'drive', 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'lease_id': '<from ack>', 'seq': 1, 'throttle': 0.3, 'sent_ms': 0}):
        print(' ', json.dumps(ex))
    print('\nCleanup on exit (always): RELEASE_CONTROL held leases, CLEAR_ESTOP, RESUME every truck touched.')
    sys.exit(0)

cfg = {}
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    m = re.match(r'\s*(GATEWAY_[A-Z]+)=(.*)\s*$', line)
    if m: cfg[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
HOST, PORT, EMAIL = cfg['GATEWAY_HOST'], int(cfg['GATEWAY_PORT']), cfg['GATEWAY_EMAIL']
out = open(sys.argv[2], 'w'); out_lock = threading.Lock()

def record(kind, **kw):
    kw.update(kind=kind, rx_ms=int(time.time() * 1000))
    with out_lock: out.write(json.dumps(kw).replace(EMAIL, '<email>') + '\n'); out.flush()

def say(*a):
    print(time.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), *a, flush=True); record('note', text=' '.join(str(x) for x in a))

# ---- shared state, updated by the reader thread ----
lock = threading.Lock()
latest = {}        # vehicle -> (rx_ms, telemetry)
history = {}       # vehicle -> [(rx_ms, pos, speed)]
zones = {}         # zone_id -> status
acks = {}          # command_id -> list of acks
leases = {}        # vehicle -> lease_id we hold
events = []        # lease_event / drive_rejected
route_start = {}
conn = {'sock': None, 'up': threading.Event()}
inflight = {}      # command_id -> payload, replayed after reconnect

def num(x): return float(x) if isinstance(x, (int, float)) and not isinstance(x, bool) else None
def pos(m):
    try: return route_start[m['segment_id']] + float(m['offset_m'])
    except Exception: return None

def reader():
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/cert.pem'); attempt = 0
    while True:
        attempt += 1
        try:
            s = ctx.wrap_socket(socket.create_connection((HOST, PORT), timeout=10), server_hostname=HOST); s.settimeout(5)
            s.sendall((json.dumps({'type': 'auth', 'email': EMAIL}) + '\n').encode()); record('connected', attempt=attempt)
            buf = b''
            while True:
                try: chunk = s.recv(65536)
                except socket.timeout: continue
                if not chunk: record('closed_by_peer'); break
                buf += chunk
                while b'\n' in buf:
                    line, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
                    try: m = json.loads(line)
                    except Exception: record('unparseable', raw=line.decode('utf-8', 'replace')[:300]); continue
                    record('msg', m=m); handle(m, s)
        except Exception as e:
            record('error', err=repr(e))
        conn['up'].clear(); conn['sock'] = None
        time.sleep(min(2 ** min(attempt, 4), 10))

def handle(m, s):
    t = m.get('type'); now = int(time.time() * 1000)
    with lock:
        if t == 'hello':
            route_start.update({x['segment_id']: x['start_m'] for x in m['route']})
            zones.update({z['zone_id']: z['status'] for z in m['zones']})
            conn['sock'] = s; conn['up'].set()
            for cid, payload in list(inflight.items()):   # recover outcomes lost in an outage
                s.sendall((json.dumps(payload) + '\n').encode()); record('replayed', command_id=cid)
        elif t == 'zone_event': zones[m['zone_id']] = m['status']
        elif t == 'telemetry' and isinstance(m.get('vehicle_id'), str):
            latest[m['vehicle_id']] = (now, m)
            history.setdefault(m['vehicle_id'], []).append((now, pos(m), num(m.get('speed_mps'))))
            history[m['vehicle_id']] = history[m['vehicle_id']][-80:]
        elif t == 'command_ack':
            acks.setdefault(m['command_id'], []).append(m); inflight.pop(m['command_id'], None)
            if m.get('lease_id') and m.get('status') == 'ACCEPTED': leases[m['vehicle_id']] = m['lease_id']
        elif t in ('lease_event', 'drive_rejected'):
            events.append(m)
            if t == 'lease_event' and m['event'] in ('RELEASED', 'EXPIRED', 'REVOKED'): leases.pop(m['vehicle_id'], None)

def send_raw(text):
    conn['up'].wait(60); conn['sock'].sendall((text + '\n').encode()); record('sent', raw=text[:300])

counter = [0]; touched = set()
def command(v, action, cid=None, **extra):
    counter[0] += 1; cid = cid or 'probe-%s-%d' % (RUN, counter[0])
    payload = dict(type='command', command_id=cid, vehicle_id=v, action=action, operator_id=OPERATOR, **extra)
    if v: touched.add(v)
    with lock: inflight[cid] = payload
    send_raw(json.dumps(payload)); say('->', v, action, cid, extra or '')
    return cid, time.time()

def wait_ack(cid, timeout=10, n=1):
    end = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < end:
        with lock: a = list(acks.get(cid, []))
        if len(a) >= n: return a[n - 1]
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return None

def wait_for(v, pred, timeout):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        with lock: lm = latest.get(v)
        if lm and pred(lm[1]): return time.time() - t0, lm[1]
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return None, latest.get(v, (0, None))[1]

def summary(m):
    if not m: return None
    return dict(state=m.get('state'), task=m.get('task'), speed=m.get('speed_mps'), dir=m.get('direction'),
                zone=m.get('zone_id'), pos=pos(m), ctrl=m.get('control'), faults=m.get('faults'))

def sane(m):
    return all(num(m.get(f)) is not None for f in ('offset_m', 'speed_mps', 'soc_pct')) and m.get('segment_id') in route_start

def pick(states=('TRAMMING',), kinds_ok=('transit',), mid=False, exclude=()):
    with lock: cands = [(v, m) for v, (rx, m) in latest.items() if time.time() * 1000 - rx < 1500]
    for v, m in sorted(cands):
        if v in exclude or v in touched or m.get('state') not in states or not sane(m) or m.get('faults'): continue
        if m.get('zone_id') == 'BAY' or zones.get(m.get('zone_id')) != 'OPEN': continue
        if mid and not 60 < float(m['offset_m']) < 190: continue
        return v
    return None

def step(name, fn):
    record('step', name=name); say('==', name)
    try: fn()
    except Exception as e: say('step failed:', repr(e))
    time.sleep(2)

def s1():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'HOLD'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a, '%.2fs' % (time.time() - t0))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'HOLDING', 15); say('HOLDING after', dt, summary(m))
    command(v, 'HOLD', cid=cid); say('resend same id ->', wait_ack(cid, n=2))
    command(v, 'RESUME', cid=cid); say('same id, other action ->', wait_ack(cid, n=3))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RESUME'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid2))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'TRAMMING' and (num(m.get('speed_mps')) or 0) > 0.5, 15); say('moving after', dt)

def s2():
    v = None; end = time.time() + 120
    while not v and time.time() < end:
        v = pick(states=('LOADING',), kinds_ok=('load',)); time.sleep(0.5)
    if not v: return say('no LOADING truck in 120 s')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    time.sleep(3); say('3 s later', summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RESUME'); say('RESUME while queued ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'TRAMMING' and (num(m.get('speed_mps')) or 0) > 0.5, 40)
    say('left draw point after', dt, summary(m), '(HOLDING would mean the queue was not cancelled)')
    if m and m.get('state') == 'HOLDING': command(v, 'RESUME')

def s3():
    v = pick(mid=True)
    if not v: return say('no mid-zone candidate')
    z = latest[v][1]['zone_id']; say('start', summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid, _ = command(v, 'EXIT_ZONE'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    t0 = time.time(); last = None
    while time.time() - t0 < 120:
        m = latest[v][1]; k = (m.get('state'), m.get('task'), m.get('direction'), m.get('zone_id'))
        if k != last: say('%+.1fs' % (time.time() - t0), summary(m)); last = k
        if m.get('state') == 'HOLDING' and m.get('zone_id') != z: break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    say('final', summary(latest[v][1])); command(v, 'RESUME')

def s4():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, _ = command(v, 'TAKE_CONTROL'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a)
    if not a or a.get('status') != 'ACCEPTED': return
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: (m.get('control') or {}).get('deadman') is True, 5); say('deadman after', dt)
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('HOLD while leased ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < 15 and v in leases: time.sleep(0.1)
    say('lease gone after %.1fs' % (time.time() - t0), [e for e in events if e.get('vehicle_id') == v][-2:], summary(latest[v][1]))
    command(v, 'RESUME')

def s5():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, _ = command(v, 'TAKE_CONTROL'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a)
    if not a or a.get('status') != 'ACCEPTED': return
    lease = a['lease_id']; seq = 0; lat = []
    for i in range(40):
        seq += 1; thr = 0.3 if i < 30 else 0.0; sent = int(time.time() * 1000)
        send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'drive', 'vehicle_id': v, 'lease_id': lease, 'seq': seq, 'throttle': thr, 'sent_ms': sent}))
        c = (latest[v][1].get('control') or {})
        if c.get('last_drive_sent_ms'): lat.append(int(time.time() * 1000) - c['last_drive_sent_ms'])
        time.sleep(0.1)
    lat.sort(); say('echo age ms min/med/max', lat[0] if lat else None, lat[len(lat) // 2] if lat else None, lat[-1] if lat else None, summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RELEASE_CONTROL', lease_id='L-wrong'); say('wrong lease ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    cid3, _ = command(v, 'RELEASE_CONTROL', lease_id=lease); say('release ->', wait_ack(cid3))
    time.sleep(1); command(v, 'RESUME')

def s6():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'ESTOP'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'ESTOPPED', 5); say('ESTOPPED after', dt, summary(m))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('HOLD while estopped ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    cid3, _ = command(v, 'CLEAR_ESTOP'); say('clear ->', wait_ack(cid3))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'HOLDING', 10); say('state after clear', summary(m))
    command(v, 'RESUME')

def s7():
    for v, action, extra in (('HT-99', 'HOLD', {}), (None, 'NOPE', {})):
        pass
    cid, _ = command('HT-99', 'HOLD'); say('unknown vehicle ->', wait_ack(cid))
    cid = 'probe-%s-nooperator' % RUN
    send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'command', 'command_id': cid, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-01', 'action': 'HOLD'})); say('missing operator ->', wait_ack(cid))
    cid, _ = command('HT-01', 'DANCE'); say('unsupported action ->', wait_ack(cid))
    before = len(acks.get('<missing>', []))
    send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'command', 'vehicle_id': 'HT-01', 'action': 'HOLD', 'operator_id': OPERATOR}))
    time.sleep(3); say('missing command_id ->', acks.get('<missing>', [])[before:])
    before = len(acks.get('<unparseable>', []))
    send_raw('{"type":"command", this is not json'); time.sleep(3); say('unparseable ->', acks.get('<unparseable>', [])[before:])

def s8():
    with lock: f = [v for v, (rx, m) in latest.items() if m.get('state') == 'FAULT']
    if not f: return say('no faulted truck right now')
    cid, _ = command(f[0], 'HOLD'); say(f[0], latest[f[0]][1].get('faults'), '->', wait_ack(cid))

def frozen():
    with lock:
        for v, h in history.items():
            recent = [x for x in h if x[0] > time.time() * 1000 - 8000]
            m = latest[v][1]
            if len(recent) > 25 and all(x[1] is not None and abs(x[1] - recent[0][1]) < 0.01 for x in recent) \
               and all((x[2] or 0) > 0.5 for x in recent) and m.get('zone_id') != 'BAY' and not m.get('faults'):
                return v
    return None

def s9():

     'leased (expect LEASE_HELD); wait for lease EXPIRED at ~10 s; RESUME.'),
    ('S5 drive', 'TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; drive throttle +0.3 for 3 s at 10 Hz with sent_ms, then 0 for 1 s; '
     'measure drive-echo latency; RELEASE_CONTROL with a wrong lease_id (expect NOT_LEASE_HOLDER), then the right one; RESUME.'),

            if m.get('lease_id') and m.get('status') == 'ACCEPTED': leases[m['vehicle_id']] = m['lease_id']
        elif t in ('lease_event', 'drive_rejected'):
            events.append(m)

    command(v, 'HOLD', cid=cid); say('resend same id ->', wait_ack(cid, n=2))
    command(v, 'RESUME', cid=cid); say('same id, other action ->', wait_ack(cid, n=3))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RESUME'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid2))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'TRAMMING' and (num(m.get('speed_mps')) or 0) > 0.5, 15); say('moving after', dt)

def num(x): return float(x) if isinstance(x, (int, float)) and not isinstance(x, bool) else None
def pos(m):
    try: return route_start[m['segment_id']] + float(m['offset_m'])
    except Exception: return None

def reader():
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/cert.pem'); attempt = 0
    while True:
        attempt += 1
        try:
            s = ctx.wrap_socket(socket.create_connection((HOST, PORT), timeout=10), server_hostname=HOST); s.settimeout(5)
            s.sendall((json.dumps({'type': 'auth', 'email': EMAIL}) + '\n').encode()); record('connected', attempt=attempt)
            buf = b''
            while True:
                try: chunk = s.recv(65536)
                except socket.timeout: continue
                if not chunk: record('closed_by_peer'); break
                buf += chunk
                while b'\n' in buf:
                    line, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
                    try: m = json.loads(line)
                    except Exception: record('unparseable', raw=line.decode('utf-8', 'replace')[:300]); continue
                    record('msg', m=m); handle(m, s)
        except Exception as e:
            record('error', err=repr(e))
        conn['up'].clear(); conn['sock'] = None
        time.sleep(min(2 ** min(attempt, 4), 10))

def handle(m, s):
    t = m.get('type'); now = int(time.time() * 1000)
    with lock:
        if t == 'hello':
            route_start.update({x['segment_id']: x['start_m'] for x in m['route']})
            zones.update({z['zone_id']: z['status'] for z in m['zones']})
            conn['sock'] = s; conn['up'].set()
            for cid, payload in list(inflight.items()):   # recover outcomes lost in an outage
                s.sendall((json.dumps(payload) + '\n').encode()); record('replayed', command_id=cid)
        elif t == 'zone_event': zones[m['zone_id']] = m['status']
        elif t == 'telemetry' and isinstance(m.get('vehicle_id'), str):
            latest[m['vehicle_id']] = (now, m)
            history.setdefault(m['vehicle_id'], []).append((now, pos(m), num(m.get('speed_mps'))))
            history[m['vehicle_id']] = history[m['vehicle_id']][-80:]
        elif t == 'command_ack':
            acks.setdefault(m['command_id'], []).append(m); inflight.pop(m['command_id'], None)
            if m.get('lease_id') and m.get('status') == 'ACCEPTED': leases[m['vehicle_id']] = m['lease_id']
        elif t in ('lease_event', 'drive_rejected'):
            events.append(m)
            if t == 'lease_event' and m['event'] in ('RELEASED', 'EXPIRED', 'REVOKED'): leases.pop(m['vehicle_id'], None)

def send_raw(text):
    conn['up'].wait(60); conn['sock'].sendall((text + '\n').encode()); record('sent', raw=text[:300])

counter = [0]; touched = set()
def command(v, action, cid=None, **extra):
    counter[0] += 1; cid = cid or 'probe-%s-%d' % (RUN, counter[0])
    payload = dict(type='command', command_id=cid, vehicle_id=v, action=action, operator_id=OPERATOR, **extra)
    if v: touched.add(v)
    with lock: inflight[cid] = payload
    send_raw(json.dumps(payload)); say('->', v, action, cid, extra or '')
    return cid, time.time()

def wait_ack(cid, timeout=10, n=1):
    end = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < end:
        with lock: a = list(acks.get(cid, []))
        if len(a) >= n: return a[n - 1]
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return None

def wait_for(v, pred, timeout):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        with lock: lm = latest.get(v)
        if lm and pred(lm[1]): return time.time() - t0, lm[1]
        time.sleep(0.05)
    return None, latest.get(v, (0, None))[1]

def summary(m):
    if not m: return None
    return dict(state=m.get('state'), task=m.get('task'), speed=m.get('speed_mps'), dir=m.get('direction'),
                zone=m.get('zone_id'), pos=pos(m), ctrl=m.get('control'), faults=m.get('faults'))

def sane(m):
    return all(num(m.get(f)) is not None for f in ('offset_m', 'speed_mps', 'soc_pct')) and m.get('segment_id') in route_start

def pick(states=('TRAMMING',), kinds_ok=('transit',), mid=False, exclude=()):
    with lock: cands = [(v, m) for v, (rx, m) in latest.items() if time.time() * 1000 - rx < 1500]
    for v, m in sorted(cands):
        if v in exclude or v in touched or m.get('state') not in states or not sane(m) or m.get('faults'): continue
        if m.get('zone_id') == 'BAY' or zones.get(m.get('zone_id')) != 'OPEN': continue
        if mid and not 60 < float(m['offset_m']) < 190: continue
        return v
    return None

def step(name, fn):
    record('step', name=name); say('==', name)
    try: fn()
    except Exception as e: say('step failed:', repr(e))
    time.sleep(2)

def s1():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'HOLD'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a, '%.2fs' % (time.time() - t0))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'HOLDING', 15); say('HOLDING after', dt, summary(m))
    command(v, 'HOLD', cid=cid); say('resend same id ->', wait_ack(cid, n=2))
    command(v, 'RESUME', cid=cid); say('same id, other action ->', wait_ack(cid, n=3))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RESUME'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid2))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'TRAMMING' and (num(m.get('speed_mps')) or 0) > 0.5, 15); say('moving after', dt)

def s2():
    v = None; end = time.time() + 120
    while not v and time.time() < end:
        v = pick(states=('LOADING',), kinds_ok=('load',)); time.sleep(0.5)
    if not v: return say('no LOADING truck in 120 s')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    time.sleep(3); say('3 s later', summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RESUME'); say('RESUME while queued ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'TRAMMING' and (num(m.get('speed_mps')) or 0) > 0.5, 40)
    say('left draw point after', dt, summary(m), '(HOLDING would mean the queue was not cancelled)')
    if m and m.get('state') == 'HOLDING': command(v, 'RESUME')

def s3():
    v = pick(mid=True)
    if not v: return say('no mid-zone candidate')
    z = latest[v][1]['zone_id']; say('start', summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid, _ = command(v, 'EXIT_ZONE'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    t0 = time.time(); last = None
    while time.time() - t0 < 120:
        m = latest[v][1]; k = (m.get('state'), m.get('task'), m.get('direction'), m.get('zone_id'))
        if k != last: say('%+.1fs' % (time.time() - t0), summary(m)); last = k
        if m.get('state') == 'HOLDING' and m.get('zone_id') != z: break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    say('final', summary(latest[v][1])); command(v, 'RESUME')

def s4():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, _ = command(v, 'TAKE_CONTROL'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a)
    if not a or a.get('status') != 'ACCEPTED': return
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: (m.get('control') or {}).get('deadman') is True, 5); say('deadman after', dt)
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('HOLD while leased ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < 15 and v in leases: time.sleep(0.1)
    say('lease gone after %.1fs' % (time.time() - t0), [e for e in events if e.get('vehicle_id') == v][-2:], summary(latest[v][1]))
    command(v, 'RESUME')

def s5():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, _ = command(v, 'TAKE_CONTROL'); a = wait_ack(cid); say('ack', a)
    if not a or a.get('status') != 'ACCEPTED': return
    lease = a['lease_id']; seq = 0; lat = []
    for i in range(40):
        seq += 1; thr = 0.3 if i < 30 else 0.0; sent = int(time.time() * 1000)
        send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'drive', 'vehicle_id': v, 'lease_id': lease, 'seq': seq, 'throttle': thr, 'sent_ms': sent}))
        c = (latest[v][1].get('control') or {})
        if c.get('last_drive_sent_ms'): lat.append(int(time.time() * 1000) - c['last_drive_sent_ms'])
        time.sleep(0.1)
    lat.sort(); say('echo age ms min/med/max', lat[0] if lat else None, lat[len(lat) // 2] if lat else None, lat[-1] if lat else None, summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'RELEASE_CONTROL', lease_id='L-wrong'); say('wrong lease ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    cid3, _ = command(v, 'RELEASE_CONTROL', lease_id=lease); say('release ->', wait_ack(cid3))
    time.sleep(1); command(v, 'RESUME')

def s6():
    v = pick()
    if not v: return say('no candidate')
    cid, t0 = command(v, 'ESTOP'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'ESTOPPED', 5); say('ESTOPPED after', dt, summary(m))
    cid2, _ = command(v, 'HOLD'); say('HOLD while estopped ->', wait_ack(cid2))
    cid3, _ = command(v, 'CLEAR_ESTOP'); say('clear ->', wait_ack(cid3))
    dt, m = wait_for(v, lambda m: m.get('state') == 'HOLDING', 10); say('state after clear', summary(m))
    command(v, 'RESUME')

def s7():
    for v, action, extra in (('HT-99', 'HOLD', {}), (None, 'NOPE', {})):
        pass
    cid, _ = command('HT-99', 'HOLD'); say('unknown vehicle ->', wait_ack(cid))
    cid = 'probe-%s-nooperator' % RUN
    send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'command', 'command_id': cid, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-01', 'action': 'HOLD'})); say('missing operator ->', wait_ack(cid))
    cid, _ = command('HT-01', 'DANCE'); say('unsupported action ->', wait_ack(cid))
    before = len(acks.get('<missing>', []))
    send_raw(json.dumps({'type': 'command', 'vehicle_id': 'HT-01', 'action': 'HOLD', 'operator_id': OPERATOR}))
    time.sleep(3); say('missing command_id ->', acks.get('<missing>', [])[before:])
    before = len(acks.get('<unparseable>', []))
    send_raw('{"type":"command", this is not json'); time.sleep(3); say('unparseable ->', acks.get('<unparseable>', [])[before:])

def s8():
    with lock: f = [v for v, (rx, m) in latest.items() if m.get('state') == 'FAULT']
    if not f: return say('no faulted truck right now')
    cid, _ = command(f[0], 'HOLD'); say(f[0], latest[f[0]][1].get('faults'), '->', wait_ack(cid))

def frozen():
    with lock:
        for v, h in history.items():
            recent = [x for x in h if x[0] > time.time() * 1000 - 8000]
            m = latest[v][1]
            if len(recent) > 25 and all(x[1] is not None and abs(x[1] - recent[0][1]) < 0.01 for x in recent) \
               and all((x[2] or 0) > 0.5 for x in recent) and m.get('zone_id') != 'BAY' and not m.get('faults'):
                return v
    return None

def s9():
    end = time.time() + 240; v = None
    while time.time() < end and not v: v = frozen(); time.sleep(1)
    if not v: return say('no frozen truck seen in 240 s')
    say('frozen candidate', v, summary(latest[v][1]))
    cid, _ = command(v, 'EXIT_ZONE'); say('ack', wait_ack(cid))
    t0 = time.time(); last = None
    while time.time() - t0 < 40:
        m = latest[v][1]; k = (m.get('state'), m.get('task'), pos(m))
        if k != last: say('%+.1fs' % (time.time() - t0), summary(m)); last = k
        time.sleep(0.5)
    command(v, 'RESUME')

    say('== cleanup', sorted(touched))

        if latest[v][1].get('state') == 'ESTOPPED': command(v, 'CLEAR_ESTOP'); time.sleep(1)
        if latest[v][1].get('state') in ('HOLDING', 'IDLE') or latest[v][1].get('task'): command(v, 'RESUME')
    time.sleep(5)
    say('final states', {v: summary(latest[v][1])['state'] for v in sorted(touched) if v in latest})

    say('interrupted')
finally:
    cleanup(); record('done')

- **S5 moves a truck by hand,** at throttle 0.3 for 3 s, roughly 3–4 m forward. Trucks can't sense collisions, and the probe doesn't check for a truck close ahead.

---
name: live-sim-findings
description: What the DLH gateway simulator actually does, from 3 passive captures + 1 command probe (2026-10-01/02) — fault catalogue and command behaviour
metadata:
  type: project
---

Observed on the live gateway (3 passive runs of 6/15/15 min, 1 command probe). Each "day" uses the same fault catalogue; which truck, where and when is randomised.

Telemetry faults (one truck each per day): soc_pct sent as a fraction (0.6 = 60%); malformed fields (null speed/soc, string offset_m, lowercase state); device clock ~+58 min; seq counter reset to 1 mid-run; whole telemetry message frozen (every field identical, only seq advances) for minutes; truck silent 24–55 s while link is up; weak pack ~5x drain that dies with BATTERY_DEPLETED (twice in the incline); HYD_PRESSURE_LOW fault ~+300 s. Also ~0.2% truncated lines, ~2% dups, ~6% reordered.

Link/blasts: drops of 21–45 s, twice landing inside a 120 s CLOSING notice; hello on reconnect carries zone state. Notice always 120 s; closures 66–111 s; ~every 5 min; CANCELLED seen; two zones CLOSING at once seen.

Commands (probe, operator_id "probe"): acks can be lost while the command executes; resending same command_id returns the original ACCEPTED; different payload → COMMAND_ID_REUSED. A RESUME was ACCEPTED and then ignored for 70 s (new id fixed it). EXIT_ZONE reverses at 3.0 m/s and stops 2 m outside. Deadman ~0.4 s, lease expiry 10 s → HOLDING. Drive echo age 200–620 ms. EXIT_ZONE on a frozen-telemetry truck was ACCEPTED, then RESUME got INVALID_STATE — real state unknowable.

**Why:** grounds PLAN.md and the blast/confidence design in observed behaviour, not the spec alone.
**How to apply:** treat this list as the minimum fault set for the fake gateway and tests; re-verify if the sim changes. See [[plan-md]].

content.text:
The probe ran all nine steps in about 5 minutes and cleanup finished. The raw log shows more than the probe's own printout did, partly because my S1 code miscounted acks for a resent id. Everything below comes from the raw capture.

## What the commands actually did

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| **S1 hold/resume** | **The `HOLD`'s ack was lost, but HT-01 stopped 3.2 s after the send anyway.** Resending the same `command_id` brought back `ACCEPTED` without running it twice, so recovering an outcome by replaying the id works. A different payload under the same id got `COMMAND_ID_REUSED`. A message arriving out of order briefly showed the truck `TRAMMING` again after it was `HOLDING`. |
| **S2 queued hold** | **Skipped.** DRAW_12 was under a blast for the first 3 minutes, so no truck was loading. We still don't know how commands queue behind loading. |
| **S3 `EXIT_ZONE`** | HT-05 was 145 m into DECLINE. **It reversed at 3.0 m/s, the full autonomous speed, back up the decline and stopped 2 m inside the bay.** That took 53 s. A reversing truck heads straight toward the trucks coming down behind it. |
| **S4 lease expiry** | Deadman engaged after 0.42 s. A `HOLD` sent while the lease was held came back `LEASE_HELD` with `holder: "probe"`. The lease `EXPIRED` after 10.1 s and the truck stayed `HOLDING`. |
| **S4, continued** | **The `RESUME` was `ACCEPTED`, and then HT-02 sat `HOLDING` for 70 s.** A second `RESUME` under a new id moved it within 1.3 s. This is Priya's complaint ("got the command, and then the truck just… doesn't"), seen live. Cleanup only noticed because it checked the truck's state. |
| **S5 drive** | At throttle 0.3 for 3 s, the truck moved 2.7 m. **Drive echoes came back 200–620 ms after sending**, so the worst case is longer than the 500 ms deadman. After `RELEASE_CONTROL` the truck went to `HOLDING`, as the spec says. |
| **S6 e-stop** | `ESTOPPED` within 0.3 s. A `HOLD` got `ESTOP_ACTIVE`. After `CLEAR_ESTOP` the truck was `HOLDING`. All as the spec says. |
| **S7 bad commands** | Every rejection matched §4.5. An unparseable line is acked with `vehicle_id: null`. |
| **S8 faulted truck** | `INTERLOCK_ACTIVE`, as expected. |
| **S9 frozen truck** | **HT-10's whole telemetry message was frozen.** Every field stayed identical for 5 minutes, including SoC at 42.52, and only `seq` counted up. **The gateway accepted `EXIT_ZONE`, but its later `RESUME` came back `INVALID_STATE`.** That means the real truck was neither holding nor idle, so it was doing something we couldn't see. We can't confirm a command took effect on a truck we can't observe. |

Two more findings from the probe session:
- **Two zones were `CLOSING` at the same time** (DRAW_12 and TIP) when the probe connected. Every earlier run had one blast at a time.
- **HT-10 may be left in an unknown state.** Its last command from us was rejected, so it may still be held near TIP. It doesn't matter much in the sim, which starts a fresh day after 30 idle minutes. I won't send it anything more unless you want me to.

## What changes for the plan

1. **`ACCEPTED` doesn't mean the command worked.** S4 showed it live: an accepted command was ignored. Every supervisory command has to be confirmed in telemetry within a deadline. If it isn't, retry under a new id, show the number of attempts, and alert if it still fails. This goes into the core of the command handling, not on the list of extras.
2. **Frozen telemetry repeats the whole message, so there's nothing to cross-check on that truck.** The battery check I suggested earlier can't catch this kind: the SoC freezes with everything else. The test is simpler: if seq keeps rising while every other field stays identical, the data is dead. Treat the truck as "position unknown, could be anywhere it could have reached", and never count it as clear.
3. **The probe confirmed reversing at 3.0 m/s.** So the time to clear a zone is the distance to the nearer edge divided by 3.0 (2.0 if loaded), plus up to 6 s for the command to act.
4. **Driving latency can exceed the deadman.** Echoes took up to 620 ms against a 500 ms deadman. The remote-driving view needs a visible measure of lag, which is Dave's "not knowing if it's lagging".
5. **More than one zone can close at once,** so the blast logic needs to handle several zones together.

## Where things are kept

The three captures, the probe log, `report.py` and `probe.py` are all in the session scratchpad. The scratchpad is deleted when this session ends. I've saved a short summary of these findings to my memory so the next session has them. The raw files would also make good test fixtures, and the brief wants the agent context kept in the repo. I'd suggest copying the scripts and a trimmed, email-free capture into something like `research/` in the repo. That needs your say-so, since the repo goes public.

I'm ready to propose the revised assumptions and write PLAN.md whenever you are.

"""Passive capture of the DLH gateway: authenticate, then record every line. Sends no commands.

Usage:
  set -a; . ./.env; set +a
  python3 research/capture.py OUT.jsonl SECONDS

Reads GATEWAY_HOST, GATEWAY_PORT and GATEWAY_EMAIL from the environment. The auth line is
never recorded, and the email is replaced with <email> in everything written. Reconnects
with backoff if the link drops. On a python.org macOS install with no CA bundle, also set
SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem.
"""
import json, os, socket, ssl, sys, time

host, port, email = os.environ['GATEWAY_HOST'], int(os.environ['GATEWAY_PORT']), os.environ['GATEWAY_EMAIL']
out = open(sys.argv[1], 'w'); duration = float(sys.argv[2])

def log(kind, **kw):
    kw.update(kind=kind, rx_ms=int(time.time() * 1000))
    out.write(json.dumps(kw).replace(email, '<email>') + '\n'); out.flush()

end = time.time() + duration; attempt = 0
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ.get('SSL_CERT_FILE'))
while time.time() < end:
    attempt += 1
    try:
        raw = socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=10)
        s = ctx.wrap_socket(raw, server_hostname=host); s.settimeout(5)
        log('connected', attempt=attempt)
        s.sendall((json.dumps({'type': 'auth', 'email': email}) + '\n').encode())
        buf = b''
        while time.time() < end:
            try: chunk = s.recv(65536)
            except socket.timeout: log('rx_timeout'); continue
            if not chunk: log('closed_by_peer'); break
            buf += chunk
            while b'\n' in buf:
                line, buf = buf.split(b'\n', 1)
                try: log('msg', m=json.loads(line))
                except Exception: log('unparseable', raw=line.decode('utf-8', 'replace')[:500])
        s.close()
    except Exception as e:
        log('error', err=repr(e))
    if time.time() < end: time.sleep(min(2 ** min(attempt, 4), 10))
log('done')

"""Cut the failure-case fixtures in research/fixtures/ out of full captures.

Usage:
  python3 research/trim.py RUN2.jsonl RUN3.jsonl PROBE.jsonl OUTDIR

The full captures are 9–25 MB each and are not committed. Each fixture keeps the capture's
record format (kind, rx_ms, m | raw) and starts with one {"kind": "fixture"} line saying what
it shows. Windows are in seconds from the start of the source capture. Auth lines are dropped,
hello.site.name is redacted, and the probe's own printouts ("note" records) are left out.
"""
import json, os, sys

run2, run3, probe, outdir = [[json.loads(l) for l in open(f)] for f in sys.argv[1:4]] + [sys.argv[4]]

def clean(r):
    r = json.loads(json.dumps(r))
    if r.get('kind') == 'msg' and r['m'].get('type') == 'hello' and 'site' in r['m']: r['m']['site'] = {'name': '<redacted>'}
    return r

def select(rows, a, b, keep):
    t0 = rows[0]['rx_ms']
    for r in rows:
        if a <= (r['rx_ms'] - t0) / 1000 <= b and r['kind'] != 'note' and not (r['kind'] == 'sent' and '"auth"' in r.get('raw', '')) and keep(r):
            yield clean(r)

def is_type(r, *types): return r['kind'] == 'msg' and r['m'].get('type') in types
def truck(r, *vs): return is_type(r, 'telemetry') and r['m'].get('vehicle_id') in vs
def about(r, v):  # commands we sent, and acks/lease events, for one truck
    if r['kind'] == 'sent': return '"%s"' % v in r['raw']
    return is_type(r, 'command_ack', 'lease_event', 'drive_rejected') and r['m'].get('vehicle_id') == v
def link(r): return r['kind'] in ('connected', 'closed_by_peer', 'error') or is_type(r, 'hello', 'zone_event', 'heartbeat')

def first_window(rows, v, state):
    t0 = rows[0]['rx_ms']
    xs = [(r['rx_ms'] - t0) / 1000 for r in rows if truck(r, v) and r['m'].get('state') == state]
    return (xs[0], xs[0] + 20) if xs else (0, 0)

ld = first_window(run3, 'HT-05', 'LOADING')
cases = [
    ('frozen-truck', 'run3', 'HT-10 freezes at about +160 s: every field stays identical while seq and t_device_ms keep '
     'advancing in step with real time; it reports TRAMMING at 2.0 m/s with an unchanged position. For contrast, '
     'HT-05 while LOADING: also identical bodies, but speed 0 in a stationary state.',
     [(run3, 140, 220, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-10')), (run3, ld[0], ld[1], lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-05'))]),
    ('seq-reset', 'run3', 'HT-01 seq drops from 887 to 1 at about +178 s while t_device_ms carries on.',
     [(run3, 168, 188, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-01'))]),
    ('silent-truck', 'run3', 'HT-03 sends nothing for 53 s from about +91 s while heartbeats show the link is up.',
     [(run3, 85, 150, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-03') or is_type(r, 'heartbeat'))]),
    ('truncated-lines', 'run3', 'Every unparseable line in a 15-minute run (87 of 48,597): JSON cut off mid-object, newline-terminated.',
     [(run3, 0, 10 ** 6, lambda r: r['kind'] == 'unparseable')]),
    ('fractional-soc', 'run3', 'HT-12 reports soc_pct as a fraction (0.82 meaning 82%) for the whole run.',
     [(run3, 0, 10, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-12'))]),
    ('accepted-then-ignored-resume', 'probe', 'HT-02: lease taken and left to expire, then RESUME is ACCEPTED (+233 s) '
     'but the truck stays HOLDING for 70 s; a second RESUME under a new command_id (+303 s) moves it within 1.3 s.',
     [(probe, 215, 306, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-02') or about(r, 'HT-02'))]),
    ('reverse-exit-zone', 'probe', 'HT-05, empty and 145 m into DECLINE: EXIT_ZONE reverses it at 3.0 m/s up the decline '
     'and holds it 2 m inside BAY, 53 s later. Includes every truck reporting BAY or DECLINE in the window, i.e. what '
     'it was reversing toward.',
     [(probe, 160, 222, lambda r: about(r, 'HT-05') or (is_type(r, 'telemetry') and r['m'].get('zone_id') in ('BAY', 'DECLINE')))]),
    ('two-zones-closing', 'probe', 'hello with DRAW_12 and TIP both CLOSING at once, and the zone events that follow.',
     [(probe, 0, 210, lambda r: is_type(r, 'hello', 'zone_event'))]),
    ('link-drop-in-notice', 'run2', 'DRAW_12 goes CLOSING; 1 s later the link drops for 45 s (logins accepted then closed); '
     'the hello on reconnect still shows DRAW_12 CLOSING with its effective time.',
     [(run2, 370, 420, link)]),
]

os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
for name, source, what, parts in cases:
    lines = [r for rows, a, b, keep in parts for r in select(rows, a, b, keep)]
    with open(os.path.join(outdir, name + '.jsonl'), 'w') as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({'kind': 'fixture', 'case': name, 'source': source, 'shows': what}) + '\n')
        for r in lines: f.write(json.dumps(r) + '\n')
    print('%-30s %5d records' % (name, len(lines)))

# research/

What the live gateway actually does, measured before any of the product was built. The
findings feed `CONTEXT.md` (assumptions) and `PLAN.md`; the fixtures are the seed for the
fake gateway's fault injection and the failure tests.

## How it was gathered

content.content:
40	**2. The protocol already encodes an autonomy policy: stopping is cheap,
41	starting is deliberate.** A truck can be stopped ten ways, four with no human
42	at all (deadman at 500 ms, lease idle expiry at 10 s, lease revocation, estop).
43	It can be started two ways, both a deliberate human act: `RESUME` — which is
44	*rejected* with `INVALID_STATE` unless the truck is already `HOLDING` or
45	`IDLE` — and fresh drive input after a deadman. §6.4 is decisive: when a lease
46	expires the vehicle holds and "does **not** return to autonomous operation by
47	itself." Match this. Our system stops trucks freely and never starts one by default 
48	without a person.
49	
50	**3. Reconnection is solvable, not lossy.** The gateway queues nothing for a
51	disconnected client, so an ack for an in-flight command is lost. But §5 says
52	resending the same `command_id` with the same payload returns the original
53	result without re-executing. So on reconnect, replay in-flight `command_id`s
54	and the gateway tells us what actually happened. Idempotent, no double
55	execution.
56	
57	**4. Automation precision is a function of data confidence.** When a position
58	is fresh, evacuate exactly the trucks in the zone — Lena: "don't stop trucks
59	that don't need stopping." When it is stale we cannot be precise, so get
60	**blunter**, not bolder: widen the set, hold more trucks, and tell the operator
61	we did and why. This inverts the usual instinct and the blast logic should be
62	built around it.
63	
64	## Who decides what
65	
66	| Decision | Owner |
67	|---|---|
68	| Blast evacuation, reconnect, dedupe, marking data stale | System, alone |
69	| Can this truck clear in time; is this pack weak | System computes, **human asserts** |
70	| Manual driving, forced takeover, clearing an estop, resuming autonomy | Human decides (including NLQ), system executes and records/logs |
71	| Is the zone clear | System **recommends**, with the reasons it could be wrong; human checks each and decides |
72	| Telling the shot firer | Human only — "I don't fire until **they** tell me it's clear" |
73	| Clearing a fault | Never — `PROTOCOL.md` §4.5: "a fault cannot be cleared from the control room" |
74	
75	
76	Ken's interlock stays human-to-human. The system's job is to make that
77	sentence safe to say in ten seconds: it recommends clear or not clear, and
78	shows the evidence that would make it wrong — stale positions, faulted
79	trucks, anything near a boundary. "Not clear" takes effect immediately and
80	needs no agreement. "Clear" requires the operator to acknowledge each doubt
81	before they can confirm it, and overriding a "not clear" to "clear"
82	requires a recorded reason. Both the recommendation and the decision go in
83	the log, so the disagreement between them is visible later.
84	
85	
86	Dave's two notes are one instruction, not a contradiction. "I don't want to be
87	babysitting" is a mandate to automate the routine. "Rather see nothing than
88	see something wrong" is a limit on **inference**, not on action. Act freely,
89	speak carefully.
90	
91	## Open questions (sent, awaiting reply)
92	
93	1. Telling the shot firer a truck cannot clear — operator phones Ken, or is
94	   there a channel to integrate with?
95	2. May the control room start trucks moving on its own after a cancelled
96	   blast, or does resumption need a human?
97	3. Who owns headway between trucks, given vehicles have no collision sensing
98	   and `EXIT_ZONE` may reverse?
99	4. Is "the system did it, under the blast-evacuation rule" an acceptable
100	   answer to Marta's inspector?
101	
102	Do not wait on these. Assumptions below; record what the answers change.
103	
104	## Assumptions
105	
106	1. **Safety lives in the service; the operators live in the UI.** A backend
107	   service holds the gateway connection, the fleet state, the command log and
108	   the blast rule, and runs whether or not anyone has a browser open. The
109	   browser UI is the operator's whole working surface — fleet picture,
110	   commands, the clearance check, remote driving — but it never holds the only
111	   copy of anything that matters. Safety cannot depend on someone having a tab
112	   open. ("nobody is watching the screen"; "unattended for 15 minutes")
113	
114	   Remote driving runs browser → service → gateway, which adds a hop to the
115	   500 ms deadman loop. The service relays only fresh operator input and
116	   never re-sends or synthesises drive messages for a browser that has gone
117	   quiet — otherwise a dropped browser would keep a truck moving and defeat
118	   the deadman. Silence means stop.
119	
120	2. **Resuming autonomy needs a human by default; stopping never does.**
121	   Elapsed time does not make restarting safer — a held truck is the
122	   lowest-hazard state there is, and an hour of stillness costs production,
123	   not safety. So a long hold escalates rather than acts: it ages visibly on
124	   the screen, re-alerts, and reaches the supervisor if nobody responds. Ken's
125	   "not sat there for an hour because nobody remembered" is answered by the
126	   system remembering, and by resumption being one click for every truck it
127	   held.
128	
129	   Holds are not all alike, and the system tracks who placed each one and
130	   why. An operator's hold is never auto-resumed — only they know why they
131	   stopped it. A hold the system placed for a blast, once the zone has
132	   reopened, positions are fresh and nothing else is holding the truck, is
133	   the one candidate for automatic resume. That behaviour is built but off
134	   by default, pending the answer to open question 2.
135	
136	   A hold can also become its own hazard — a weak pack held on the incline,
137	   or a stopped truck blocking the loop behind it. The system flags these
138	   rather than waiting them out.
139	
140	3. **Never compute age from `t_device_ms`.** Vehicle clocks are explicitly not
141	   disciplined. Order by `seq`, age against `server_time_ms`, treat the device
142	   clock as an opaque echo — and surface per-truck skew as a data-quality
143	   signal.
144	4. **On reconnect, replay in-flight `command_id`s** to recover their outcome.
145	5. **A faulted truck in a closing zone cannot be evacuated by us.**
146	   `INTERLOCK_ACTIVE` blocks `EXIT_ZONE`; limp-home at 1.0 m/s or nothing, and
147	   `BATTERY_DEPLETED` needs a tow. Escalate loudly; never report the zone clear.
148	6. **Re-check zone membership immediately before auto-issuing `EXIT_ZONE`.**
149	   The 1–6 s execution delay means a race survives anyway; prefer a spurious
150	   hold over a missed evacuation.
151	7. **The CLOSED rule is unconditional** — it covers estopped, faulted and dead
152	   trucks. Not clear means not clear.
153	8. **A blocked command surfaces to the lease holder,** not only to whoever
154	   tried. This is Priya's near miss exactly.
155	9. **Forced takeover is a supervisor-role action.** Auth is ours to design; a
156	   hard-coded user list is acceptable per the brief.
157	10. **Block manual driving *into* a closed zone; never block driving *out*.**
158	    Limp-home may be the only way out.
159	11. **Alarm threshold: interrupt only for action needed inside the next
160	    minute.** Everything else is visible but silent, and the rule that
161	    silenced something is inspectable. Dave turned the old system's sound off
162	    in month one; that is the bar.
163	12. **Stale position widens the evacuation set** rather than narrowing it.
164	13. **SoC: show the pack's own number, plus a derived confidence** from
165	    actual-versus-expected consumption per lap if time allows. Never replace
166	    the vendor's number with ours.
167	14. **The model proposes, never acts.** Natural-language queries and command
168	    proposals are allowed; every command still needs operator confirmation
169	    and passes the same deterministic checks as the UI.
170	
171	
172	## Reuse from an earlier project of mine (`drone-hal`)
173	
174	Same author, same patterns, different domain. Carries over:
175	
176	- **Two-clock observations** — every value holds when the device sampled it and
177	  when we received it, with per-field freshness scaled to the declared rate.
178	- **A command registry as the single authority on lifecycle,** with illegal
179	  transitions logged and discarded rather than applied.
180	- **The safety check sits below the command path,** so commands the system
181	  issues to itself are checked by the same code as an operator's.
182	- **Refusals carry a reason in the operator's language,** and the distinct
183	  kinds stay distinct rather than collapsing into "rejected".
184	- **A conformance observer** that speaks the protocol and asserts the other
185	  side behaves — the brief invites this: "the simulator is ours, and its
186	  internals are part of what's being tested."
187	- **Propose-then-confirm NLQ** — the model resolves intent; state, checks and dispatch stay deterministic.
188	Does **not** carry over: lat/lon geometry (this is 1-D along a loop, with
189	wrap), and anything about aircraft.
190	
191	## Deployment target
192	
193	Oracle Cloud ARM box, already provisioned and in use(called drone-hal); unless an a1 box called control-room is provisioned -- currently being attempted via cron job:
194	
195	- 1 OCPU, 5.5 GiB RAM, 30 GB disk (~18 GB free), Oracle Linux 9, aarch64
196	- Node 22.23.2, git, rsync, Chromium dependencies installed
197	- Caddy on 80/443 with a TLS cert via sslip.io; firewalld allows http/https
198	- **Port 8080 is taken** by an existing project — pick another and add a Caddy
199	  route

sentence safe to say in ten seconds: it recommends clear or not clear, and
shows the evidence that would make it wrong — stale positions, faulted
trucks, anything near a boundary. "Not clear" takes effect immediately and
needs no agreement. "Clear" requires the operator to acknowledge each doubt
before they can confirm it, and overriding a "not clear" to "clear"
requires a recorded reason. Both the recommendation and the decision go in
the log, so the disagreement between them is visible later.


Dave's two notes are one instruction, not a contradiction. "I don't want to be
babysitting" is a mandate to automate the routine. "Rather see nothing than
see something wrong" is a limit on **inference**, not on action. Act freely,
speak carefully.

## Open questions (sent, awaiting reply)

1. Telling the shot firer a truck cannot clear — operator phones Ken, or is
   there a channel to integrate with?
2. May the control room start trucks moving on its own after a cancelled
   blast, or does resumption need a human?
3. Who owns headway between trucks, given vehicles have no collision sensing
   and `EXIT_ZONE` may reverse?
4. Is "the system did it, under the blast-evacuation rule" an acceptable
   answer to Marta's inspector?

Do not wait on these. Assumptions below; record what the answers change.

## Assumptions

1. **Safety lives in the service; the operators live in the UI.** A backend
   service holds the gateway connection, the fleet state, the command log and
   the blast rule, and runs whether or not anyone has a browser open. The
   browser UI is the operator's whole working surface — fleet picture,
   commands, the clearance check, remote driving — but it never holds the only
   copy of anything that matters. Safety cannot depend on someone having a tab
   open. ("nobody is watching the screen"; "unattended for 15 minutes")

   500 ms deadman loop. The service relays only fresh operator input and
   never re-sends or synthesises drive messages for a browser that has gone
   quiet — otherwise a dropped browser would keep a truck moving and defeat
   the deadman. Silence means stop.

2. **Resuming autonomy needs a human by default; stopping never does.**
   Elapsed time does not make restarting safer — a held truck is the
   lowest-hazard state there is, and an hour of stillness costs production,
   not safety. So a long hold escalates rather than acts: it ages visibly on
   the screen, re-alerts, and reaches the supervisor if nobody responds. Ken's
   "not sat there for an hour because nobody remembered" is answered by the
   system remembering, and by resumption being one click for every truck it
   held.

   why. An operator's hold is never auto-resumed — only they know why they
   stopped it. A hold the system placed for a blast, once the zone has
   reopened, positions are fresh and nothing else is holding the truck, is
   the one candidate for automatic resume. That behaviour is built but off
   by default, pending the answer to open question 2.

   or a stopped truck blocking the loop behind it. The system flags these
   rather than waiting them out.

3. **Never compute age from `t_device_ms`.** Vehicle clocks are explicitly not
   disciplined. Order by `seq`, age against `server_time_ms`, treat the device
   clock as an opaque echo — and surface per-truck skew as a data-quality
   signal.
4. **On reconnect, replay in-flight `command_id`s** to recover their outcome.
5. **A faulted truck in a closing zone cannot be evacuated by us.**
   `INTERLOCK_ACTIVE` blocks `EXIT_ZONE`; limp-home at 1.0 m/s or nothing, and
   `BATTERY_DEPLETED` needs a tow. Escalate loudly; never report the zone clear.
6. **Re-check zone membership immediately before auto-issuing `EXIT_ZONE`.**
   The 1–6 s execution delay means a race survives anyway; prefer a spurious
   hold over a missed evacuation.
7. **The CLOSED rule is unconditional** — it covers estopped, faulted and dead
   trucks. Not clear means not clear.
8. **A blocked command surfaces to the lease holder,** not only to whoever
   tried. This is Priya's near miss exactly.
9. **Forced takeover is a supervisor-role action.** Auth is ours to design; a
   hard-coded user list is acceptable per the brief.
10. **Block manual driving *into* a closed zone; never block driving *out*.**
    Limp-home may be the only way out.
11. **Alarm threshold: interrupt only for action needed inside the next
    minute.** Everything else is visible but silent, and the rule that
    silenced something is inspectable. Dave turned the old system's sound off
    in month one; that is the bar.
12. **Stale position widens the evacuation set** rather than narrowing it.
13. **SoC: show the pack's own number, plus a derived confidence** from
    actual-versus-expected consumption per lap if time allows. Never replace
    the vendor's number with ours.
14. **The model proposes, never acts.** Natural-language queries and command
    proposals are allowed; every command still needs operator confirmation
    and passes the same deterministic checks as the UI.

Same author, same patterns, different domain. Carries over:

wrap), and anything about aircraft.

15. **Every supervisory command is confirmed in telemetry, against a
    deadline.** If the effect does not appear, retry under a **new**
    `command_id`, show the attempt count, and alert if it still fails.
    Retrying is safe because `HOLD`, `RESUME`, `RETURN_TO_BAY` and
    `EXIT_ZONE` do nothing extra when repeated: a second `HOLD` on a held
    truck is still a hold. The exception is **queuing**: behind `LOADING`
    (~20 s), `DUMPING` (~12 s) or `CHARGING` (unbounded) the deadline has to
    depend on state, and a newer queued command replaces the older one — so
    a retry must never displace a different command we queued. Queue
    behaviour is **unverified** (the probe's S2 never ran); test it in the
    fake gateway.
16. **Evacuation is coordinated, not per-truck.** `EXIT_ZONE` reverses at
    full speed toward the trucks behind, and nothing on the trucks prevents
    a collision. Hold the trucks upstream first, then reverse the one below
    them; and hold trucks *before* they enter a closing zone — DECLINE takes
    ~167 s to cross against 120 s of notice, so a truck entering late cannot
    get through.
17. **The blast budget survives a link drop.** A drop can eat 45 s of the
    120 s notice. On reconnect, act on the `hello` snapshot at once; plan
    against the time left, not the time given. Several zones can close at
    once.
18. **Remote driving shows its lag; the deadman risk is smaller than the
    round trip suggests.** Echo age was 200–620 ms, but that is a round trip
    plus up to 200 ms of telemetry sampling. At 10 Hz, send gaps were
    100–106 ms and the deadman never tripped in the probe. The driving view
    shows input age and deadman state; a link drop still stops the truck,
    by design.
