Two things: the site has answered my four questions we previosuly sent, and I've reviewed TESTING.md. Do the answers first — they change some of the review.

## The answers

1. The operator and Ken talk directly, by radio. Ken calls about two minutes before firing, around when the system notice arrives, and doesn't fire until the operator says it's clear. If the operator isn't sure, they ask him to hold the shot — costly, but always right when in doubt. The gateway can't reach the blasting crew. Clearing people isn't our problem; clearing trucks is.
2. The system may restart trucks on its own once a zone reopens, whether the blast happened or was called off. No sign-off needed. The site wants trucks back at work without operators chasing each one.
3. Spacing is out of scope. Assume it's handled elsewhere; don't build for it. The simulator doesn't model trucks interacting — they never block or hit each other, even reversing.
4. The system acting on its own is expected, especially for blasts, since nights are one operator. Its actions go in the same log as the operators', showing what it did, when and why. That's a good answer for the inspector.

What that changes:

- Auto-resume is now MVP and on by default. When a zone reopens (CLEARED or CANCELLED), the system resumes the trucks IT held for that blast — never a truck an operator held, never one with a lease or a fault, and never into another zone that's closing or closed. The resume goes through command confirmation like any other command, and is logged as the system, with the rule and inputs.
- Coordinated evacuation is gone: drop upstream holds before reversing (assumption 16, L2.8, L3.7, and that half of PLAN's MVP item 3). With spacing out of scope they'd only be unnecessary stops. Hold-before-entry stays — that's about the zone, not spacing.
- A can't-clear alarm names the action: "radio the shot firer to hold the shot", with the truck, the zone and the reason.
- System and operator actions share one log, with what, when and why.

Don't edit PLAN.md's body. Record the four answers and what they changed in CONTEXT.md now (mark the questions answered; 5 and 6 stay open), and they'll go into PLAN's "What changed" section at the end. CLAUDE.md's "starting always does" needs to change to match answer 2.

## The TESTING.md review

Very well done! — the belief/truth split, the IDs and the task table are exactly right. Your four choices are fine, but the open thresholds need numbers early in the ingest task: L4.R1's 10 s rule means nothing until they're set. Two gaps I see:

1. A system that does nothing passes the blast suite. L4 rules on alarming (R1), on wrongly saying clear (R2a–c), and over-holding (M1). Nothing requires trucks to get out. A system that never moves a truck and alarms about every one passes R1, never says clear, and scores a perfect M1. CLAUDE.md invariant 5 reads as a permission ("may be inside only if an alarm went up"). Add L4.R0, against the truth: every truck that could have been cleared or held before entry is outside the zone when it closes — "could" meaning the data allowed it in time, the time to clear plus command delay fits in the time left, and it wasn't interlocked. The alarm is for the trucks that couldn't. Reword invariant 5 so the alarm never replaces evacuation.

2. Nothing says the site might be different. We'll be run against a site we haven't seen, but nowhere do the docs say to take the route, loop length, vehicle list and notice length from hello. Every number we have is from one site, and an agent will hardcode them. Add a CLAUDE.md invariant: nothing site-specific is a constant. Then a test where the fake gateway serves a different site — different route, truck count, shorter notice — and the whole L4 suite still passes.

Smaller:

- Auto-resume (from answer 2): every truck the system held for a zone is resumed within a bound after it reopens, unless still blocked; an operator's hold is never resumed; nothing is resumed into a closing or closed zone. Plus a metric: time trucks sat after a reopen.
- Operator commands that route through a closing zone: RETURN_TO_BAY takes "the shorter direction", which can pass through one; an operator RESUME of a truck held for a blast; and EXIT_ZONE picks the nearest boundary itself, which can land a truck in an adjacent zone that's also closing. The safety check sits below operator commands too — test all three.
- The three MVP items with no cases: alerting (which events interrupt, which are silent, the silencing rule visible); battery warnings (drain against the fleet, can it reach the bay); and hand-back after driving — release leaves the truck HOLDING, so the UI has to make the RESUME step obvious. The brief names hand-back explicitly.
- E-stop pressed while the site link is down: shown as not delivered, never as done.
- L0.C3 checks the fake against duplicates ~2 %, reordering ~6 %, loss ~3 %, closures 66–111 s and drops 20–45 s, "within the ranges in research/README.md" — but those aren't in research/README.md. Measure them from the captures and record them there.
- A weak-pack fixture: it died in the incline in two of three runs. If the full captures still exist, cut one with trim.py.
- A false-alarm metric beside M1: can't-clear alarms for trucks that then cleared. Crying wolf is how the old system got muted.
- Every route and the websocket refuse an unauthenticated user.
- In-flight commands persisted before sending — L6.1's replay depends on it.
- BAY closing (open question 5): EXIT_ZONE is refused there, so driving is the only way out.
- README "Around the corner": note that on a real site, spacing would have to be owned somewhere — we were told not to build it here.

Commits, adding paths explicitly:
1. CONTEXT.md — the answers and what they changed.
2. CLAUDE.md and TESTING.md together — the starting rule, the reworded invariant 5, the site-independence invariant, R0 and the new cases are one change.
3. research/README.md with the measured statistics, plus the weak-pack fixture if you can cut it.

# CLAUDE.md

Control-room software for Deep Level Haulage's autonomous haul trucks. Read before any task.

## Read first

1. `dlh-candidate-package/BRIEF.md`, then `OPERATOR_NOTES.md`, then `PROTOCOL.md`, in that order.
2. `CONTEXT.md`: findings, open questions and the numbered assumptions. Treat them as decisions.
3. `PLAN.md` (frozen: never edit it, except its final "What changed" section, and only when asked).
4. `research/README.md`: what the live gateway actually does, verified against assumed.
5. `TESTING.md`: the cases your task must pass.

## Invariants

These are not negotiable. If a task seems to need one broken, stop and ask.

1. **Time is injected.** No component reads the wall clock directly. Everything takes a clock,
   so blast scenarios run in milliseconds in tests.
2. **`operator_id` comes from the server-side session,** never from the browser's payload.
3. **Drive input is relayed only while fresh,** and never re-sent or synthesised by the service.
   Silence means stop: a browser that goes quiet must let the deadman stop the truck.
4. **No model on the control path.** Nothing an LLM produces sends a command.
5. **Blast safety: never silent.** A truck may be inside a `CLOSED` zone only if a can't-clear
   alarm, with its reason, went up within 10 s of `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing that
   conclusion, whichever is later (`TESTING.md` L4).
6. **Blast safety: never wrongly clear.** The system never recommends "clear" while any truck
   might be inside. "Might" includes old, silent and contradicted data.

The rest of `CONTEXT.md`'s assumptions bind too. The ones most often forgotten: `ACCEPTED` is
not done, so confirm the effect in telemetry. Order by `seq` within a controller run and age
against `server_time_ms`, never the device clock. Stopping needs no person; starting always does.

## How to work

- Tests first, from the cases in `TESTING.md`. Replay `research/fixtures/` rather than inventing data.
- Done means the tests pass **and** every claim in your summary was checked against raw data:
  logs, captures, the database. Never check a claim only against your own printout.
  (`AI_LOG.md` entry 1 is why.)
- If the simulator seems to behave wrongly, write it down. Never work around it silently.
- Keep it small. A focused system that is right beats a broad one.

## Repository hygiene

- **Never `git add .` or `git add -A`.** Add paths explicitly. The repo is on exFAT, where macOS
  writes a `._` file beside every file, and the repo goes public.
- **Never print `.env`** or echo `GATEWAY_EMAIL`, a key or a password into output, logs, commits
  or fixtures. Credentials come from the environment only; `.env.example` lists them.
- Commit as you go, one logical change per commit. The history is read.

54:resending the same `command_id` with the same payload returns the original

content.content:
## Invariants

These are not negotiable. If a task seems to need one broken, stop and ask.

1. **Time is injected.** No component reads the wall clock directly. Everything takes a clock,
   so blast scenarios run in milliseconds in tests.
2. **`operator_id` comes from the server-side session,** never from the browser's payload.
3. **Drive input is relayed only while fresh,** and never re-sent or synthesised by the service.
   Silence means stop: a browser that goes quiet must let the deadman stop the truck.
4. **No model on the control path.** Nothing an LLM produces sends a command.
5. **Blast safety: get every truck out that can be got out; alarm for the rest.** Every truck
   that can be cleared from a closing zone, or held before entering it, in the time left is
   outside when it closes. For a truck that can't, a can't-clear alarm ("radio the shot firer
   to hold the shot", with the truck, the zone and the reason) goes up within 10 s of
   `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing that conclusion, whichever is later. The alarm
   never replaces evacuation (`TESTING.md` L4).
6. **Blast safety: never wrongly clear.** The system never recommends "clear" while any truck
   might be inside. "Might" includes old, silent and contradicted data.
7. **Nothing site-specific is a constant.** We will be run against a site we haven't seen.
   Route, segments, zones, loop length and vehicle list come from `hello`; notice length comes
   from each `zone_event`'s `effective_at_ms`. Speeds and delays are parameters with their source
   noted (spec or measured), never literals scattered through the code.

The rest of `CONTEXT.md`'s assumptions bind too. The ones most often forgotten: `ACCEPTED` is
not done, so confirm the effect in telemetry. Order by `seq` within a controller run and age
against `server_time_ms`, never the device clock. Stopping needs no person. The system restarts
only trucks it held for a blast, once that zone reopens; every other hold waits for a person. The
safety check sits below every command path, operators' included.

## How to work

"""Cut the failure-case fixtures in research/fixtures/ out of full captures.

Usage:
  python3 research/trim.py RUN2.jsonl RUN3.jsonl PROBE.jsonl OUTDIR

The full captures are 9–25 MB each and are not committed. Each fixture keeps the capture's
record format (kind, rx_ms, m | raw) and starts with one {"kind": "fixture"} line saying what
it shows. Windows are in seconds from the start of the source capture. Auth lines are dropped,
hello.site.name is redacted, and the probe's own printouts ("note" records) are left out.
"""
import json, os, sys

run2, run3, probe, outdir = [[json.loads(l) for l in open(f)] for f in sys.argv[1:4]] + [sys.argv[4]]

def clean(r):
    r = json.loads(json.dumps(r))
    if r.get('kind') == 'msg' and r['m'].get('type') == 'hello' and 'site' in r['m']: r['m']['site'] = {'name': '<redacted>'}
    return r

def select(rows, a, b, keep):
    t0 = rows[0]['rx_ms']
    for r in rows:
        if a <= (r['rx_ms'] - t0) / 1000 <= b and r['kind'] != 'note' and not (r['kind'] == 'sent' and '"auth"' in r.get('raw', '')) and keep(r):
            yield clean(r)

def is_type(r, *types): return r['kind'] == 'msg' and r['m'].get('type') in types
def truck(r, *vs): return is_type(r, 'telemetry') and r['m'].get('vehicle_id') in vs
def about(r, v):  # commands we sent, and acks/lease events, for one truck
    if r['kind'] == 'sent': return '"%s"' % v in r['raw']
    return is_type(r, 'command_ack', 'lease_event', 'drive_rejected') and r['m'].get('vehicle_id') == v
def link(r): return r['kind'] in ('connected', 'closed_by_peer', 'error') or is_type(r, 'hello', 'zone_event', 'heartbeat')

def first_window(rows, v, state):
    t0 = rows[0]['rx_ms']
    xs = [(r['rx_ms'] - t0) / 1000 for r in rows if truck(r, v) and r['m'].get('state') == state]
    return (xs[0], xs[0] + 20) if xs else (0, 0)

ld = first_window(run3, 'HT-05', 'LOADING')
cases = [
    ('frozen-truck', 'run3', 'HT-10 freezes at about +160 s: every field stays identical while seq and t_device_ms keep '
     'advancing in step with real time; it reports TRAMMING at 2.0 m/s with an unchanged position. For contrast, '
     'HT-05 while LOADING: also identical bodies, but speed 0 in a stationary state.',
     [(run3, 140, 220, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-10')), (run3, ld[0], ld[1], lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-05'))]),
    ('seq-reset', 'run3', 'HT-01 seq drops from 887 to 1 at about +178 s while t_device_ms carries on.',
     [(run3, 168, 188, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-01'))]),
    ('silent-truck', 'run3', 'HT-03 sends nothing for 53 s from about +91 s while heartbeats show the link is up.',
     [(run3, 85, 150, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-03') or is_type(r, 'heartbeat'))]),
    ('truncated-lines', 'run3', 'Every unparseable line in a 15-minute run (87 of 48,597): JSON cut off mid-object, newline-terminated.',
     [(run3, 0, 10 ** 6, lambda r: r['kind'] == 'unparseable')]),
    ('fractional-soc', 'run3', 'HT-12 reports soc_pct as a fraction (0.82 meaning 82%) for the whole run.',
     [(run3, 0, 10, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-12'))]),
    ('accepted-then-ignored-resume', 'probe', 'HT-02: lease taken and left to expire, then RESUME is ACCEPTED (+233 s) '
     'but the truck stays HOLDING for 70 s; a second RESUME under a new command_id (+303 s) moves it within 1.3 s.',
     [(probe, 215, 306, lambda r: truck(r, 'HT-02') or about(r, 'HT-02'))]),
    ('reverse-exit-zone', 'probe', 'HT-05, empty and 145 m into DECLINE: EXIT_ZONE reverses it at 3.0 m/s up the decline '
     'and holds it 2 m inside BAY, 53 s later. Includes every truck reporting BAY or DECLINE in the window, i.e. what '
     'it was reversing toward.',
     [(probe, 160, 222, lambda r: about(r, 'HT-05') or (is_type(r, 'telemetry') and r['m'].get('zone_id') in ('BAY', 'DECLINE')))]),
    ('two-zones-closing', 'probe', 'hello with DRAW_12 and TIP both CLOSING at once, and the zone events that follow.',
     [(probe, 0, 210, lambda r: is_type(r, 'hello', 'zone_event'))]),
    ('link-drop-in-notice', 'run2', 'DRAW_12 goes CLOSING; 1 s later the link drops for 45 s (logins accepted then closed); '
     'the hello on reconnect still shows DRAW_12 CLOSING with its effective time.',
     [(run2, 370, 420, link)]),
]

os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
for name, source, what, parts in cases:
    lines = [r for rows, a, b, keep in parts for r in select(rows, a, b, keep)]
    with open(os.path.join(outdir, name + '.jsonl'), 'w') as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({'kind': 'fixture', 'case': name, 'source': source, 'shows': what}) + '\n')
        for r in lines: f.write(json.dumps(r) + '\n')

All three commits are in, in your order, with every path added explicitly. Nothing is pushed, and I've stopped before any code.

```
9661737 Add measured radio and blast statistics and a weak-pack fixture
3007adb Require evacuation, site independence and the answers in the test spec
e80359b Record the site's answers to questions 1-4 in CONTEXT.md
```

**What changed in each:**
- **CONTEXT.md:**
  - Questions 1–4 are marked answered, with a "What the answers changed" list; 5 and 6 stay open.
  - Assumption 2 now has auto-resume on by default for the system's own blast holds.
  - Assumption 16 is hold-before-entry only.
  - The decision table has a row for resuming the system's own blast holds.
  - The can't-clear alarm wording is recorded.
  - The spacing note for README "Around the corner" is recorded.
- **CLAUDE.md:**
  - Invariant 5 now requires getting trucks out, with the alarm only for those that can't.
  - New invariant 7: nothing site-specific is a constant.
  - The restart rule now matches answer 2.
- **TESTING.md** covers everything in your review:
  - L4.R0, against the truth: trucks that could be got out are out.
  - The auto-resume rules R3–R5, plus metrics for time sat after a reopen (M2) and false alarms (M3).
  - L4.S: the whole blast suite run against a different site, plus a build check for hard-coded site literals (L1.3).
  - The safety check under operator commands (L2.50–L2.54, including BAY closing).
  - Alerting, battery, hand-back, e-stop while the link is down, refusal of unauthenticated users, and commands written to the log before sending.
  - Upstream holds removed.
- **Thresholds now have numbers, checked against all three captures:**
  - "old" after 2 s: the longest normal gap was 1.67 s.
  - "silent" after 5 s: flags only the known silent trucks.
  - "frozen" after 3 s of reported motion with no change in position: flags exactly one truck per run.
  - "link down" after 5 s without a heartbeat.
- **research/README.md** has the measured statistics, and the new `weak-pack` fixture is in.

**One correction to my own numbers:** reordering is about 5%, not the ~6% I'd been quoting. My `report.py` counted reordering loosely. research/README.md says so.

**Choices of mine to check:**
- **Auto-resume within 15 s of a reopen** (L4.R3). That's the 6 s command delay plus one retry, with margin.
- **An e-stop pressed while the link is down is sent as soon as the link returns** (L7.8), on the grounds that stopping is always safe. You may prefer the operator to confirm it again first.
- **The supervisor escalation time in L2.63 has no number yet.**
- **For PLAN's "What changed":** PLAN says "the nine research/fixtures/", and there are now ten.

## Which task I'd start with

**First, a small foundation: injectable time, protocol types, and a site model built from `hello`.** It's a day's work at most, but every later task needs it, and both are hard to retrofit (L1, invariants 1 and 7). It's small enough that I'd write it with an agent in this session and review it in full.

**Then two tasks in parallel, in separate worktrees:**
- **The fake gateway (task 1)**, as its own agent task. It's the oracle for L4, which is where the riskiest part (blast safety) gets tested. Every blast test waits on it. And its conformance check (L0.C2: run `research/probe.py` against it and match the live acks) is the earliest proof that our model of the site matches the real one. I'd keep its first milestone narrow: geometry, duty cycle, commands and leases, enough to pass L0.C2 and L0.C4 (same seed, same stream). Fault injectors come next, starting with the three combinations we saw live.
- **Ingest and fleet state (task 2).** Its tests replay the real fixtures, not the fake, so it doesn't wait. It also owns the thresholds that L4.R1 depends on.

**While those run, I'd write the blast engine's rules spec myself.** That task needs the closest review, and it shouldn't start until the fake gateway passes conformance.

**The live re-probe of queuing waits until you approve it,** since it sends real commands.

content.text:
Agree: start with the foundation as laid out, then the fake gateway and ingest in parallel.

Your choices:
- Auto-resume within 15 s: yes.
- E-stop while the link is down: not automatic on reconnect. Stopping is safe in isolation, not in context — a stale e-stop revokes leases, so it could strand an operator limp-homing a faulted truck out of a closing zone. Keep it pending and visible with a cancel. Send it automatically only if the link returns within 10 s; after that, show the truck's current state and ask the operator to confirm again.
- Escalation: re-alert at 15 minutes, supervisor at 30. But on nights the operator is alone and is the supervisor, so escalation there means more persistent alerting to that same person, not handing it on.
- Note "ten fixtures, not nine" for PLAN's What changed.

The UI. Building it at step 6 is fine; designing it that late isn't. Operator experience is one of the five graded criteria, a novice will drive a truck through it, and the decision log needs an operator-experience decision. So alongside the foundation, write UI.md — the design spec the UI task will build from — and plan to prototype it against replayed fixtures, so it's designed around frozen, silent and stale trucks from the start. Direction:

- A track diagram, not a map: the loop drawn like a metro line from hello's route, zones as bands showing OPEN, a CLOSING countdown or CLOSED, trucks as chips on the line.
- Position as a range when we're unsure: a frozen or silent truck drawn as a bar over everywhere it could have reached, not a dot.
- A zone clearance panel: for each closing zone, CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE, with the doubts listed and, when not clear, "Radio the shot firer to hold the shot." Priya's 10-second question should take 2.
- A fleet table sorted by attention: state, zone, SoC as the pack's number with a confidence flag, control mode with who holds the lease, the data state in words as well as colour, and the last command's outcome with its attempt count.
- Command outcomes as a timeline: sent, acknowledged, effect seen — or "retry 2 of 3", or failed with the reason in plain words.
- An attention tray: interrupts at the top, silent items below, each with the rule that silenced it; acknowledgements attributed.
- A driving view: lag meter (input age, echo age), deadman state, speed, distance to the next zone boundary and its status, and hand-back as an obvious two-step — Release, then Resume.
- E-stop in a fixed place on every view, distinct in shape as well as colour, with a visible "pending, not delivered" state.
- Two link indicators — site and service. When either drops, the picture visibly ages instead of freezing.
- Who else is on: operators logged in, and who holds which lease.
- Built for a 12-hour shift: dark, low glare, large type, calm by default — nothing moves or flashes unless it needs action. Sound only for interrupts, distinct tones, never continuous. Colour never carries meaning alone.
- An audit view that answers "who moved HT-06 at 3:12" directly.

# CLAUDE.md

Control-room software for Deep Level Haulage's autonomous haul trucks. Read before any task.

## Read first

1. `dlh-candidate-package/BRIEF.md`, then `OPERATOR_NOTES.md`, then `PROTOCOL.md`, in that order.
2. `CONTEXT.md`: findings, open questions and the numbered assumptions. Treat them as decisions.
3. `PLAN.md` (frozen: never edit it, except its final "What changed" section, and only when asked).
4. `research/README.md`: what the live gateway actually does, verified against assumed.
5. `TESTING.md`: the cases your task must pass.

## Invariants

These are not negotiable. If a task seems to need one broken, stop and ask.

1. **Time is injected.** No component reads the wall clock directly. Everything takes a clock,
   so blast scenarios run in milliseconds in tests.
2. **`operator_id` comes from the server-side session,** never from the browser's payload.
3. **Drive input is relayed only while fresh,** and never re-sent or synthesised by the service.
   Silence means stop: a browser that goes quiet must let the deadman stop the truck.
4. **No model on the control path.** Nothing an LLM produces sends a command.
5. **Blast safety: get every truck out that can be got out; alarm for the rest.** Every truck
   that can be cleared from a closing zone, or held before entering it, in the time left is
   outside when it closes. For a truck that can't, a can't-clear alarm ("radio the shot firer
   to hold the shot", with the truck, the zone and the reason) goes up within 10 s of
   `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing that conclusion, whichever is later. The alarm
   never replaces evacuation (`TESTING.md` L4).
6. **Blast safety: never wrongly clear.** The system never recommends "clear" while any truck
   might be inside. "Might" includes old, silent and contradicted data.
7. **Nothing site-specific is a constant.** We will be run against a site we haven't seen.
   Route, segments, zones, loop length and vehicle list come from `hello`; notice length comes
   from each `zone_event`'s `effective_at_ms`. Speeds and delays are parameters with their source
   noted (spec or measured), never literals scattered through the code.

The rest of `CONTEXT.md`'s assumptions bind too. The ones most often forgotten: `ACCEPTED` is
not done, so confirm the effect in telemetry. Order by `seq` within a controller run and age
against `server_time_ms`, never the device clock. Stopping needs no person. The system restarts
only trucks it held for a blast, once that zone reopens; every other hold waits for a person. The
safety check sits below every command path, operators' included.

## How to work

- Tests first, from the cases in `TESTING.md`. Replay `research/fixtures/` rather than inventing data.
- Done means the tests pass **and** every claim in your summary was checked against raw data:
  logs, captures, the database. Never check a claim only against your own printout.
  (`AI_LOG.md` entry 1 is why.)
- If the simulator seems to behave wrongly, write it down. Never work around it silently.
- Keep it small. A focused system that is right beats a broad one.

## Repository hygiene

- **Never `git add .` or `git add -A`.** Add paths explicitly. The repo is on exFAT, where macOS
  writes a `._` file beside every file, and the repo goes public.
- **Never print `.env`** or echo `GATEWAY_EMAIL`, a key or a password into output, logs, commits
  or fixtures. Credentials come from the environment only; `.env.example` lists them.
- Commit as you go, one logical change per commit. The history is read.

input.content:
# UI

The design spec the UI task builds from. The operators are in `OPERATOR_NOTES.md`; the cases these
screens must pass are in `TESTING.md` (L2.60–L2.64, L7, L9). It is prototyped against the replayed
`research/fixtures/` before it is wired to the live service, so it is designed around frozen, silent and
old trucks from the start, not retrofitted for them.

## Principles

1. **Answer the question before showing the data.** Priya's "is L4 South clear?" takes 2 seconds: a
   word, not a count of dots.
2. **Never show a guess as a fact.** A truck we're unsure of is drawn as a range over everywhere it
   could be, and labelled in words. When the data stops, the picture ages visibly; it never freezes
   looking current.
3. **Calm until it matters.** Built for a 12-hour shift, on one of four screens: dark, low glare,
   large type. Trucks move smoothly along the line; nothing else animates, pulses or flashes. Sound
   only for interrupts (assumption 11): distinct short tones, never continuous.
4. **Colour never carries meaning alone.** Every state also has a word, a shape or a pattern.
5. **Show what actually happened.** A command is "sent", "acknowledged" and "done" as three separate
   things, and a failure says why in plain words.
6. **One obvious next step.** Every alarm names its action; every held truck shows how to resume it.

## Always on screen

- **E-stop**, in a fixed place on every view: a distinct shape (octagon), not just red. One press per
  truck. Pressed while the site link is down, it shows **pending, not delivered**, with a cancel; it is
  sent automatically only if the link returns within 10 s, and otherwise asks again with the truck's
  current state (L7.8). It shows "done" only when telemetry confirms `ESTOPPED`.
- **Two link indicators: site and service.** Each shows its own age. If either drops, the whole picture
  greys and every age counter keeps counting (L9.2, L9.3).
- **Who else is on:** operators logged in, their roles, and who holds which truck's lease.
- **Sound armed.** Browsers block sound until the page is clicked. After login the operator clicks once
  to arm it; until then "Sound off" shows in a fixed place, because an interrupt nobody hears isn't one.

## Screens

**1. Overview** (the default, and what's on the screen most of the shift)

- **Track diagram, not a map.** The loop drawn like a metro line from `hello`'s route, in route order,
  with zones as labelled bands. Each band shows OPEN, a CLOSING countdown, or CLOSED. Trucks are chips
  on the line with their id. A truck we're sure of is a chip; a frozen or silent truck is a hatched bar
  over everything it could have reached, with its age. Held trucks show who held them.
- **Zone clearance panel.** One row per closing or closed zone: **CLEAR**, **NOT CLEAR** or **UNSURE**,
  in words, with the countdown. NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both say **"Radio the shot firer to hold the
  shot"** and list the reasons (truck, why: inside, can't get out in time, frozen, silent, faulted).
  UNSURE never looks like CLEAR (invariant 6; answer 1: in doubt, hold the shot). The operator can
  record "I've confirmed it's clear" over UNSURE or NOT CLEAR only with a reason, and both the
  recommendation and their decision go in the log.
- **Attention tray.** Interrupts at the top, each needing an attributed acknowledgement. Below them, the
  silent items, each showing the rule that kept it silent (L2.60–L2.62). Re-alerts at 15 minutes,
  escalates at 30; on nights, when the operator is the supervisor, escalation is more persistent
  alerting to them (L2.63).
- **Fleet table, sorted by attention:** truck, state, zone, SoC as the pack's own number with a flag
  when we doubt it (fractional, draining fast, can't reach the bay), control mode and lease holder, the
  data state in words (live, old 4 s, silent 32 s, contradicted), and the last command with its outcome
  and attempt count.

**2. Truck detail** (click any truck)

- Everything in its table row, plus faults (which, when, where), skew of its clock, battery drain against
  the fleet, and its controller restarts.
- **Command timeline:** each command as sent → acknowledged → effect seen, with times; or "retry 2 of 3";
  or failed with the reason in plain words ("HT-04 is being driven by Marta"). A command blocked by a
  lease is also shown to the lease holder (L8.1).
- Actions: Hold, Resume, Return to bay, Exit zone, Take control. A refusal from the safety check says
  why and what would make it allowed (L2.50–L2.52).

**3. Driving** (after Take control)

- **Lag meter:** input age and echo age, with the deadman threshold marked. **Deadman state** in words.
  Speed, direction, and distance to the next zone boundary with that zone's status.
- Keyboard: hold to drive, release to stop. Losing focus or hiding the window sends zero and stops
  streaming (L7.5).
- Driving into a closed zone is refused at the boundary; driving out never is (L7.6). A limp-home truck
  shows its 1.0 m/s limit; a `BATTERY_DEPLETED` truck says "needs a tow" instead of offering control.
- **Hand-back is two obvious steps:** Release, then Resume. After release the truck shows "held by you —
  Resume" until someone resumes it (L7.9, L9.5).
- A forced takeover says who took it, and when (L7.3).

**4. Audit**

- Answers "who moved HT-06 at 3:12?" directly: pick a truck and a time, and get every command around it
  — operator or system, the rule and inputs for system actions, the ack and the effect (L8.4).

## States each screen must show

| State | Track diagram | Fleet table | Driving view |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live | Solid chip | "live" | Normal |
| Old (> 2 s) | Chip greyed, age shown | "old 4 s" | Lag meter in warning |
| Silent (> 5 s) | Hatched range, age | "silent 32 s" | Deadman expected; says so |
| Contradicted (frozen) | Hatched range, "data frozen" | "contradicted" | Driving refused: position unknown |

screens must pass are in `TESTING.md` (L2.60–L2.64, L7, L9). It is prototyped against the replayed

old trucks from the start, not retrofitted for them.

1. **Answer the question before showing the data.** Priya's "is L4 South clear?" takes 2 seconds: a
   word, not a count of dots.
2. **Never show a guess as a fact.** A truck we're unsure of is drawn as a range over everywhere it
   could be, and labelled in words. When the data stops, the picture ages visibly; it never freezes
   looking current.
3. **Calm until it matters.** Built for a 12-hour shift, on one of four screens: dark, low glare,
   large type. Trucks move smoothly along the line; nothing else animates, pulses or flashes. Sound
   only for interrupts (assumption 11): distinct short tones, never continuous.
4. **Colour never carries meaning alone.** Every state also has a word, a shape or a pattern.
5. **Show what actually happened.** A command is "sent", "acknowledged" and "done" as three separate
   things, and a failure says why in plain words.

  truck. Pressed while the site link is down, it shows **pending, not delivered**, with a cancel; it is
  sent automatically only if the link returns within 10 s, and otherwise asks again with the truck's
  current state (L7.8). It shows "done" only when telemetry confirms `ESTOPPED`.
- **Two link indicators: site and service.** Each shows its own age. If either drops, the whole picture
  greys and every age counter keeps counting (L9.2, L9.3).
- **Who else is on:** operators logged in, their roles, and who holds which truck's lease.
- **Sound armed.** Browsers block sound until the page is clicked. After login the operator clicks once
  to arm it; until then "Sound off" shows in a fixed place, because an interrupt nobody hears isn't one.

  with zones as labelled bands. Each band shows OPEN, a CLOSING countdown, or CLOSED. Trucks are chips
  on the line with their id. A truck we're sure of is a chip; a frozen or silent truck is a hatched bar
  over everything it could have reached, with its age. Held trucks show who held them.

# Task 1: fake gateway, milestone 1

**Goal.** A deterministic fake of the site gateway that plays trucks, commands, leases and blasts
well enough that `research/probe.py` gets the same answers from it as it got from the live site.
It becomes the oracle for the blast-safety tests (`TESTING.md` L4), so it must be right before it is
broad. Fault injectors are milestone 2, a separate task.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md`, then everything it lists. `research/README.md` and the fixtures are the
ground truth for behaviour; `PROTOCOL.md` fills the rest.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L0.M, L0.C4 and L0.C2. Not yet: L0.F, L0.C1, L0.C3, L0.S, L0.P
(design for them, so milestone 2 adds rather than rewrites).

## Scope

1. **Model (L0.M)** in `fake/`, not `src/` (it is test infrastructure). Takes a `Clock` from
   `src/clock.ts` and a seed; never reads the wall clock. The site comes from a config object (route,
   vehicles, notice length), with a default matching DLH-1's `hello` in the fixtures. Nothing
   site-specific is hard-coded in the model itself: a different config must just work.
   - Trucks move along the loop at the spec's speeds, with the duty cycle (load ~20 s at the end of the
     load segment, dump ~12 s at the end of the dump segment, charge below 25 % to 90 % at the end of
     the bay), energy proportional to distance and higher when loaded.
   - Telemetry at ~5 Hz per truck with the fields in `PROTOCOL.md` §4.2; heartbeats every 2 s.
   - Commands per §5 with their effects 1–6 s after acceptance (lease operations and e-stop at once);
     de-duplication on `command_id` (same payload → original result; different payload →
     `COMMAND_ID_REUSED`); every rejection reason in §4.5 where it applies; queuing behind LOADING /
     DUMPING / CHARGING with the newest replacing the older, **behind a parameter** (L0.P: spec version
     only for now).
   - `EXIT_ZONE`: nearest boundary, forward or reverse at the autonomous speed for the load state, stop
     ~2 m outside, hold. `RETURN_TO_BAY`: shorter direction, charge to 90 %, park `IDLE`.
   - Leases per §6: `TAKE_CONTROL` (with `force`), drive messages with `seq` rules, deadman at 500 ms,
     lease expiry at 10 s → `HOLDING`, `RELEASE_CONTROL` with `lease_id`, `lease_event`s, limp-home.
   - A blast schedule: `CLOSING` with the configured notice, `CLOSED`, then `CLEARED` or `CANCELLED`.
   - **Truth access** for tests: the true position and state of every truck, separate from what is sent.
2. **Transport:** an in-process API for tests (push messages in, receive lines out), and a TCP + TLS
   NDJSON server with the auth flow from §1.1, for `probe.py`. Use a test certificate generated at
   test time; never commit a private key.
3. **Determinism (L0.C4):** the same seed and the same inputs give a byte-identical output stream.
4. **Probe conformance (L0.C2):** run `research/probe.py --live` against the fake (point it there
   with `GATEWAY_HOST`, `GATEWAY_PORT`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`) and compare the ack sequence and reasons for
   S1, S3–S8 with the live probe's, which are in `research/README.md` and the fixtures. Where the live
   ack was lost (S1's first HOLD), the fake has no loss in milestone 1, so the expected sequence is the
   spec's. Write the comparison as a test that runs the probe as a subprocess, skipped if `python3` is
   missing.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- Getting the clock wrong: the fake must run a 15-minute day in well under a second with a
  `ManualClock`.
- Making commands take effect instantly. The 1–6 s delay is what makes blast evacuation hard.
- Letting a truck keep moving under a lease without fresh drive input.
- Trusting your own printout. Check the probe comparison against the probe's raw output file.

## Working rules

Tests first. Commit as you go on your worktree branch, one logical change per commit, adding paths
explicitly (never `git add .`/`-A`), with the attribution line from the repository's existing commits.
Don't push and don't merge; I review and merge. If the spec and the research disagree, follow the
research and write the difference down in your summary. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, every
place you guessed, and anything that looked wrong in `PROTOCOL.md` or the research.

# Task 2: ingest and fleet state

**Goal.** Turn the gateway's unreliable stream into a fleet picture that never shows a guess as a
fact: what each truck last reported, how sure we are, and where it could be. Everything downstream
(blast engine, UI, alerts) reads this.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md`, then everything it lists. `research/fixtures/` is the real data; replay
it rather than inventing cases. `UI.md`'s states table is what the operator will see from your output.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L2.1–L2.6 (geometry and reachable sets), L2.10–L2.17 (ingest per fault
class), L2.20–L2.23 (restart versus duplicate), L2.24–L2.26 (frozen detection and the thresholds over
the full captures), L2.27–L2.28 (battery), and L3.1–L3.5, L3.8, L3.10 (fixture replay). L2.7–L2.8
belong to the blast engine; L3.6–L3.7 need the command registry; L3.9 needs the gateway link.

## Scope

In `src/`, using `src/clock.ts`, `src/protocol.ts`, `src/site.ts` and `src/params.ts` as they are. If
one of them needs to change, make that a separate commit and say why.

1. **Parse and validate** one line at a time: truncated or non-JSON lines are dropped and counted;
   unknown `type`s are ignored; each telemetry field is validated on its own, so one bad field makes
   that field unknown (keeping its last known value and age) without discarding the message. Every
   repair or rejection is a data-quality event, counted per truck and per kind.
2. **Ordering:** per-truck controller runs. Duplicates dropped; older messages never overwrite newer
   state; a large `seq` drop while `t_device_ms` moves forward starts a new run (`seq-reset`).
3. **Time:** ages against server time, estimated from `server_time_ms` on heartbeats and other
   messages plus the injected clock. Never from `t_device_ms`; that is shown only as per-truck skew.
4. **Confidence per truck:** live, old, silent or contradicted, using the thresholds in `params.ts`
   (owned by this task; change them only with L2.26 re-run over the full captures). A frozen or silent
   truck has a **reachable range** on the loop: everywhere it could have got to since its last
   believable position, at the speeds it could have had. Ranges wrap.
5. **Battery:** SoC is shown as the pack reports it, flagged when fractional, never scaled. Drain rate

# Task 1: fake gateway, milestone 1

**Goal.** A deterministic fake of the site gateway that plays trucks, commands, leases and blasts
well enough that `research/probe.py` gets the same answers from it as it got from the live site.
It becomes the oracle for the blast-safety tests (`TESTING.md` L4), so it must be right before it is
broad. Fault injectors are milestone 2, a separate task.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md`, then everything it lists. `research/README.md` and the fixtures are the
ground truth for behaviour; `PROTOCOL.md` fills the rest.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L0.M, L0.C4 and L0.C2. Not yet: L0.F, L0.C1, L0.C3, L0.S, L0.P
(design for them, so milestone 2 adds rather than rewrites).

## Scope

1. **Model (L0.M)** in `fake/`, not `src/` (it is test infrastructure). Takes a `Clock` from
   `src/clock.ts` and a seed; never reads the wall clock. The site comes from a config object (route,
   vehicles, notice length), with a default matching DLH-1's `hello` in the fixtures. Nothing
   site-specific is hard-coded in the model itself: a different config must just work.
   - Trucks move along the loop at the spec's speeds, with the duty cycle (load ~20 s at the end of the
     load segment, dump ~12 s at the end of the dump segment, charge below 25 % to 90 % at the end of
     the bay), energy proportional to distance and higher when loaded.
   - Telemetry at ~5 Hz per truck with the fields in `PROTOCOL.md` §4.2; heartbeats every 2 s.
   - Commands per §5 with their effects 1–6 s after acceptance (lease operations and e-stop at once);
     de-duplication on `command_id` (same payload → original result; different payload →
     `COMMAND_ID_REUSED`); every rejection reason in §4.5 where it applies; queuing behind LOADING /
     DUMPING / CHARGING with the newest replacing the older, **behind a parameter** (L0.P: spec version
     only for now).
   - `EXIT_ZONE`: nearest boundary, forward or reverse at the autonomous speed for the load state, stop
     ~2 m outside, hold. `RETURN_TO_BAY`: shorter direction, charge to 90 %, park `IDLE`.
   - Leases per §6: `TAKE_CONTROL` (with `force`), drive messages with `seq` rules, deadman at 500 ms,
     lease expiry at 10 s → `HOLDING`, `RELEASE_CONTROL` with `lease_id`, `lease_event`s, limp-home.
   - A blast schedule: `CLOSING` with the configured notice, `CLOSED`, then `CLEARED` or `CANCELLED`.
   - **Truth access** for tests: the true position and state of every truck, separate from what is sent.
2. **Transport:** an in-process API for tests (push messages in, receive lines out), and a TCP + TLS
   NDJSON server with the auth flow from §1.1, for `probe.py`. Use a test certificate generated at
   test time; never commit a private key.
3. **Determinism (L0.C4):** the same seed and the same inputs give a byte-identical output stream.
4. **Probe conformance (L0.C2):** run `research/probe.py --live` against the fake (point it there
   with `GATEWAY_HOST`, `GATEWAY_PORT`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`) and compare the ack sequence and reasons for
   S1, S3–S8 with the live probe's, which are in `research/README.md` and the fixtures. Where the live
   ack was lost (S1's first HOLD), the fake has no loss in milestone 1, so the expected sequence is the
   spec's. Write the comparison as a test that runs the probe as a subprocess, skipped if `python3` is
   missing.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- Getting the clock wrong: the fake must run a 15-minute day in well under a second with a
  `ManualClock`.
- Making commands take effect instantly. The 1–6 s delay is what makes blast evacuation hard.
- Letting a truck keep moving under a lease without fresh drive input.
- Trusting your own printout. Check the probe comparison against the probe's raw output file.

## Working rules

Tests first. Commit as you go on your worktree branch, one logical change per commit, adding paths
explicitly (never `git add .`/`-A`), with the attribution line from the repository's existing commits.
Don't push and don't merge; I review and merge. If the spec and the research disagree, follow the
research and write the difference down in your summary. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, every
place you guessed, and anything that looked wrong in `PROTOCOL.md` or the research.

Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  ## Task 2 (ingest and fleet state): done, except L2.26 against the full captures, which needs you to run it
  
  Branch **`task/02-ingest`**, in worktree `/Volumes/Transcend/control_room/.claude/worktrees/agent-a66bc5df06ca2fdf4`. The worktree's own branch (`worktree-agent-a66bc5df06ca2fdf4`) was sitting at the repo's first commit, without `src/` or `tasks/`. So I branched from `main` (8312c17). Nothing is pushed or merged, and no `._` files are tracked.
  
  ### What passes
  - `npm test`: **78 tests, 77 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped.**
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean.
  - Covered: L2.1–L2.6, L2.10–L2.17, L2.20–L2.25e, L2.27–L2.28, and L3.1–L3.5, L3.8 and L3.10.
  - I also added the fleet-state half of L3.9: zone state survives the reconnect `hello`, the time left is recalculated, and heartbeats show stale during the outage.
  - L1.1 and L1.3 still pass: no wall clock and no site literals in `src/`.
  - I checked that the frozen tests can fail: with contradiction detection disabled, L2.24, L2.25e, L3.1 and the null-speed test go red; restored, they pass.
  
  ### What does not, or isn't checked yet
  - **L2.26 against the full captures is skipped until you run it.** Run `DLH_CAPTURES=a.jsonl:b.jsonl:c.jsonl node --test test/captures.test.ts`.
    - The expected answers come from an independent oracle computed straight from the raw records, sharing no code with the product. A truck is genuinely silent if it has a gap over 10 s while heartbeats show the link up. It is genuinely frozen if its position is identical for 10 s or more while it reports motion.
    - Every product flag must fall inside one of those episodes, and every episode must be flagged.
    - Each capture prints a summary: outages, silent and frozen episodes, flagged trucks, controller restarts, drain flags and data-quality totals.
    - The same checker passes on the `silent-truck` and `frozen-truck` fixtures.
    - I don't know how it does on the full captures.
  - L3.6, L3.7 and the link half of L3.9 belong to later tasks, as the brief says.
  
  ### Thresholds and rules I chose, and why
  All are in `src/params.ts` with their sources (separate commit `ec443ee`; I added `count` and `ratio` units). The four in `TESTING.md` are unchanged: old 2 s, silent 5 s, frozen 3 s / 0.5 m/s / 0.05 m, link 5 s.
  
  | Name | Value | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | `reorderWindow` | 50 seqs | The deepest reordering in any fixture is 6 seqs. |
  | `telemetryLatencyAllowance` | 1.5 s (measured) | A truck's spread of `t_device − rx` reaches 1.25 s within one fixture; this is added to every range's elapsed time. |
  | `deviceSkewFlagAbove` | 10 s | Every other truck is within 3 s; the skewed one is about +58 min. |
  | `offsetTolerance` | 0.5 m | No fixture has an offset outside its segment. |
  | `fractionalSocJump` | 2 points | See the SoC rule below. |
  | `serverTimeSamples` | 8 | Server-time offset is the max over the last 8 samples, since transit delay only makes a sample too small. |
  | `drainWindow` | 500 m | Drain rate is measured over the last 500 m in each load state. |
  | `drainMinEvidence` | **60 m** | Changed from 100 m: see below. |
  | `drainMaxGap` | 10 s | Over a longer gap the path travelled isn't known. |
  | `drainRatioFlag` | 2× | Healthy trucks are within 1 % of the median (6.0 %/km empty, 9.0 %/km loaded); the weak pack is exactly 5×. |
  | `fleetMinTrucks` | 3 others | Minimum for a fleet median. |
  | `loadedDrainFactor` | 1.5 (measured) | Used only until the fleet itself gives a loaded/empty ratio. |
  | `batteryReserveFactor` | 1.25 | Warns while there's still time to act. |
  
  On `drainMinEvidence`: at 100 m, HT-06 was flagged 64 s in, which fails L3.10's "first minute". The fleet median also needs three *other* trucks with that much running. At 60 m it is flagged at 34 s, and a healthy truck's drop still reads within 3 % at the pack's 0.01 % resolution.
  
  **Rules worth reviewing:**
  - **Restart vs reorder.** A lower seq is a new controller run only if the device clock moved forward *and* (the drop exceeds the window *or* the new seq is within the window). A late message from the old run, which has a higher seq but an older device time, is treated as old.
  - **Frozen.**
    - The clock starts at the first message reporting motion at an unchanged position, and at least one repeat is required.
    - The range is anchored at the last stationary report at that position, or else its first message.
    - Silence takes precedence: a frozen truck that goes quiet shows as silent, keeps its pre-freeze anchor, and its reason says its last data was frozen. The checker found this — I originally left it "contradicted" forever.
  - **Reachable range.**
    - Top speed is the mode's maximum, not the reported speed: 3.0 m/s auto, 4.0 m/s manual. The frozen HT-10 reported 2.0 loaded but had very probably dumped and left empty.
    - Silent, contradicted, manual, tasked or reversing trucks can be anywhere in both directions; other trucks only forward.
    - Range ends count as inside (closed), so a range touching a boundary is in both zones.
    - A truck with no valid position yet, or every truck before `hello`, could be anywhere on the loop.
  - **Fractional SoC.** A value of 1.0 or less is a fraction unless the pack drained smoothly into it, i.e. the previous reading was within 2 points. Exactly 0 is never flagged. It is never scaled, and battery conclusions are suppressed while it's flagged.
  - **Ages** are elapsed time on the injected clock since receipt. Timestamps are mapped onto server time through the learned offset. `t_device_ms` is used only for restart ordering and skew.
  - **Zones.** A route zone missing from `hello` has status `null` (unknown, never open). A `zone_event` older than what we already hold is dropped and counted.
  - **Battery warnings**, in order:
    - `DEPLETED` ("needs a tow").
    - `CANNOT_REACH_BAY`: not enough charge even by the shorter way.
    - `WONT_FINISH_LAP`: the forward duty cycle (load at the end of a `load` segment, dump at the end of a `dump` segment, from `hello`'s kinds) needs more than it has. The message says "return to bay now". It is skipped when the truck is about to charge or is already returning.
  
  ### Public interface the blast engine and UI will read (`src/fleet.ts`)
  - `new FleetState(clock)` with:
    - `ingestLine(line)`, `ingest(msg)`, `newConnection()`
    - `tick()`, `start(ms)`, `stop()`
    - `snapshot(): FleetSnapshot`, `subscribe(fn): unsubscribe`, `serverNow()`, `site`
  - `FleetSnapshot` has `atServerMs`, `siteId`, `loopLengthM`, `heartbeat {lastServerMs, ageMs, stale}`, `zones: ZoneView[]`, `trucks: TruckView[]`, `fleetDrain`, and `dataQuality {total, connection}`.
  - `ZoneView` has `zoneId`, `status | null`, `reason`, `effectiveAtMs`, `msUntilEffective`, `updatedServerMs` and `trucksMightBeIn`.
  - `TruckView` has:
    - `confidence: 'live'|'old'|'silent'|'contradicted'|'unknown'` and `confidenceReason`
    - `ageMs`, `lastMessageServerMs`
    - each reported field as `Known<T> = {value, atServerMs, ageMs} | null`: `state`, `task`, `socPct`, `speedMps`, `direction`, `payloadKg`, `faults`, `control`, `position {segmentId, zoneId, offsetM, loopM}`
    - `socFractional`, `loaded`
    - `anchor`, `range: Range|null`, `mightBeIn: string[]`
    - `frozenEpisodes`, `skewMs`, `skewFlagged`, `run {index, restarts, seq}`, `radio {applied, duplicates, older}`
    - `dataQuality` (`<field>:<problem>` counts)
    - `battery {drain, ratioToFleet, drainHigh, reach {toBay, onRoute}, warning, message}`
  - `FleetEvent` is one of `confidence`, `controller_restart`, `data_quality`, `zone`, `battery` or `site`.
  - Also usable on their own: `src/geometry.ts` (`zoneExit`, `timeToClearMs` with speed and delay overrides, `reachableRange`, `rangesOverlap`, `zonesOverlapping`), `src/ingest.ts` (`parseLine`, `validateTelemetry`, `validateZone`) and `src/battery.ts`.
  - Everything in the snapshot is plain data.
  
  ### Surprises in the fixtures (checked against the files, not printouts)
  1. **`weak-pack.jsonl` is not in arrival order.** HT-06's records (lines 2–614) come first, then the fleet's, starting 535 s earlier. `research/trim.py` writes multi-part fixtures part by part without sorting. The replay helper now sorts by `rx_ms`, and a test asserts the file is out of order on disk. Before the fix, the other trucks were never applied. **`trim.py` should be fixed**; I didn't touch `research/`.
  2. **The weak pack drains through values ≤ 1.0** (0.94 → 0.04 → 0), so "SoC ≤ 1 means a fraction" would have misflagged it. Its first `FAULT` message (seq 2527) still reports 2.0 m/s.
  3. **HT-03's silence is not radio loss.** The last record before the 53 s gap (line 31) is a duplicate of seq 449, and the truck resumes at seq 450 (line 58), so its controller sent nothing in between.
  4. **HT-10 dumped for only 4.4 s** (seq 776–797; the spec says about 12 s), with payload still 42000. The frozen body from seq 798 is TRAMMING, loaded, 2.0 m/s at 59.95, the very end of the loop.
  5. **The malformed-field fault (HT-02) leaves `soc_pct` out entirely** rather than sending null. It also has `speed_mps: null`, `offset_m` as a string, and lowercase `tramming`, `loading`, `manual` and `holding`.

+# agent worktrees
+.claude/worktrees/
+# UI
+The design spec the UI task builds from. The operators are in `OPERATOR_NOTES.md`; the cases these
+screens must pass are in `TESTING.md` (L2.60–L2.64, L7, L9). It is prototyped against the replayed
+`research/fixtures/` before it is wired to the live service, so it is designed around frozen, silent and
+old trucks from the start, not retrofitted for them.
+## Principles
+1. **Answer the question before showing the data.** Priya's "is L4 South clear?" takes 2 seconds: a
+   word, not a count of dots.
+2. **Never show a guess as a fact.** A truck we're unsure of is drawn as a range over everywhere it
+   could be, and labelled in words. When the data stops, the picture ages visibly; it never freezes
+   looking current.
+3. **Calm until it matters.** Built for a 12-hour shift, on one of four screens: dark, low glare,
+   large type. Trucks move smoothly along the line; nothing else animates, pulses or flashes. Sound
+   only for interrupts (assumption 11): distinct short tones, never continuous.
+4. **Colour never carries meaning alone.** Every state also has a word, a shape or a pattern.
+5. **Show what actually happened.** A command is "sent", "acknowledged" and "done" as three separate
+   things, and a failure says why in plain words.
+6. **One obvious next step.** Every alarm names its action; every held truck shows how to resume it.
+## Always on screen
+- **E-stop**, in a fixed place on every view: a distinct shape (octagon), not just red. One press per
+  truck. Pressed while the site link is down, it shows **pending, not delivered**, with a cancel; it is
+  sent automatically only if the link returns within 10 s, and otherwise asks again with the truck's
+  current state (L7.8). It shows "done" only when telemetry confirms `ESTOPPED`.
+- **Two link indicators: site and service.** Each shows its own age. If either drops, the whole picture
+  greys and every age counter keeps counting (L9.2, L9.3).
+- **Who else is on:** operators logged in, their roles, and who holds which truck's lease.
+- **Sound armed.** Browsers block sound until the page is clicked. After login the operator clicks once
+  to arm it; until then "Sound off" shows in a fixed place, because an interrupt nobody hears isn't one.
+## Screens
+**1. Overview** (the default, and what's on the screen most of the shift)
+- **Track diagram, not a map.** The loop drawn like a metro line from `hello`'s route, in route order,
+  with zones as labelled bands. Each band shows OPEN, a CLOSING countdown, or CLOSED. Trucks are chips
+  on the line with their id. A truck we're sure of is a chip; a frozen or silent truck is a hatched bar
+  over everything it could have reached, with its age. Held trucks show who held them.
+- **Zone clearance panel.** One row per closing or closed zone: **CLEAR**, **NOT CLEAR** or **UNSURE**,
+  in words, with the countdown. NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both say **"Radio the shot firer to hold the
+  shot"** and list the reasons (truck, why: inside, can't get out in time, frozen, silent, faulted).
+  UNSURE never looks like CLEAR (invariant 6; answer 1: in doubt, hold the shot). The operator can
+  record "I've confirmed it's clear" over UNSURE or NOT CLEAR only with a reason, and both the
+  recommendation and their decision go in the log.
+- **Attention tray.** Interrupts at the top, each needing an attributed acknowledgement. Below them, the
+  silent items, each showing the rule that kept it silent (L2.60–L2.62). Re-alerts at 15 minutes,
+  escalates at 30; on nights, when the operator is the supervisor, escalation is more persistent
+  alerting to them (L2.63).
+- **Fleet table, sorted by attention:** truck, state, zone, SoC as the pack's own number with a flag
+  when we doubt it (fractional, draining fast, can't reach the bay), control mode and lease holder, the
+  data state in words (live, old 4 s, silent 32 s, contradicted), and the last command with its outcome
+  and attempt count.
+**2. Truck detail** (click any truck)
+- Everything in its table row, plus faults (which, when, where), skew of its clock, battery drain against
+  the fleet, and its controller restarts.
+- **Command timeline:** each command as sent → acknowledged → effect seen, with times; or "retry 2 of 3";
+  or failed with the reason in plain words ("HT-04 is being driven by Marta"). A command blocked by a
+  lease is also shown to the lease holder (L8.1).
+- Actions: Hold, Resume, Return to bay, Exit zone, Take control. A refusal from the safety check says
+  why and what would make it allowed (L2.50–L2.52).
+**3. Driving** (after Take control)
+- **Lag meter:** input age and echo age, with the deadman threshold marked. **Deadman state** in words.
+  Speed, direction, and distance to the next zone boundary with that zone's status.
+- Keyboard: hold to drive, release to stop. Losing focus or hiding the window sends zero and stops
+  streaming (L7.5).
+- Driving into a closed zone is refused at the boundary; driving out never is (L7.6). A limp-home truck
+  shows its 1.0 m/s limit; a `BATTERY_DEPLETED` truck says "needs a tow" instead of offering control.
+- **Hand-back is two obvious steps:** Release, then Resume. After release the truck shows "held by you —
+  Resume" until someone resumes it (L7.9, L9.5).
+- A forced takeover says who took it, and when (L7.3).
+**4. Audit**
+- Answers "who moved HT-06 at 3:12?" directly: pick a truck and a time, and get every command around it
+  — operator or system, the rule and inputs for system actions, the ack and the effect (L8.4).
+## States each screen must show
+| State | Track diagram | Fleet table | Driving view |
+| Live | Solid chip | "live" | Normal |
+| Old (> 2 s) | Chip greyed, age shown | "old 4 s" | Lag meter in warning |
+| Silent (> 5 s) | Hatched range, age | "silent 32 s" | Deadman expected; says so |
+| Contradicted (frozen) | Hatched range, "data frozen" | "contradicted" | Driving refused: position unknown |
+| Site link down | Everything greys; banner with age | All rows aged | "Link down: truck will stop" |
+| Service down | Banner "disconnected"; picture greys | All rows aged | Same |
+| Zone CLOSING / CLOSED | Band with countdown / hatched band | Zone column marked | Boundary status ahead |
+| Command pending / retrying / failed | Badge on chip | Outcome column | Banner |
+| E-stop pending (link down) | Octagon badge "pending" | "e-stop pending" | Octagon "pending" |
+| Fault / limp-home / tow | Chip with fault mark | Fault in words | Limit shown / refused |
+## Prototype
+A fixture player feeds `research/fixtures/` through ingest and fleet state into the UI, with time
+controls, so each screen can be checked against frozen-truck, silent-truck, link-drop-in-notice,
+two-zones-closing and weak-pack before it ever touches the gateway. Screenshots from the player become
+the README walkthrough, revised after the novice test (L11).

+// Battery (TESTING.md L2.27-L2.28; CONTEXT.md assumption 13). The pack's own SoC is always shown as
+// reported. Beside it: the truck's drain per metre against the fleet, and whether it can reach the
+// bay on what it has, at its own rate. Warnings name the action; acting stays with the operator.
+import { forwardDistance, normalise } from './geometry.ts';
+import { PARAMS } from './params.ts';
+import type { Direction, Task, VehicleState } from './protocol.ts';
+import type { Site } from './site.ts';
+// PROTOCOL.md §6.6: the fault a truck cannot limp home from.
+export const DEPLETED_FAULT = 'BATTERY_DEPLETED';
+interface Sample { dropPct: number; distM: number }
+// The last PARAMS.drainWindow metres of travel in one load state.
+class DrainWindow {
+  #samples: Sample[] = [];
+  #drop = 0;
+  #dist = 0;
+  add(dropPct: number, distM: number): void {
+    this.#samples.push({ dropPct, distM });
+    this.#drop += dropPct;
+    this.#dist += distM;
+    while (this.#samples.length > 1 && this.#dist - this.#samples[0]!.distM >= PARAMS.drainWindow.value) {
+      const s = this.#samples.shift()!;
+      this.#drop -= s.dropPct;
+      this.#dist -= s.distM;
+  get evidenceM(): number { return this.#dist; }
+  // %/m, or null without enough evidence.
+  rate(): number | null {
+    return this.#dist >= PARAMS.drainMinEvidence.value ? Math.max(0, this.#drop) / this.#dist : null;
+export class DrainTracker {
+  readonly empty = new DrainWindow();
+  readonly loaded = new DrainWindow();
+  add(loaded: boolean, dropPct: number, distM: number): void {
+    (loaded ? this.loaded : this.empty).add(dropPct, distM);
+export interface FleetDrain {
+  emptyPctPerM: number | null;
+  loadedPctPerM: number | null;
+export function median(xs: number[]): number | null {
+  if (xs.length === 0) return null;
+  const s = [...xs].sort((a, b) => a - b);
+  const mid = s.length >> 1;
+  return s.length % 2 ? s[mid]! : (s[mid - 1]! + s[mid]!) / 2;
+// The median of other trucks' rates, if there are enough of them.
+export function fleetMedianExcluding(rates: Array<{ id: string; rate: number | null }>, self: string): number | null {
+  const others = rates.filter((r) => r.id !== self && r.rate !== null).map((r) => r.rate!);
+  return others.length >= PARAMS.fleetMinTrucks.value ? median(others) : null;
+export interface PathLegs { distanceM: number; emptyM: number; loadedM: number }
+// Shorter way to the nearest bay: forward to a bay's start or back to its end. Zero inside one.
+export function shorterWayToBay(site: Site, positionM: number): { direction: Direction; distanceM: number } | null {
+  const L = site.loopLengthM;
+  const bays = site.bayZones().flatMap((z) => z.ranges);
+  if (bays.length === 0) return null;
+  const p = normalise(L, positionM);
+  let fwd = Infinity, rev = Infinity;
+  for (const r of bays) {
+    if (forwardDistance(L, r.startM, p) < r.lengthM) return { direction: 'FWD', distanceM: 0 };
+    fwd = Math.min(fwd, forwardDistance(L, p, r.startM));
+    rev = Math.min(rev, forwardDistance(L, normalise(L, r.startM + r.lengthM), p));
+  return fwd <= rev ? { direction: 'FWD', distanceM: fwd } : { direction: 'REV', distanceM: rev };
+// The autonomous duty cycle forward from `positionM` to the next arrival at a bay: a truck becomes
+// loaded at the end of a load segment and empty at the end of a dump segment (PROTOCOL.md §3; kinds
+// come from hello). A truck starting inside a bay first leaves it.
+export function dutyCycleToBay(site: Site, positionM: number, loaded: boolean): PathLegs | null {
+  const L = site.loopLengthM;
+  const segs = site.segments;
+  if (segs.length === 0 || !segs.some((s) => s.kind === 'bay')) return null;
+  const p = normalise(L, positionM);
+  let i = segs.findIndex((s) => forwardDistance(L, s.startM, p) < s.lengthM);
+  if (i < 0) return null;
+  let left = segs[i]!.lengthM - forwardDistance(L, segs[i]!.startM, p);
+  let leftBay = segs[i]!.kind !== 'bay';
+  let state = loaded;
+  const legs: PathLegs = { distanceM: 0, emptyM: 0, loadedM: 0 };
+  for (let steps = 0; steps <= 2 * segs.length + 1; steps++) {
+    const s = segs[i]!;
+    legs.distanceM += left;
+    if (state) legs.loadedM += left; else legs.emptyM += left;
+    if (s.kind === 'load' && !state) state = true;
+    else if (s.kind === 'dump' && state) state = false;
+    i = (i + 1) % segs.length;
+    const next = segs[i]!;
+    if (next.kind !== 'bay') leftBay = true;
+    else if (leftBay) return legs;
+    left = next.lengthM;
+  return null;
+export type BatteryWarning = 'DEPLETED' | 'CANNOT_REACH_BAY' | 'WONT_FINISH_LAP';
+export interface Reach {
+  toBay: { direction: Direction; distanceM: number; needPct: number } | null;
+  onRoute: { distanceM: number; needPct: number } | null;
+  rateSource: 'own' | 'own, loaded estimated' | 'fleet' | null;
+export interface Assessment {
+  reach: Reach;
+  warning: BatteryWarning | null;
+  message: string | null;
+export interface BatteryInput {
+  site: Site | undefined;
+  socPct: number | undefined;
+  socFractional: boolean;
+  positionM: number | undefined;
+  loaded: boolean | undefined;
+  state: VehicleState | undefined;
+  task: Task | null | undefined;
+  faults: string[] | undefined;
+  ownEmpty: number | null; // %/m
+  ownLoaded: number | null;
+  fleet: FleetDrain;
+const NO_REACH: Reach = { toBay: null, onRoute: null, rateSource: null };
+export function assess(b: BatteryInput): Assessment {
+  if (b.faults?.includes(DEPLETED_FAULT)) {
+    return { reach: NO_REACH, warning: 'DEPLETED', message: 'Battery depleted: needs a tow; cannot be driven' };
+  if (!b.site || b.socPct === undefined || b.socFractional || b.positionM === undefined || b.loaded === undefined) {
+    return { reach: NO_REACH, warning: null, message: null };
+  const rates = rateFor(b);
+  if (!rates) return { reach: NO_REACH, warning: null, message: null };
+  const need = (empty: number, loadedM: number) => empty * rates.empty + loadedM * rates.loaded;
+  const way = shorterWayToBay(b.site, b.positionM);
+  const toBay = way && { ...way, needPct: b.loaded ? need(0, way.distanceM) : need(way.distanceM, 0) };
+  const legs = b.task === 'RETURN_TO_BAY' ? null : dutyCycleToBay(b.site, b.positionM, b.loaded);
+  const onRoute = legs && { distanceM: legs.distanceM, needPct: need(legs.emptyM, legs.loadedM) };
+  const reach: Reach = { toBay, onRoute, rateSource: rates.source };
+  if (b.state === 'CHARGING') return { reach, warning: null, message: null };
+  const reserve = PARAMS.batteryReserveFactor.value;
+  const soc = b.socPct;
+  const pct = (x: number) => `${x.toFixed(1)} %`;
+  if (toBay && soc < toBay.needPct * reserve) {
+    return {
+      reach, warning: 'CANNOT_REACH_BAY',
+      message: `May not reach the bay: needs about ${pct(toBay.needPct)} going ${toBay.direction === 'FWD' ? 'forward' : 'back'}, has ${pct(soc)}. Return to bay now and plan for a tow`,
+  const inBay = toBay?.distanceM === 0;
+  const willCharge = inBay && soc < PARAMS.chargeBelow.value;
+  if (onRoute && !willCharge && soc < onRoute.needPct * reserve) {
+    return {
+      reach, warning: 'WONT_FINISH_LAP',
+      message: `Will not finish its lap on this charge: needs about ${pct(onRoute.needPct)}, has ${pct(soc)}. Return to bay now, while it still can`,
+  return { reach, warning: null, message: null };
+// The truck's own rates where known; a missing load state is estimated from the other one by the
+// fleet's loaded/empty ratio (or the measured factor); with no own data, the fleet's median.
+function rateFor(b: BatteryInput): { empty: number; loaded: number; source: Reach['rateSource'] } | null {
+  const fleetRatio = b.fleet.emptyPctPerM && b.fleet.loadedPctPerM ? b.fleet.loadedPctPerM / b.fleet.emptyPctPerM : PARAMS.loadedDrainFactor.value;
+  if (b.ownEmpty !== null && b.ownLoaded !== null) return { empty: b.ownEmpty, loaded: b.ownLoaded, source: 'own' };
+  if (b.ownEmpty !== null) return { empty: b.ownEmpty, loaded: b.ownEmpty * fleetRatio, source: 'own, loaded estimated' };
+  if (b.ownLoaded !== null) return { empty: b.ownLoaded / fleetRatio, loaded: b.ownLoaded, source: 'own, loaded estimated' };
+  if (b.fleet.emptyPctPerM !== null && b.fleet.loadedPctPerM !== null) return { empty: b.fleet.emptyPctPerM, loaded: b.fleet.loadedPctPerM, source: 'fleet' };

content.text: Two things from this review belong in AI_LOG: the agent's own checker was wrong about the product, and the agent caught a bug of mine. Adding entry 3 while it's fresh:

input.command:
cat >> AI_LOG.md <<'EOF'

---

## 3. The ingest agent's checker failed the product, and the product was right

**Session:** planning session, ingest task run as a sub-agent in its own worktree, 2026-10-02.

**Asked.** Task 2 (`tasks/02-ingest.md`): ingest and fleet state, tests first, from `TESTING.md`.
The threshold test L2.26 had to run over the full captures, which aren't in the repo, so the agent
wrote it to read their paths from an environment variable, and I ran it.

**Came back.** 77 passing tests and a careful report. For L2.26 the agent built an independent
checker that shares no code with the product, which was the right instinct. Run against the
captures, it failed the product on run 2: HT-08 "flagged silent at +873 s with no genuine silence".

**What was wrong.** The checker, not the product. It discarded any gap in a truck's messages that
touched a link outage. In the raw capture the link returned at +866.7 s, heartbeats arrived every 2 s
and other trucks reported, while HT-08 stayed quiet until +896.9 s: 30 s of real silence, which the
product flagged correctly. Had I trusted the test, I would have "fixed" correct product code.

**How it was found.** By reading the raw capture around the failure instead of the assertion message:
link events, heartbeats, HT-08's messages, another truck's messages.

**What was done.** The checker now cuts outages out of each gap and judges the link-up pieces on their
own (`ae8dcf2`). L2.26 then passed on all three captures, flagging exactly the trucks found by hand.

The same review ran the other way. The agent found that my `research/trim.py` wrote the weak-pack
fixture out of arrival order, and said so rather than quietly working around it. I checked the file,
confirmed it, and fixed the script (`8250678`). An independent check is only as good as its own
definition of the truth, whoever wrote it.
EOF

One test runs an invented 3-truck site with a 900 m loop and a 60 s notice through the same model.
  - **L0.C4:** the same seed and inputs give a byte-identical 15-minute day; a different seed gives a different day. A day costs about 0.5 s of CPU.
  - **L0.C2:** `probe.py --live` against the fake over TLS. I generate the certificate at test time and build the probe's environment from scratch, pointing only at 127.0.0.1. The test stops the probe when S9 starts: S9 waits up to 240 s for a frozen truck, which the fake can't produce until milestone 2, and S9 is outside L0.C2 anyway.   - **S4:** TAKE_CONTROL accepted with lease details, HOLD gets `LEASE_HELD` naming the holder, RESUME accepted. The deadman tripped 501–790 ms after the grant on the gateway's clock; the lease expired at 10.02 s.

content.thinking: Adding another AI_LOG entry: the ack-counting trap has now tripped up three separate pieces of code, reinforcing the need to centralize ack-to-send matching in one tested place.

input.command:
cat >> AI_LOG.md <<'EOF'

---

## 4. The same ack-matching mistake, three times, by two different authors

**Session:** planning session; fake gateway run as a sub-agent in its own worktree, 2026-10-02.

**Asked.** Task 1 (`tasks/01-fake-gateway.md`): a fake gateway that gives `research/probe.py` the same
answers as the live site (L0.C2). In review, I compared the fake's acks with the live probe's.

**Came back.** The agent reported that its own probe checker had been wrong: it paired acks with
sends inside a 50 ms window, and S1's resend and reuse go out 50 ms apart, so the resend's ack was
credited to the reuse. It found this in the raw file and fixed it. Then my review comparison flagged
two S1 mismatches between the live probe and the fake.

**What was wrong.** My comparison, not the fake. It matched the nth ack of a `command_id` to its nth
send. Live, the first `HOLD`'s ack was lost, so everything after it shifted by one: exactly the
mistake in entry 1, made again by me in the review meant to catch such things. Read correctly,
the fake matches the live probe on every command of S1 and S3–S8 except the lost ack, which the
fake does not inject until milestone 2.

**How it was found.** The two "mismatches" were both on the one id with a lost ack; reading the raw
send and ack lines for that id showed the shift.

**What was done.** Recorded the corrected result in the merge commit (`54b6d26`). The lesson is that
remembering doesn't work: three pieces of code by two authors made the same mistake within a day. Ack
correlation (by time, against the latest send) belongs in one tested place, the command registry
(`TESTING.md` L2.33), and every later tool that reads acks uses it rather than rewriting it.
EOF

content.text:
Both parallel tasks are now merged into main, reviewed against raw data. `npm test` runs 122 tests in about 25 s, with L2.26 skipped as designed; the conformance test passes separately. Nothing is pushed.

**The fake gateway, milestone 1:**
- **Conformance holds against the live recording, not just the spec.** Its acks match the real probe on every command of S1 and S3–S8. The one exception is S1's lost ack: loss is a fault injector, which comes in milestone 2.
- **Same seed, same day:** a seed produces a byte-identical 15-minute day, in about 0.5 s of CPU.
- **Its changes to shared files only add rules.** The fake must also take an injected clock, and only its default site config may contain this site's literals.
- **Its biggest open point is ack latency:** the fake answers instantly, where the real gateway doesn't. That's for milestone 2.

**What I changed in review:**
- **The probe-conformance test moved out of `npm test`** into `npm run test:slow`. It takes 2.5 minutes, too slow for test-first work; `npm run check` still runs everything. My first attempt at the header note was a careless `sed` that inserted it before every comment in the file. I restored the file and confirmed that only the two intended lines changed.
- **research/README.md now records three things from the agent's work:**
  - S9's `INVALID_STATE` fits a truck still carrying out its `EXIT_ZONE`. So a `RESUME` can't interrupt an `EXIT_ZONE`; the blast engine must send `HOLD` first.
  - Our live "~0.4 s" deadman was measured on receive times and may understate. The spec's 500 ms is the safer figure.
  - Six questions the spec leaves open, each answered by a marked guess in the fake.
- **AI_LOG entry 4.** The entry-1 ack-matching mistake struck twice more today: in the agent's probe checker, which it caught itself, and in my own comparison while reviewing it. The lesson in the log is that ack matching belongs in one tested place, the command registry (L2.33), for everything to reuse.

**What I'd do next:**
- **Run two tasks in parallel:** fake-gateway milestone 2 (fault injectors, pessimistic queuing, L0.C1/C3, site variants), and the command registry (task 4) with the gateway link (task 3). The registry is where the ack-matching rule finally gets built once.
- **Meanwhile, write the blast engine's rules spec myself.** It has to include `HOLD` before any `RESUME` that would cancel an evacuation.

Two questions are still waiting on you:
- **When should the queuing re-probe's real commands go out?**
- **Should it also measure the loaded reverse speed?**

Nice, UI.md is good — the sound-arming point is one i missed lol.

Answers:
- Queuing re-probe: approved, at the start of the registry task, since that's when L2.36's deadlines get built. Only while DRAW_12 isn't closing, operator_id "probe", cleanup confirmed in telemetry rather than assumed, and the times recorded in research/README.md. Tell me just before it runs.
- Loaded reverse speed: yes, in the same run — one EXIT_ZONE on a loaded truck turns our last assumed speed into a measured one.

A few more things:

1. AI_SESSIONS.md only lists this session, but the fake gateway and ingest were built by the two sub-agents in worktrees, and the brief wants sessions covering the whole build. Add rows for both, and plan to export their transcripts into ai-sessions/ if they can't be share-linked. Strip my account email from every export — it's in each transcript's metadata.

2. The blast engine's rules spec: draft it, but I've to review and edit  before anything is built on it per PLAN.md. Show me the draft before it's committed.

3. Start the UI now, as a third task: the fixture player and the Overview screen from UI.md, against replayed fixtures. It needs only ingest and fleet state, which are merged; it touches no gateway and sends no commands, and it fits in the time the blast engine waits for milestone 2, the registry and the rules spec. Priorities, in order: the track diagram with ranges for unsure trucks, the zone clearance panel, and the fleet table. Screenshot each fixture's state as you go — they become the README walkthrough.

4. Push to origin/main now, and after each merge. The repo is on an external (/transcend/control_room) drive and GitHub is the only backup; it stays private until submission.

Then go: fake-gateway milestone 2 and the registry with the gateway link, as you proposed, plus the UI task.
