70	## 3. The ingest agent's checker failed the product, and the product was right
71	
72	**Session:** planning session, ingest task run as a sub-agent in its own worktree, 2026-10-02.
73	
74	**Asked.** Task 2 (`tasks/02-ingest.md`): ingest and fleet state, tests first, from `TESTING.md`.
75	The threshold test L2.26 had to run over the full captures, which aren't in the repo, so the agent
76	wrote it to read their paths from an environment variable, and I ran it.
77	
78	**Came back.** 77 passing tests and a careful report. For L2.26 the agent built an independent
79	checker that shares no code with the product, which was the right instinct. Run against the
80	captures, it failed the product on run 2: HT-08 "flagged silent at +873 s with no genuine silence".
81	
82	**What was wrong.** The checker, not the product. It discarded any gap in a truck's messages that
83	touched a link outage. In the raw capture the link returned at +866.7 s, heartbeats arrived every 2 s
84	and other trucks reported, while HT-08 stayed quiet until +896.9 s: 30 s of real silence, which the
85	product flagged correctly. Had I trusted the test, I would have "fixed" correct product code.
86	
87	**How it was found.** By reading the raw capture around the failure instead of the assertion message:
88	link events, heartbeats, HT-08's messages, another truck's messages.
89	
90	**What was done.** The checker now cuts outages out of each gap and judges the link-up pieces on their
91	own (`ae8dcf2`). L2.26 then passed on all three captures, flagging exactly the trucks found by hand.
92	
93	The same review ran the other way. The agent found that my `research/trim.py` wrote the weak-pack
94	fixture out of arrival order, and said so rather than quietly working around it. I checked the file,
95	confirmed it, and fixed the script (`8250678`). An independent check is only as good as its own
96	definition of the truth, whoever wrote it.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 4. The same ack-matching mistake, three times, by two different authors
101	
102	**Session:** planning session; fake gateway run as a sub-agent in its own worktree, 2026-10-02.
103	
104	**Asked.** Task 1 (`tasks/01-fake-gateway.md`): a fake gateway that gives `research/probe.py` the same
105	answers as the live site (L0.C2). In review, I compared the fake's acks with the live probe's.
106	
107	**Came back.** The agent reported that its own probe checker had been wrong: it paired acks with
108	sends inside a 50 ms window, and S1's resend and reuse go out 50 ms apart, so the resend's ack was
109	credited to the reuse. It found this in the raw file and fixed it. Then my review comparison flagged
110	two S1 mismatches between the live probe and the fake.
111	
112	**What was wrong.** My comparison, not the fake. It matched the nth ack of a `command_id` to its nth
113	send. Live, the first `HOLD`'s ack was lost, so everything after it shifted by one: exactly the
114	mistake in entry 1, made again by me in the review meant to catch such things. Read correctly,
115	the fake matches the live probe on every command of S1 and S3–S8 except the lost ack, which the
116	fake does not inject until milestone 2.
117	
118	**How it was found.** The two "mismatches" were both on the one id with a lost ack; reading the raw
119	send and ack lines for that id showed the shift.
120	
121	**What was done.** Recorded the corrected result in the merge commit (`54b6d26`). The lesson is that
122	remembering doesn't work: three pieces of code by two authors made the same mistake within a day. Ack
123	correlation (by time, against the latest send) belongs in one tested place, the command registry
124	(`TESTING.md` L2.33), and every later tool that reads acks uses it rather than rewriting it.

Four things, in this order:
1. **Push.** I'll scan the whole history for the email and secrets first, since GitHub keeps whatever goes up.
2. **Sessions.** Add AI_SESSIONS.md rows for both sub-agents, and export their transcripts now. They live under `/private/tmp`, which may not outlive this session.

# Task 1b: fake gateway, milestone 2

**Goal.** Give the fake gateway the faults the live site has, the pessimistic versions of what we
haven't verified, and other sites, and prove it matches the live statistics. After this, its
results count as the oracle for blast safety (`TESTING.md` L4).

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md` and everything it lists; `tasks/01-fake-gateway.md` (milestone 1);
`research/README.md`, especially "Radio and blast statistics", "Verified, and not" and "Open in the
spec". Milestone 1's code is in `fake/`.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L0.F, L0.P, L0.S, L0.C1 and L0.C3, with L0.M, L0.C2 and L0.C4 still passing.

## Scope

1. **Fault injectors (L0.F)**, one per class, each switchable, seeded and recorded in the fake's truth
   log (which truck, when, what), so a test can ask "what was really wrong at time t". The classes are
   listed in L0.F. Their shapes come from the fixtures: a frozen truck repeats its whole message with
   `seq` and `t_device_ms` still advancing (`frozen-truck`); a truck that freezes while stationary
   then moves is its own injector, since it is the undetectable case (L4.R2c). Rates and lengths come
   from the statistics table. A "default day" turns on the live catalogue: one truck per fault class,
   at random, as the live site does.
2. **Ack latency.** Milestone 1 answers instantly; the live gateway doesn't. Measure the send-to-ack
   delay from the live probe log (ask me for it; it is not in the repo) or from
   `research/fixtures/accepted-then-ignored-resume.jsonl`, which has sends and acks, and model it.
   Lost acks and accepted-then-ignored commands are injectors.
3. **Pessimistic versions (L0.P)**, as parameters: queued commands sometimes dropped without notice;
   loaded reverse at 1.5 m/s. A live re-probe of queuing and loaded reverse speed runs at the start of
   the registry task; when its results land in `research/README.md`, update the spec versions to match
   in a separate commit.
4. **Site variants (L0.S):** a different route and zone names, 7 and 20 trucks, a 60 s notice; plus BAY
   closing.
5. **Conformance:** L0.C1 (each fixture's fault, injected, is flagged by `research/report.py` the same
   way) and L0.C3 (a 15-minute default day within the measured ranges; any gap written down).
6. **Number formatting:** milestone 1 serialises `2.0` as `2`. The live site sends `2.0`. Match it if it
   is cheap; otherwise write down why it doesn't matter to ingest.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- A fault that the fake's truth log doesn't record: the blast tests then can't tell a correct alarm
  from a false one.
- Faults that happen to be easy: the live frozen truck reports motion; a link drop lands inside a
  blast notice in two of three live runs; the weak pack dies in the incline. Make sure the default day
  can produce each of these.
- Breaking determinism (L0.C4) with a new source of randomness.
- Trusting your own printout. L0.C1 runs `research/report.py`: compare against its output file.

## Working rules

Tests first. Commit as you go on your branch, one logical change per commit, adding paths explicitly
(never `git add .`/`-A`). Before starting, make sure your branch is based on local `main`, not on a
stale `origin/main`. Don't push and don't merge; I review, merge and push. Never connect to the real
gateway. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, every place you guessed, and anything in the
research that disagrees with what you built.

# Task 6a: UI, the fixture player and the Overview screen

**Goal.** The operator's main screen, built against replayed fixtures before it touches the
gateway, so it is designed around frozen, silent and old trucks from the start. `UI.md` is the
design spec; this task builds its fixture player and its Overview screen.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md` and everything it lists; then `UI.md`, which wins over anything here on
how things look. Read `OPERATOR_NOTES.md` again before you design anything: Priya, Dave and Ken are
the users. The data comes from `src/fleet.ts` (`FleetState`, `FleetSnapshot`); read its types first.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L9.1 (live, old, silent and contradicted trucks look different), and the
Overview states in `UI.md`'s table. Not yet: L9.2–L9.5, which need the service and driving.

## Scope, in priority order

1. **Fixture player:** replays a fixture from `research/fixtures/` through `FleetState` with a
   `ManualClock`, with play, pause, step and speed controls, and serves snapshots to the browser.
   No gateway, no commands: this task sends nothing anywhere.
2. **Track diagram:** the loop as a metro line from `hello`'s route, in route order, zones as labelled
   bands with their status (OPEN, a CLOSING countdown, CLOSED), trucks as chips. A frozen or silent
   truck is a hatched bar over its reachable range (`TruckView.range`), with its age. Ranges wrap.
   It must work for any site: test it with a different route (`test/site.test.ts` has one).
3. **Zone clearance panel:** for each closing or closed zone, CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE, in words, with
   the countdown and the reasons; NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both say "Radio the shot firer to hold the
   shot". **The blast engine's rules are still being written.** For now implement only invariant 6,
   from belief: NOT CLEAR if a live or old truck is in the zone; UNSURE if only a silent, contradicted
   or unknown truck's range overlaps it; CLEAR only if no truck might be inside. Put that rule in one
   small pure function in `src/` with its own tests and a comment saying the blast engine will own it.
4. **Fleet table, sorted by attention:** truck, state, zone, SoC as the pack reports it with a flag when
   doubted (fractional, draining fast, can't reach the bay), control mode and lease holder, data state
   in words, and a placeholder for the last command (the registry isn't built yet).
5. **Always-on elements**, as far as they make sense without a service: the e-stop's place and shape
   (inert, labelled "not connected" in the player), the site-link indicator from heartbeat age, and
   "Sound off".

## How it is built

`PLAN.md` says a plain browser UI. No front-end framework, and no build step unless you justify one:
Node 24 can strip TypeScript types for the browser (`module.stripTypeScriptTypes`), so the server can
serve `.ts` modules directly. Keep UI code that doesn't need the DOM in pure functions, tested with
`node --test`. Product code still follows L1.1 and L1.3: time from the injected clock, nothing site-
specific. Dark, low glare, large type, colour never alone (`UI.md` principles).

## Screenshots

Take a screenshot of the Overview at each fixture's telling moment (the freeze, the silence, the link
drop, both zones closing, the weak pack's warning, and so on) and commit them under `docs/screenshots/`
with a short index saying what each shows. They become the README walkthrough. Use Playwright if it
runs on this machine (macOS 12); if not, use a headless Chrome directly, and say which.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- An unsure truck drawn as a dot. A range is the point.
- UNSURE that looks anything like CLEAR, in colour, word or position.
- A picture that looks current when the data has stopped.
- Motion or flashing that isn't needed: only the trucks move.
- Hard-coding this site's zones or loop.

## Working rules

Tests first for the pure parts. Commit as you go on your branch, one logical change per commit,
adding paths explicitly (never `git add .`/`-A`). Before starting, make sure your branch is based on
local `main`, not on a stale `origin/main`. Don't push and don't merge; I review, merge and push.
Never connect to any gateway. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, screenshots taken, every design
choice you made that `UI.md` didn't decide, and anything in `UI.md` that didn't work in practice.

how things look. Read `OPERATOR_NOTES.md` again before you design anything: Priya, Dave and Ken are
the users. The data comes from `src/fleet.ts` (`FleetState`, `FleetSnapshot`); read its types first.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L9.1 (live, old, silent and contradicted trucks look different), and the
Overview states in `UI.md`'s table. Not yet: L9.2–L9.5, which need the service and driving.

## Scope, in priority order

1. **Fixture player:** replays a fixture from `research/fixtures/` through `FleetState` with a
   `ManualClock`, with play, pause, step and speed controls, and serves snapshots to the browser.
   No gateway, no commands: this task sends nothing anywhere.
2. **Track diagram:** the loop as a metro line from `hello`'s route, in route order, zones as labelled
   bands with their status (OPEN, a CLOSING countdown, CLOSED), trucks as chips. A frozen or silent
   truck is a hatched bar over its reachable range (`TruckView.range`), with its age. Ranges wrap.
   It must work for any site: test it with a different route (`test/site.test.ts` has one).
3. **Zone clearance panel:** for each closing or closed zone, CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE, in words, with
   the countdown and the reasons; NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both say "Radio the shot firer to hold the
   shot". **The blast engine's rules are still being written.** For now implement only invariant 6,
   from belief: NOT CLEAR if a live or old truck is in the zone; UNSURE if only a silent, contradicted
   or unknown truck's range overlaps it; CLEAR only if no truck might be inside. Put that rule in one
   small pure function in `src/` with its own tests and a comment saying the blast engine will own it.
4. **Fleet table, sorted by attention:** truck, state, zone, SoC as the pack reports it with a flag when
   doubted (fractional, draining fast, can't reach the bay), control mode and lease holder, data state
   in words, and a placeholder for the last command (the registry isn't built yet).
5. **Always-on elements**, as far as they make sense without a service: the e-stop's place and shape
   (inert, labelled "not connected" in the player), the site-link indicator from heartbeat age, and
   "Sound off".

## How it is built

`PLAN.md` says a plain browser UI. No front-end framework, and no build step unless you justify one:
Node 24 can strip TypeScript types for the browser (`module.stripTypeScriptTypes`), so the server can
serve `.ts` modules directly. Keep UI code that doesn't need the DOM in pure functions, tested with
`node --test`. Product code still follows L1.1 and L1.3: time from the injected clock, nothing site-
specific. Dark, low glare, large type, colour never alone (`UI.md` principles).

## Screenshots

Take a screenshot of the Overview at each fixture's telling moment (the freeze, the silence, the link
drop, both zones closing, the weak pack's warning, and so on) and commit them under `docs/screenshots/`
with a short index saying what each shows. They become the README walkthrough. Use Playwright if it
runs on this machine (macOS 12); if not, use a headless Chrome directly, and say which.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- An unsure truck drawn as a dot. A range is the point.
- UNSURE that looks anything like CLEAR, in colour, word or position.
- A picture that looks current when the data has stopped.
- Motion or flashing that isn't needed: only the trucks move.
- Hard-coding this site's zones or loop.

## Working rules

Tests first for the pure parts. Commit as you go on your branch, one logical change per commit,
adding paths explicitly (never `git add .`/`-A`). Before starting, make sure your branch is based on
local `main`, not on a stale `origin/main`. Don't push and don't merge; I review, merge and push.
Never connect to any gateway. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, screenshots taken, every design
choice you made that `UI.md` didn't decide, and anything in `UI.md` that didn't work in practice.

import json, os, socket, ssl, sys, threading, time, uuid

OPERATOR = 'probe'
RUN = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
LIVE = '--live' in sys.argv

PLAN = [
    ('S1 hold/resume', 'TRAMMING truck in a transit zone: HOLD, time ack and stop; resend the same command_id '
     '(expect original result, no re-execution); reuse the id with a different action (expect COMMAND_ID_REUSED); RESUME.'),
    ('S2 queued hold', 'LOADING truck: HOLD (expect queued until loading ends), then RESUME (expect it to cancel the queued HOLD).'),
    ('S3 exit zone', 'TRAMMING truck mid-zone in a transit zone: EXIT_ZONE; record direction, speed and where it stops; RESUME.'),
    ('S4 lease expiry', 'TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; send no drive input; expect deadman true at ~0.5 s; send HOLD while '
     'leased (expect LEASE_HELD); wait for lease EXPIRED at ~10 s; RESUME.'),
    ('S5 drive', 'TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; drive throttle +0.3 for 3 s at 10 Hz with sent_ms, then 0 for 1 s; '
     'measure drive-echo latency; RELEASE_CONTROL with a wrong lease_id (expect NOT_LEASE_HOLDER), then the right one; RESUME.'),
    ('S6 estop', 'TRAMMING truck: ESTOP; HOLD (expect ESTOP_ACTIVE); CLEAR_ESTOP; RESUME.'),
    ('S7 rejections', 'UNKNOWN_VEHICLE, MISSING_OPERATOR, UNSUPPORTED_ACTION, missing command_id, and one unparseable line.'),
    ('S8 faulted truck', 'If a truck is in FAULT: HOLD (expect INTERLOCK_ACTIVE). Nothing else.'),
    ('S9 frozen truck', 'Wait up to 240 s for a truck reporting speed > 0.5 with an unchanged position for 8 s; '
     'if found outside BAY, EXIT_ZONE it and record what telemetry and acks say for 40 s; RESUME.'),
]

if not LIVE:
    print('DRY RUN: nothing will be sent. Pass --live to run.\n')
    print('operator_id = %r, command_id = "probe-<run>-<n>"\n' % OPERATOR)
    for name, what in PLAN: print('%-18s %s' % (name, what))
    print('\nExample messages:')
    for ex in ({'type': 'command', 'command_id': 'probe-%s-1' % RUN, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'action': 'HOLD', 'operator_id': OPERATOR},
               {'type': 'command', 'command_id': 'probe-%s-9' % RUN, 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'action': 'TAKE_CONTROL', 'operator_id': OPERATOR},
               {'type': 'drive', 'vehicle_id': 'HT-xx', 'lease_id': '<from ack>', 'seq': 1, 'throttle': 0.3, 'sent_ms': 0}):

S3 exit zone               TRAMMING truck mid-zone in a transit zone: EXIT_ZONE; record direction, speed and where it stops; RESUME.
S4 lease expiry            TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; send no drive input; expect deadman true at ~0.5 s; send HOLD while leased (expect LEASE_HELD); wait for lease EXPIRED at ~10 s; RESUME.
S5 drive                   TRAMMING truck: TAKE_CONTROL; drive throttle +0.3 for 3 s at 10 Hz with sent_ms, then 0 for 1 s; measure drive-echo latency; RELEASE_CONTROL with a wrong lease_id (expect NOT_LEASE_HOLDER), then the right one; RESUME.

S7 rejections              UNKNOWN_VEHICLE, MISSING_OPERATOR, UNSUPPORTED_ACTION, missing command_id, and one unparseable line.
S8 faulted truck           If a truck is in FAULT: HOLD (expect INTERLOCK_ACTIVE). Nothing else.
S9 frozen truck            Wait up to 240 s for a truck reporting speed > 0.5 with an unchanged position for 8 s; if found outside BAY, EXIT_ZONE it and record what telemetry and acks say for 40 s; RESUME.

# Blast engine rules

**Draft for review. Nothing is built on this until it has been reviewed and edited.**

What the blast engine decides, on what evidence, and what it leaves to people. It implements
`CLAUDE.md` invariants 5 and 6, and is tested by `TESTING.md` L4 and L5. Rule ids (B1…) are what the
audit log records against every system action.

## What it does and doesn't do

- **Does:** for every zone that is `CLOSING` or `CLOSED`, decide per truck whether to do nothing, hold it
  before it enters, get it out, or alarm; recommend CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE; resume the trucks it
  held once the zone reopens.
- **Doesn't:** tell the shot firer (the operator does, by radio: answer 1); clear faults; move a truck
  someone is driving; manage spacing between trucks (answer 3).

## Inputs and timing

- Belief comes from `FleetState`: each truck's confidence (live, old, silent, contradicted, unknown) and
  its reachable range. Never from the fake's truth.
- **Time left** = `effective_at_ms` − estimated server now. Recomputed on every evaluation, so a link drop
  shrinks it (CONTEXT assumption 17).
- **Evaluate** on every snapshot change, and at once on `CLOSING`, on `hello` after a reconnect, and when
  a command's confirmation deadline passes.
- **Time to clear** = remaining queued work (LOADING ~20 s, DUMPING ~12 s, from the truck's own
  history) + up to 6 s for the command to take effect + distance to the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` will pick
  ÷ speed for its load state + margin. Loaded reverse speed: measured by the re-probe, or 2.0 m/s
  assumed, with the 1.5 m/s pessimistic version tested.

## Per truck, per closing zone

**B1. Unsure trucks are held, never sent out.** If the truck is silent, contradicted or unknown and its
range overlaps the zone or reaches it before it reopens: `HOLD`, and the zone is UNSURE. Not
`EXIT_ZONE`: it leaves the zone the truck is in *when accepted*, so if the truck is really just outside,
it could drive it *into* the closing zone. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9).

**B2. Inside, confident, will leave on its own in time.** If the truck is driving forward, has no duty
stop (load, dump, charge) before the far boundary, and reaches it with the margin to spare: no command.
Watch it; if it is late against its own estimate, apply B3. (Lena: don't stop trucks that don't need
stopping.)

**B3. Inside, confident, can be got out in time.** `EXIT_ZONE`, unless B4 applies. Confirm the effect in
telemetry (the truck's `task` and direction) by the state-aware deadline; retry under a new id; alarm
if it still fails.

**B4. Never send a truck into another closing or closed zone.** If the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` would pick
puts the truck in another zone that is not `OPEN` and that it cannot also clear in time: `HOLD` instead,
raise the can't-clear alarm, and offer remote driving out the other way (L2.52).

**B5. Inside but cannot be got out in time:** too far, interlocked (fault, e-stop, depleted battery),
or under someone's lease. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9) within 10 s. Still send `EXIT_ZONE` if it can
move at all and B4 allows: a truck that gets out late lets the shot go late rather than not at all.
A leased truck is never commanded; its lease holder gets the alarm with the countdown.

**B6. Outside, approaching: hold before entry.** A truck whose path would cross into the zone before it
reopens, and which cannot pass all the way through before `effective_at` with the margin, is held at a
hold point before the boundary. The `HOLD` goes out when the truck is (6 s + telemetry age + latency
allowance) × speed + margin from the boundary, not at `CLOSING`: a truck far away may never need
stopping. A truck that *can* pass through in time is let through. Once `CLOSED`, every approaching truck
is held.

**B7. Stopping an `EXIT_ZONE` in progress takes `HOLD`, not `RESUME`.** `RESUME` is rejected while a
task is running (`research/README.md`, S9).

**B8. Several zones at once.** A truck is judged against every zone that is not `OPEN`; its exit path
must end in an `OPEN` zone (B4); a truck that one zone's rules would move and another's would hold is
held.

**B9. The can't-clear alarm.** Within 10 s of `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing the conclusion,
whichever is later. It names the action ("Radio the shot firer to hold the shot"), the truck, the zone
and the reason in words. It interrupts (L2.60). It clears itself only when the truck is confirmed
outside, the zone reopens, or the blast is cancelled; never because time passed.

**B10. BAY closing.** `EXIT_ZONE` is refused in BAY, so every truck in BAY gets the can't-clear alarm at
once with "drive it out or hold the shot"; trucks approaching BAY are held before entry (B6).

## The clearance recommendation

**B11.** Per zone that is not `OPEN`, from belief only (invariant 6):
- **NOT CLEAR** if a live or old truck is inside.
- **UNSURE** if no live or old truck is inside, but a silent, contradicted or unknown truck's range
  overlaps it, or the site link is down.
- **CLEAR** only if no truck might be inside and the link is up.

NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both carry "Radio the shot firer to hold the shot" and their reasons. The operator
may record "I've confirmed it's clear" over either, only with a reason; recommendation and override are
both logged.

## When a zone reopens

**B12. Auto-resume** (answer 2), on `CLEARED` or `CANCELLED`: within 15 s, `RESUME` every truck the
system held **for that zone**, confirmed in telemetry, unless it is now held for another zone (B8), has a
lease or a fault, or was also held by an operator. Never resumes into a zone that is not `OPEN` (L4.R5).
An operator's hold is never resumed (L4.R4).

## Link and service

**B13. Link down.** Nothing can be sent. Every zone that is not `OPEN` becomes UNSURE; "link down while
a zone is closing" interrupts. On reconnect, act on the `hello` snapshot at once against the time left.
Commands in flight are replayed by the registry.

**B14. Service restart.** The engine's holds and their reasons are persisted with the command log, so a
restart mid-blast knows which trucks it held and for which zone (L6.1).

## Every decision is logged

**B15.** Each system action is logged as the system, with the rule id, the zone, the truck's belief
(confidence, range, time left, time to clear) and the command's outcome, in the same log as the
operators' (answer 4).

## Open for review

1. **B2 (let confident trucks leave on their own).** Fewer commands and fewer unnecessary stops, but
   one more prediction that can be wrong. The alternative is `EXIT_ZONE` for every truck inside.
2. **B5 (keep evacuating a truck that can't make it in time).** I think yes; it shortens the held shot.
3. **B6's margin.** The trigger distance is 6 s plus the truck's telemetry age at its speed. I'm unsure
   whether the stop itself is instant in the simulator. The re-probe's `HOLD` timings will show it.
4. **Queuing.** B3's deadline and B4's command order depend on whether a queued command is replaced by
   a newer one and whether `RESUME` cancels a queue. The re-probe answers both; this draft assumes the
   spec.
5. **B1 for a frozen truck that is really outside.** Holding it costs production until its data
   recovers; the alternative is an operator check. Holding is the safe default.

# Blast engine rules

**Draft for review. Nothing is built on this until it has been reviewed and edited.**

What the blast engine decides, on what evidence, and what it leaves to people. It implements
`CLAUDE.md` invariants 5 and 6, and is tested by `TESTING.md` L4 and L5. Rule ids (B1…) are what the
audit log records against every system action.

## What it does and doesn't do

- **Does:** for every zone that is `CLOSING` or `CLOSED`, decide per truck whether to do nothing, hold it
  before it enters, get it out, or alarm; recommend CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE; resume the trucks it
  held once the zone reopens.
- **Doesn't:** tell the shot firer (the operator does, by radio: answer 1); clear faults; move a truck
  someone is driving; manage spacing between trucks (answer 3).

## Inputs and timing

- Belief comes from `FleetState`: each truck's confidence (live, old, silent, contradicted, unknown) and
  its reachable range. Never from the fake's truth.
- **Time left** = `effective_at_ms` − estimated server now. Recomputed on every evaluation, so a link drop
  shrinks it (CONTEXT assumption 17).
- **Evaluate** on every snapshot change, and at once on `CLOSING`, on `hello` after a reconnect, and when
  a command's confirmation deadline passes.
- **Time to clear** = remaining queued work (LOADING ~20 s, DUMPING ~12 s, from the truck's own
  history) + up to 6 s for the command to take effect + distance to the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` will pick
  ÷ speed for its load state + margin. Loaded reverse speed: measured by the re-probe, or 2.0 m/s
  assumed, with the 1.5 m/s pessimistic version tested.

## Per truck, per closing zone

**B1. Unsure trucks are held, never sent out.** If the truck is silent, contradicted or unknown and its
range overlaps the zone or reaches it before it reopens: `HOLD`, and the zone is UNSURE. Not
`EXIT_ZONE`: it leaves the zone the truck is in *when accepted*, so if the truck is really just outside,
it could drive it *into* the closing zone. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9).

**B2. Inside, confident, will leave on its own in time.** If the truck is driving forward, has no duty
stop (load, dump, charge) before the far boundary, and reaches it with the margin to spare: no command.
Watch it; if it is late against its own estimate, apply B3. (Lena: don't stop trucks that don't need
stopping.)

**B3. Inside, confident, can be got out in time.** `EXIT_ZONE`, unless B4 applies. Confirm the effect in
telemetry (the truck's `task` and direction) by the state-aware deadline; retry under a new id; alarm
if it still fails.

**B4. Never send a truck into another closing or closed zone.** If the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` would pick
puts the truck in another zone that is not `OPEN` and that it cannot also clear in time: `HOLD` instead,
raise the can't-clear alarm, and offer remote driving out the other way (L2.52).

**B5. Inside but cannot be got out in time:** too far, interlocked (fault, e-stop, depleted battery),
or under someone's lease. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9) within 10 s. Still send `EXIT_ZONE` if it can
move at all and B4 allows: a truck that gets out late lets the shot go late rather than not at all.
A leased truck is never commanded; its lease holder gets the alarm with the countdown.

**B6. Outside, approaching: hold before entry.** A truck whose path would cross into the zone before it
reopens, and which cannot pass all the way through before `effective_at` with the margin, is held at a
hold point before the boundary. The `HOLD` goes out when the truck is (6 s + telemetry age + latency
allowance) × speed + margin from the boundary, not at `CLOSING`: a truck far away may never need
stopping. A truck that *can* pass through in time is let through. Once `CLOSED`, every approaching truck
is held.

**B7. Stopping an `EXIT_ZONE` in progress takes `HOLD`, not `RESUME`.** `RESUME` is rejected while a
task is running (`research/README.md`, S9).

**B8. Several zones at once.** A truck is judged against every zone that is not `OPEN`; its exit path
must end in an `OPEN` zone (B4); a truck that one zone's rules would move and another's would hold is
held.

**B9. The can't-clear alarm.** Within 10 s of `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing the conclusion,
whichever is later. It names the action ("Radio the shot firer to hold the shot"), the truck, the zone
and the reason in words. It interrupts (L2.60). It clears itself only when the truck is confirmed
outside, the zone reopens, or the blast is cancelled; never because time passed.

**B10. BAY closing.** `EXIT_ZONE` is refused in BAY, so every truck in BAY gets the can't-clear alarm at
once with "drive it out or hold the shot"; trucks approaching BAY are held before entry (B6).

## The clearance recommendation

**B11.** Per zone that is not `OPEN`, from belief only (invariant 6):
- **NOT CLEAR** if a live or old truck is inside.
- **UNSURE** if no live or old truck is inside, but a silent, contradicted or unknown truck's range
  overlaps it, or the site link is down.
- **CLEAR** only if no truck might be inside and the link is up.

NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both carry "Radio the shot firer to hold the shot" and their reasons. The operator
may record "I've confirmed it's clear" over either, only with a reason; recommendation and override are
both logged.

## When a zone reopens

**B12. Auto-resume** (answer 2), on `CLEARED` or `CANCELLED`: within 15 s, `RESUME` every truck the
system held **for that zone**, confirmed in telemetry, unless it is now held for another zone (B8), has a

**B13. Link down.** Nothing can be sent. Every zone that is not `OPEN` becomes UNSURE; "link down while
a zone is closing" interrupts. On reconnect, act on the `hello` snapshot at once against the time left.
Commands in flight are replayed by the registry.

restart mid-blast knows which trucks it held and for which zone (L6.1).

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

input.content:
# Tasks 3 and 4: the gateway link and the command registry

**Goal.** One connection to the site that recovers on its own and never lets anyone mistake an old
picture for a current one; and one place that sends every command, knows what actually happened to
it, and records it. Everything that commands a truck (operators, the blast engine, auto-resume) goes
through the registry. Nothing else talks to the gateway.

**Read first:** `CLAUDE.md` and everything it lists. In `research/README.md`, read "Verified, and
not" and "Re-probe, 2026-10-03" closely: they are why this task exists. `AI_LOG.md` entries 1 and 4
are about the one mistake this task must make impossible.

**Must pass:** `TESTING.md` L2.30–L2.39 (registry), L2.40–L2.44 (link), the link and command rows of
L5 that milestone 1 of the fake can produce (link drops by closing the connection; the rest when
milestone 2 merges), L6.1 (the replay half: in-flight commands survive a restart), L6.2, L6.6, L7.8
(e-stop while the link is down), L8.1–L8.5.

## Scope

**Gateway link** (`src/link.ts`)
- TLS to `GATEWAY_HOST:GATEWAY_PORT`, auth with `GATEWAY_EMAIL`; credentials from the environment only.
- Reconnect with capped, jittered backoff; a login accepted then closed before `hello` is an outage.
- Link down after `PARAMS.linkDownAfter` without a heartbeat; link status is part of what the UI shows.
- On `hello`: hand the snapshot to `FleetState` (zones, leases, vehicles) and replay in-flight commands.
- Feed every line to `FleetState.ingestLine`; keep up with 12 trucks at 5 Hz plus bursts, never 4 MB
  behind (L6.2: measure it).
- One connection per service, whatever the number of browsers (L6.4 later relies on this).

**Command registry** (`src/registry.ts`)
- **Ack matching lives here and only here:** an ack belongs to the latest send of its `command_id`,
  matched by time, never by counting acks (L2.33). Export it for every tool that reads acks.
- Lifecycle: pending → sent → acknowledged (or no ack) → effect seen in telemetry, or failed with a
  reason in the operator's words (L2.39).
- **`ACCEPTED` is not done.** Each action has an effect predicate on `FleetState` (HOLD: `HOLDING`;
  RESUME: moving or back in its duty cycle; EXIT_ZONE: `task` set, then holding outside the zone;
  RETURN_TO_BAY: `task` set; ESTOP: `ESTOPPED`; and so on) and a deadline.
- **Deadlines depend on state** (L2.36): ~6 s normally; behind LOADING or DUMPING, the remaining work
  plus 6 s; behind CHARGING, no fixed deadline. The re-probe showed a queued `HOLD` can be
  `ACCEPTED` and never carried out, so a queued command is checked the moment the work ends and
  retried at once if it hasn't taken effect.
- **Retry** under a new `command_id` when the deadline passes, up to a set number of attempts, with
  the attempt count visible; then fail and alarm (L2.37). Never retry `COMMAND_ID_REUSED` (L2.34). A
  retry never displaces a different command we queued on that truck (L2.38).
- **A command on its way can't be called back:** `RESUME` within another command's 1–6 s delay is
  rejected (re-probe Q3). The registry doesn't pretend otherwise.
- **The safety check sits below every caller:** before sending, the registry asks a `SafetyGate`
  (an interface; the blast engine implements it later) whether the command is allowed, and records
  the refusal and its reason if not. Ship an allow-all gate for now, clearly named as such, with the
  interface tested.
- **Persist before sending** (L6.6), in SQLite through `node:sqlite`: every command, its sends, acks,
  effect and outcome; an append-only audit log in which system and operator actions sit together, each
  with who (an operator id or "system" plus the rule), what, when and why (L8.4, L8.5). On restart,
  commands still in flight are replayed; ones older than their deadline are marked expired, not sent.
- **E-stop while the link is down** (L7.8): pending and visible with a cancel; sent automatically only
  if the link returns within 10 s; after that it needs the operator to confirm again.
- **Leases:** `TAKE_CONTROL` / `RELEASE_CONTROL` and the lease ids from acks; a command blocked by
  `LEASE_HELD` is reported to the lease holder as well as the sender (L8.1); forced takeover only for a
  supervisor (L8.2). The registry takes the operator's identity from its caller, which will be the
  server's session; it never reads one from a browser payload (L8.3).
- Drive messages are not commands; the drive relay is a later task. Leave room for it.

## Ways to be wrong that matter

- Matching acks by counting. Three pieces of code did this in one day (`AI_LOG.md` entry 4).
- Treating `ACCEPTED` as done, or a queued command as safe.
- Sending a command before it is written down.
- A retry storm: a truck that can't comply (interlocked, leased) must fail with the reason, not be
  retried forever.
- Reading the wall clock: everything takes the injected `Clock`, including backoff and deadlines.

## Working rules

Tests first, against the fake gateway's in-process API and its TLS server; never the real gateway.
Replay `research/fixtures/` where they cover a case (`accepted-then-ignored-resume`,
`queued-hold-dropped`, `resume-during-pending-hold`, `link-drop-in-notice`). Commit as you go on your
branch, one logical change per commit, adding paths explicitly (never `git add .`/`-A`). Before
starting, make sure your branch is based on local `main`, not a stale `origin/main`. Don't push and
don't merge; I review, merge and push. Finish with: what passes, what doesn't, the registry's public
interface, every deadline, retry count and backoff you chose and why, and the L6.2 measurement.

Everything you asked for is done or running, and main is pushed (`67a22a7`).

## The queuing re-probe

It ran live on 2026-10-03 from 10:39:53 to 10:46:02 EDT, under `operator_id: "probe"`. I first ran it against the fake gateway to test the probe itself. Every truck it touched was confirmed moving again in telemetry. The times and results are in research/README.md, with three new fixtures.

| Step | Live result |
|---|---|
| Q1 `HOLD` queued behind loading | **`ACCEPTED`, then never carried out.** When loading ended, the truck drove straight into L4_SOUTH. One sample, so it may be the accepted-then-ignored fault landing on a queued command |
| Q2 does a newer queued command replace an older one? | **Didn't run.** L4_SOUTH was closed for the whole 180 s window |
| Q3 does `RESUME` cancel a queued command? | **Didn't test the queue:** loading ended before the `RESUME` arrived. It showed something else: a `RESUME` sent during another command's 1–6 s delay is rejected, and that command still takes effect. A command on its way can't be recalled |
| R1 loaded reverse speed | **2.0 m/s, measured thinly:** 1.99 m/s over 2.4 m, then the truck went silent for 41 s. I first read the probe's "2.4 m in 1.2 s" as the whole reverse; the raw log showed the gap |

`params.ts`, its test, and CONTEXT assumptions 6 and 15 now say what was measured and how thinly.

## Your other points

- **Pushed** after every change since you asked. Before the first push I scanned the whole history: no email, `.env`, `._` files or keys. Large pushes need `http.postBuffer`, which I pass per command rather than putting in your config.
- **Your git identity: 42 of the 43 commits are authored as `<redacted-email>`**, a placeholder in your local git config. I haven't touched it. If you want your real address on them, the history needs rewriting before submission.
- **AI_SESSIONS.md has rows for both sub-agents.** Their transcripts are exported in `ai-sessions/` as scrubbed JSONL plus readable Markdown. `tools/export_session.py` drops every email field, replaces every email address, and refuses to finish if one survives. I checked both exports myself.
- **Three agents are running, from committed briefs:**
  - Fake-gateway milestone 2. I've sent it the re-probe results, and it will add "queued command dropped" as a fault the fake can inject.
  - The UI fixture player and Overview, with screenshots as it goes.
  - The registry and gateway link, which carries the re-probe's lessons: queued commands are checked when the work ends and retried at once, and ack matching lives only in the registry.
- **Both first agents were stopped by the account's session limit** within minutes, before writing anything. I relaunched them fresh and cleaned up the empty branches they'd left.

## The blast rules draft: `BLAST.md`, uncommitted, for your edit

It defines rules B1–B15, each with an id that the audit log records against system actions. The decisions most worth your attention:

- **B1: an unsure truck is held, never sent out.** `EXIT_ZONE` leaves whatever zone the truck is *actually* in, so a frozen truck that's really just outside could be driven *into* the closing zone.
- **B2: a confident truck that will leave on its own in time gets no command.**
- **B4: never send a truck into another zone that isn't open;** hold it and alarm instead.
- **B6: hold before entry, timed for when it's needed,** not at `CLOSING`.
- **B6a, new from the re-probe:** the end of the draw point is L4_SOUTH's boundary. I propose the system take the truck with `TAKE_CONTROL` there. It's immediate, and the truck then ends up `HOLDING`.
- **B7: never rely on cancelling a sent command.**
- **B11:** the CLEAR / NOT CLEAR / UNSURE rule.
- **B12:** auto-resume.

Six open points at the end need your decision. The biggest is **B6a**: it would be the one place the system takes manual control of a truck. I lean towards it, but it interrupts loading and shows "system" as a lease holder to operators.

content.text:
I've reviewed, merged and pushed the UI work (`973631c`). Fake-gateway milestone 2 and the registry are still running.

**What's on main:**
- **The fixture player:** `npm run player -- --fixture frozen-truck --port 8091`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8091/. It listens on localhost only, and a test checks it contains no network client.
- **The Overview screen:** track diagram, clearance panel, fleet table sorted by attention, and the always-on bar.
- **Thirteen screenshots in `docs/screenshots/`**, with an index. I looked at them myself: the frozen truck drawn as a hatched range across the loop's end, the link drop greying the picture under a banner, and all four data states at once in the weak-pack recording.
- **Tests, all passing in my own runs:** 162 of 163 in `npm test`, both slow tests, and all six real-browser tests (`npm run test:browser`, using the local Chrome through `playwright-core`; no browser download).

**What I changed in review:** a battery flag said **"can't reach the bay"** while the reason beside it said **"may not"**. The warning fires on a 1.25× safety reserve, so the truck may well make it, and a flag that overstates its evidence is how operators stop trusting a screen. It now says "may not reach the bay", and the screenshot is retaken; the other twelve came out identical. The merge message cites that fix by a placeholder ("b8f") instead of its real hash, `682b178`. It's pushed, and I'm leaving it rather than force-pushing.

**Gaps the agent reported, with my view:**
- **No screenshot shows CLEAR or NOT CLEAR.** The two closing-zone fixtures carry no truck telemetry, so every truck is "never reported" and every verdict is UNSURE. Both verdicts are tested in Node and in the browser. The live soak, or a fake-gateway recording once milestone 2 lands, will provide real screenshots.
- **"Never reported" rows clutter the fixture views:** most fixtures carry only 1–3 of the 12 trucks. That's true to the data, and on the live site every truck reports within seconds. I'd leave it.
- **Rows can flicker in order.** With the thinned weak-pack data, trucks flip between old and live, so the attention-sorted table reorders every few seconds. I'd add hysteresis when the UI task resumes.

**Two design questions for you, from building it:**
1. **When the link drops, should the clearance panel stay in colour?** UI.md says everything greys. That greys UNSURE's amber too, leaving its word, glyph, stripes and dashed edge to carry it. I'd exempt the clearance panel: it's the one thing Priya must read in two seconds.
2. **Where does a "controller restarted" note go?** It has no place on the Overview yet. I'd put it in the attention tray as a silent item, which arrives with the registry work.

**Still waiting on you:** your review and edits of `BLAST.md`, uncommitted, especially open point 6 (B6a: should the system take manual control to stop a truck leaving the draw point into a closing zone?).

The test now prints the link's status whenever lines go unprocessed.
  
  ### Public interfaces
  - **Registry (`src/registry.ts`):**
    - `new CommandRegistry({clock, fleet, store, transport, gate, newId?, commandIdFor?, systemOperatorId?='system', keepClosed?})`
    - Commands: `submit(req: {vehicleId, action, force?, leaseId?, why?}, actor)`, `cancel(id, actor)`, `reconfirm(id, actor)`
    - Reads: `get(id)`, `list({open?, vehicleId?})`, `lease(v)`, `leases()`
    - From the link: `linkUp(hello)`, `linkDown(reason)`, `message(msg)`
    - Running: `tick()`, `start()`, `stop()`, `subscribe(fn)`
    - Events: `command`, `notify` (with recipients), `alarm` (`command_failed` or `estop_undelivered`), `lease`.

    - Statuses: pending → sent → acknowledged → confirmed, or failed / refused / expired / cancelled / superseded. Each record has an operator-facing `summary` and an attempt count.
  - **Ack matching:** exported as `matchAck(sends, rxMs)` and `AckBook`; the registry uses them itself. An ack belongs to the latest send at or before the moment it is received, never the nth ack to the nth send.
  - **Safety gate:** `SafetyGate.check({record, attempt, replay, truck})` returns `{allow}` or `{allow:false, code, reason}`. It is asked before every send, including retries and replays. The shipped gate is `ALLOW_ALL_GATE_NO_BLAST_SAFETY`.
  - **Store (`src/store.ts`, `node:sqlite`):** tables `commands`, `sends`, `acks` and `audit`. Triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE on `sends`, `acks` and `audit`. Methods: `history(vehicleId, fromServerMs, toServerMs)` (L8.4), `auditLog(vehicleId?)`, `openCommands()`. Writes are synchronous and wrapped in a transaction; each send row is written before the line is handed to the link.
  - **Link (`src/link.ts`):**
    - `new GatewayLink({clock, fleet, dial, email, random?})` with `start()`, `stop()`, `status()`, `isUp()`, `send(cmd)`, `sendDrive(drive)` and `subscribe(fn)`.
    - Events: `status`, `up` (carries hello), `down`, `message`, `alarm`.
    - Helpers: `tlsDialer({host, port, ca?})`, `linkConfigFromEnv(env)` (its errors name missing variables but never echo a value), and `attachRegistry(link, registry)` to wire the two together.

  - **FleetState additions:** `setLink(up, reason)` (while the link is down, nothing is shown as live), `truck(id)`, `TruckView.stateSinceServerMs`, and `snapshot().link`.
  
  ### Deadlines, retries and backoff, and why
  | Setting | Value | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | Supervisory deadline | 8.0 s from send | 6 s spec delay + 1.5 s telemetry latency + 0.5 s uplink. Not 6 s, because a working command's effect can arrive up to 7.5 s after the send; 6 s would retry commands that are fine. |
  | Uplink allowance | 0.5 s | All 11 fixture acks were stamped 43–58 ms after the probe's send (probe and gateway clocks differ). Acks arrived 0.31–2.58 s after the send. |
  | ESTOP and lease commands | 3 s | They take effect on receipt. |
  | Behind LOADING or DUMPING | Work left + 8 s | Work left is computed from when the state began. |
  | Behind CHARGING | No deadline | Shows an estimate at 0.1 %/s (a guess; no charging was ever captured). |
  | Queued command when the work ends | Checked on the first telemetry after it ends, retried at once if not in effect | As the brief asks. |
  | Attempts | 3 normally, 5 for ESTOP | Each retry has a new command_id. |
  | EXIT_ZONE completion | 2 × distance ÷ 2.0 m/s + 7.5 s | Loaded reverse speed is only thinly measured. |
  | E-stop / commands while the link is down | Auto-send within 10 s; after that the operator must confirm again (system commands expire) | |
  | Reconnect backoff | 0.5 s doubling to a 5 s cap; jitter between half and all of each step | A 21–49 s outage costs at most 5 s more of a 120 s blast notice, and a retry is never instant. |
  | TOO_MANY_CONNECTIONS / SERVER_FULL | 5 s doubling to 30 s | The gateway is loaded. |
  | Other auth errors | Stop and alarm | Retrying won't fix them. |
  | Hello timeout | 5 s | |
  | Link down | No heartbeat for 5 s; drops and redials | |
  
  Every value is in `PARAMS` with its source noted.
  
  Rules the registry also enforces:
  - A refusal from the site is never retried.
  - A retry refused with INVALID_STATE waits about 2 s to see if an earlier attempt worked before failing.
  - EXIT_ZONE is never re-sent once under way, and is only retried if live data still puts the truck in the target zone.
  - A newer command on a truck supersedes the older one, so a retry can never displace a different queued command (L2.38). A RESUME supersedes only once it is accepted, and only commands that are queued.
  - A RESUME sent while the truck is already moving confirms only on an ACCEPTED ack. Otherwise a RESUME refused during a HOLD's delay would look done.

  - **In-process cost:** 60,000 lines shaped from the weak-pack fixture went through link → fleet → registry, with 3 commands open. Every line was applied and the link never redialled. content.text: An AI_LOG entry for this one. A fixture I trimmed hid the evidence, an agent built a fault model on the gap, and I had misread the same data myself:

input.command:
cat >> AI_LOG.md <<'EOF'

---

## 5. A fixture that left out the evidence, read wrong twice

**Session:** planning session; fake gateway milestone 2 run as a sub-agent, 2026-10-03.

**Asked.** Milestone 2 of the fake gateway (`tasks/01b-fake-gateway-m2.md`): fault injectors that
reproduce the live fixtures, checked by running `research/report.py` over both (L0.C1).

**Came back.** All tests passing, and a report that the research disagreed with the fake in three
places. One: the re-probe's R1 fixture "is more than a silent truck": no heartbeats for 26 s while the
connection stayed open. The agent built a "link stall" injector to reproduce it.

**What was wrong.** Both readings of R1. I had written it up as the truck going silent for 41 s. The
agent read it as a stalled link. The raw log has HT-04 quiet for ~15 s while the link was up, then
the gateway closing the connection and refusing logins for ~25 s. The fixture I cut had kept HT-04's
messages and the heartbeats but not the connection events, so the drop was invisible in it. My
trimming decided what both of us could see. The agent's two other claims were right: my loss figures
for runs 2 and 3 were too low, because I measured outages between heartbeats, which overshoot; and my
`report.py` crashed on the weak-pack fixture.

**How it was found.** By going back to the full re-probe log, not the fixture: link events,
heartbeats and every truck's telemetry across the gap.

**What was done.** The fixture now includes link events; the conformance test models a link drop that
ends before the fifth reconnect, as live; the stall injector stays, marked as not seen live; the loss
figures and `report.py` are fixed (`4531e4c`, `e007d97`). A fixture is a claim about what matters in a
recording. Cutting it narrowly hides the context that would show the claim is wrong.
EOF

Everything that was running is now reviewed, merged and pushed to origin/main (`09b70ac`). No agents are running. `BLAST.md` is the only thing still uncommitted, waiting for you.

## Merged

**Fake gateway, milestone 2.**
- Every fault class can be injected, and each injection is recorded with the truck and time, so the blast tests can tell a correct alarm from a false one.
- A "live day" puts one fault on each of eight trucks, as the real site does.
- The fake matches the measured radio statistics, and can serve other sites.
- Probe conformance now includes live ack latency and S1's lost ack.
- With the captures supplied, all its tests pass.

**Gateway link and command registry.**
- **One connection** to the site, with backoff and a heartbeat watchdog. In-flight commands are replayed after a reconnect.
- **One place that sends commands:** every command is written to SQLite before it's sent, checked against telemetry by a deadline, and retried under a new id.
- **Ack matching lives only in the registry**, matched by time, so the mistake in AI_LOG entries 1 and 4 can't recur.
- **The audit log is append-only**, enforced by the database.
- **The safety gate is checked before every send**, retries included. It's currently a pass-through named `ALLOW_ALL_GATE_NO_BLAST_SAFETY` until the blast engine replaces it.

I spot-checked that the operator id sent to the gateway comes only from the server side. On the combined tree, 278 of 280 fast tests pass (the 2 skips need the live captures), plus 6 of 6 browser tests and the slow suite twice. The one throughput stall the agent saw didn't recur.

## Corrections to my own research (AI_LOG entry 5)

I checked the milestone-2 agent's three claims against the raw logs:
- **R1 was misread by both of us.** The truck went quiet for about 15 s, then the link dropped for about 25 s, with logins refused. My fixture had left out the connection events, so I called it a silent truck and the agent called it a stalled link. The fixture now includes them, and the conformance test models the drop.
- **My loss figures were too low:** runs 2 and 3 lose 3.06% and 2.95%, not 2.68% and 2.51%. I had measured outages between heartbeats, which overshoots.
- **`report.py` crashed on the weak-pack fixture.** It's fixed, and it now reads fixture files directly.

## Sessions

AI_SESSIONS.md lists all seven sub-agent sessions, including two first attempts cut short by the account's session limit. All are exported, email-free. Embedded screenshot images are now replaced by a note of their size, which brought the UI transcript from 6.7 MB to 1.6 MB.

## What's next, and what needs you

- **`BLAST.md` blocks the blast engine.** Open point 6 (B6a) matters most: whether the system takes manual control to stop a truck at the draw point from entering a closing zone.
- **The registry made one choice you should know about.** System commands reach the gateway with `operator_id: "system"`; the rule that triggered them is recorded only in our own audit log. That fits answer 4, but the site's statutory log will show only "system".
- **While you review, I'd start the server task:** login with roles, the WebSocket to the browser, and wiring the UI to the live link. It's independent of the blast rules.
- **Deploying to dronehal1 needs you to say when.** Docker CE goes on a box that's already serving another project.

<pasted_content id="7017">
I checked out BLAST.md – good stuff!

Open points:
1. B2: yes, with a guard. Decide at the last safe moment — the latest point EXIT_ZONE can still get the truck out — and send EXIT_ZONE then if it isn't out. Not "if it's late".
2. B5: yes.
3. B6's margin: 6 s until the re-probe's HOLD timings say otherwise.
4. Never queue two different commands on one truck: agreed.
5. B1 for a frozen truck that's really outside: hold. The B11 override, with a reason, is the operator's way out.
6. B6a: approved. The alternative fails L4.R0 by design — a truck that could have been held but entered is exactly what R0 forbids. And the lease expires after 10 s, so "system" holds it only briefly. Better than ESTOP, which needs CLEAR_ESTOP and reads as an emergency.

Things the draft missed:
- B11 can say CLEAR when it isn't. It judges live and old trucks by position and only silent ones by range. Old runs from 2 to 5 s — about 15 m at 3 m/s — so an old truck reported just outside and heading in could be inside. CLEAR requires every truck's range to be outside, old trucks included. Add a test.
- B6a applies to all three duty stops, not just the draw point: PROTOCOL §3 puts loading, dumping and charging each at a segment's end, at a zone boundary (DRAW_12 into L4_SOUTH, TIP wrapping to BAY, BAY into DECLINE). Naming "the draw point" also breaks invariant 7. Rule: any duty stop at a boundary into a zone that isn't OPEN.
- B6's pass-through check ignores duty stops inside the zone: a truck passing through DRAW_12 stops there to load and leaves at loaded speed. Use B2's duty-stop logic.
- Commands to silent or contradicted trucks can't be confirmed in telemetry, so the registry would retry them to exhaustion and report a failure. Mark them unconfirmable: bounded retries, then "can't verify: data frozen", not "failed".
- B12 contradicts B7: at reopen a truck may still be carrying out its EXIT_ZONE, and RESUME is rejected then. HOLD first, then RESUME.
- Write down in BLAST.md, and later README §5: a silent truck's range grows to cover the loop within minutes, so every closing zone is UNSURE until its data returns. Correct, and it's a limit of enforcement.

operator_id: send "system:<rule id>" (e.g. system:B3), not bare "system". Answer 4 asked for what, when and why in the same log; this puts the why in the site's statutory log too.

Then: commit BLAST.md with these edits, and start the server task as you proposed. Deploying to dronehal1 waits for me — I'll pick the window, and I'll take a boot-volume backup first.

90	**What was done.** The checker now cuts outages out of each gap and judges the link-up pieces on their

106	
107	**Came back.** The agent reported that its own probe checker had been wrong: it paired acks with
108	sends inside a 50 ms window, and S1's resend and reuse go out 50 ms apart, so the resend's ack was
109	credited to the reuse. It found this in the raw file and fixed it. Then my review comparison flagged
110	two S1 mismatches between the live probe and the fake.
111	
112	**What was wrong.** My comparison, not the fake. It matched the nth ack of a `command_id` to its nth
113	send. Live, the first `HOLD`'s ack was lost, so everything after it shifted by one: exactly the
114	mistake in entry 1, made again by me in the review meant to catch such things. Read correctly,
115	the fake matches the live probe on every command of S1 and S3–S8 except the lost ack, which the
116	fake does not inject until milestone 2.
117	
118	**How it was found.** The two "mismatches" were both on the one id with a lost ack; reading the raw
119	send and ack lines for that id showed the shift.
120	
121	**What was done.** Recorded the corrected result in the merge commit (`54b6d26`). The lesson is that
122	remembering doesn't work: three pieces of code by two authors made the same mistake within a day. Ack
123	correlation (by time, against the latest send) belongs in one tested place, the command registry
124	(`TESTING.md` L2.33), and every later tool that reads acks uses it rather than rewriting it.
125

133	reproduce the live fixtures, checked by running `research/report.py` over both (L0.C1).
134	
135	**Came back.** All tests passing, and a report that the research disagreed with the fake in three
136	places. One: the re-probe's R1 fixture "is more than a silent truck": no heartbeats for 26 s while the
137	connection stayed open. The agent built a "link stall" injector to reproduce it.
138	
139	**What was wrong.** Both readings of R1. I had written it up as the truck going silent for 41 s. The
140	agent read it as a stalled link. The raw log has HT-04 quiet for ~15 s while the link was up, then
141	the gateway closing the connection and refusing logins for ~25 s. The fixture I cut had kept HT-04's
142	messages and the heartbeats but not the connection events, so the drop was invisible in it. My
143	trimming decided what both of us could see. The agent's two other claims were right: my loss figures
144	for runs 2 and 3 were too low, because I measured outages between heartbeats, which overshoot; and my
145	`report.py` crashed on the weak-pack fixture.
146	
147	**How it was found.** By going back to the full re-probe log, not the fixture: link events,
148	heartbeats and every truck's telemetry across the gap.
149	
150	**What was done.** The fixture now includes link events; the conformance test models a link drop that
151	ends before the fifth reconnect, as live; the stall injector stays, marked as not seen live; the loss
152	figures and `report.py` are fixed (`4531e4c`, `e007d97`). A fixture is a claim about what matters in a
153	recording. Cutting it narrowly hides the context that would show the claim is wrong.

content.content:
1	# Blast engine rules
2	
3	**Draft for review. Nothing is built on this until it has been reviewed and edited.**
4	
5	What the blast engine decides, on what evidence, and what it leaves to people. It implements
6	`CLAUDE.md` invariants 5 and 6, and is tested by `TESTING.md` L4 and L5. Rule ids (B1…) are what the
7	audit log records against every system action.
8	
9	## What it does and doesn't do
10	
11	- **Does:** for every zone that is `CLOSING` or `CLOSED`, decide per truck whether to do nothing, hold it
12	  before it enters, get it out, or alarm; recommend CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE; resume the trucks it
13	  held once the zone reopens.
14	- **Doesn't:** tell the shot firer (the operator does, by radio: answer 1); clear faults; move a truck
15	  someone is driving; manage spacing between trucks (answer 3).
16	
17	## Inputs and timing
18	
19	- Belief comes from `FleetState`: each truck's confidence (live, old, silent, contradicted, unknown) and
20	  its reachable range. Never from the fake's truth.
21	- **Time left** = `effective_at_ms` − estimated server now. Recomputed on every evaluation, so a link drop
22	  shrinks it (CONTEXT assumption 17).
23	- **Evaluate** on every snapshot change, and at once on `CLOSING`, on `hello` after a reconnect, and when
24	  a command's confirmation deadline passes.
25	- **Time to clear** = remaining queued work (LOADING ~20 s, DUMPING ~12 s, from the truck's own
26	  history) + up to 6 s for the command to take effect + distance to the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` will pick
27	  ÷ speed for its load state + margin. Loaded reverse: 2.0 m/s, measured thinly by the re-probe; the
28	  1.5 m/s pessimistic version is tested too.
29	- **Queued commands are unreliable** (re-probe Q1: a `HOLD` queued behind loading was `ACCEPTED` and
30	  never carried out). Any command sent to a LOADING, DUMPING or CHARGING truck is checked the moment
31	  the work ends and retried at once.
32	
33	## Per truck, per closing zone
34	
35	**B1. Unsure trucks are held, never sent out.** If the truck is silent, contradicted or unknown and its
36	range overlaps the zone or reaches it before it reopens: `HOLD`, and the zone is UNSURE. Not
37	`EXIT_ZONE`: it leaves the zone the truck is in *when accepted*, so if the truck is really just outside,
38	it could drive it *into* the closing zone. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9).
39	
40	**B2. Inside, confident, will leave on its own in time.** If the truck is driving forward, has no duty
41	stop (load, dump, charge) before the far boundary, and reaches it with the margin to spare: no command.
42	Watch it; if it is late against its own estimate, apply B3. (Lena: don't stop trucks that don't need
43	stopping.)
44	
45	**B3. Inside, confident, can be got out in time.** `EXIT_ZONE`, unless B4 applies. Confirm the effect in
46	telemetry (the truck's `task` and direction) by the state-aware deadline; retry under a new id; alarm
47	if it still fails.
48	
49	**B4. Never send a truck into another closing or closed zone.** If the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` would pick
50	puts the truck in another zone that is not `OPEN` and that it cannot also clear in time: `HOLD` instead,
51	raise the can't-clear alarm, and offer remote driving out the other way (L2.52).
52	
53	**B5. Inside but cannot be got out in time:** too far, interlocked (fault, e-stop, depleted battery),
54	or under someone's lease. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9) within 10 s. Still send `EXIT_ZONE` if it can
55	move at all and B4 allows: a truck that gets out late lets the shot go late rather than not at all.

# Blast engine rules

**Draft for review. Nothing is built on this until it has been reviewed and edited.**

What the blast engine decides, on what evidence, and what it leaves to people. It implements
`CLAUDE.md` invariants 5 and 6, and is tested by `TESTING.md` L4 and L5. Rule ids (B1…) are what the
audit log records against every system action.

## What it does and doesn't do

- **Does:** for every zone that is `CLOSING` or `CLOSED`, decide per truck whether to do nothing, hold it
  before it enters, get it out, or alarm; recommend CLEAR, NOT CLEAR or UNSURE; resume the trucks it
  held once the zone reopens.
- **Doesn't:** tell the shot firer (the operator does, by radio: answer 1); clear faults; move a truck
  someone is driving; manage spacing between trucks (answer 3).

## Inputs and timing

- Belief comes from `FleetState`: each truck's confidence (live, old, silent, contradicted, unknown) and
  its reachable range. Never from the fake's truth.
- **Time left** = `effective_at_ms` − estimated server now. Recomputed on every evaluation, so a link drop
  shrinks it (CONTEXT assumption 17).
- **Evaluate** on every snapshot change, and at once on `CLOSING`, on `hello` after a reconnect, and when
  a command's confirmation deadline passes.
- **Time to clear** = remaining queued work (LOADING ~20 s, DUMPING ~12 s, from the truck's own
  history) + up to 6 s for the command to take effect + distance to the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` will pick
  ÷ speed for its load state + margin. Loaded reverse: 2.0 m/s, measured thinly by the re-probe; the
  1.5 m/s pessimistic version is tested too.
- **Queued commands are unreliable** (re-probe Q1: a `HOLD` queued behind loading was `ACCEPTED` and
  never carried out). Any command sent to a LOADING, DUMPING or CHARGING truck is checked the moment
  the work ends and retried at once.

## Per truck, per closing zone

**B1. Unsure trucks are held, never sent out.** If the truck is silent, contradicted or unknown and its
range overlaps the zone or reaches it before it reopens: `HOLD`, and the zone is UNSURE. Not
`EXIT_ZONE`: it leaves the zone the truck is in *when accepted*, so if the truck is really just outside,
it could drive it *into* the closing zone. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9).

**B2. Inside, confident, will leave on its own in time.** If the truck is driving forward, has no duty
stop (load, dump, charge) before the far boundary, and reaches it with the margin to spare: no command.
Watch it; if it is late against its own estimate, apply B3. (Lena: don't stop trucks that don't need
stopping.)

**B3. Inside, confident, can be got out in time.** `EXIT_ZONE`, unless B4 applies. Confirm the effect in
telemetry (the truck's `task` and direction) by the state-aware deadline; retry under a new id; alarm
if it still fails.

**B4. Never send a truck into another closing or closed zone.** If the boundary `EXIT_ZONE` would pick
puts the truck in another zone that is not `OPEN` and that it cannot also clear in time: `HOLD` instead,
raise the can't-clear alarm, and offer remote driving out the other way (L2.52).

**B5. Inside but cannot be got out in time:** too far, interlocked (fault, e-stop, depleted battery),
or under someone's lease. Raise the can't-clear alarm (B9) within 10 s. Still send `EXIT_ZONE` if it can
move at all and B4 allows: a truck that gets out late lets the shot go late rather than not at all.
A leased truck is never commanded; its lease holder gets the alarm with the countdown.

**B6. Outside, approaching: hold before entry.** A truck whose path would cross into the zone before it
reopens, and which cannot pass all the way through before `effective_at` with the margin, is held at a
hold point before the boundary. The `HOLD` goes out when the truck is (6 s + telemetry age + latency
allowance) × speed + margin from the boundary, not at `CLOSING`: a truck far away may never need
stopping. A truck that *can* pass through in time is let through. Once `CLOSED`, every approaching truck
is held.

**B6a. A working truck at a closing zone's boundary.** The draw point ends exactly at the next zone's
boundary, so a truck loading there leaves straight into it when loading ends. A queued `HOLD` may be
dropped, and a retry after loading ends takes up to 6 s, about 12 m inside. Draft rule: if the zone it
would enter is `CLOSED`, or `CLOSING` and the truck cannot pass through in time, take the truck with
`TAKE_CONTROL` as the system. That takes effect at once and interrupts loading (`PROTOCOL.md` §5); with
no drive input the deadman stops it and the lease expires to `HOLDING` after 10 s, which the truck does
not leave by itself. Otherwise queue a `HOLD` and check it when loading ends (open point 6).

**B7. A command on its way can't be recalled.** Stopping an `EXIT_ZONE` in progress takes `HOLD`, not
`RESUME`: `RESUME` is rejected while a task is running (S9), and while another command is within its
1–6 s delay (re-probe Q3). The engine never relies on cancelling a command it has sent.

**B8. Several zones at once.** A truck is judged against every zone that is not `OPEN`; its exit path
must end in an `OPEN` zone (B4); a truck that one zone's rules would move and another's would hold is
held.

**B9. The can't-clear alarm.** Within 10 s of `CLOSING`, or of the data first allowing the conclusion,
whichever is later. It names the action ("Radio the shot firer to hold the shot"), the truck, the zone
and the reason in words. It interrupts (L2.60). It clears itself only when the truck is confirmed
outside, the zone reopens, or the blast is cancelled; never because time passed.

**B10. BAY closing.** `EXIT_ZONE` is refused in BAY, so every truck in BAY gets the can't-clear alarm at
once with "drive it out or hold the shot"; trucks approaching BAY are held before entry (B6).

## The clearance recommendation

**B11.** Per zone that is not `OPEN`, from belief only (invariant 6):
- **NOT CLEAR** if a live or old truck is inside.
- **UNSURE** if no live or old truck is inside, but a silent, contradicted or unknown truck's range
  overlaps it, or the site link is down.
- **CLEAR** only if no truck might be inside and the link is up.

NOT CLEAR and UNSURE both carry "Radio the shot firer to hold the shot" and their reasons. The operator
may record "I've confirmed it's clear" over either, only with a reason; recommendation and override are
both logged.

## When a zone reopens

**B12. Auto-resume** (answer 2), on `CLEARED` or `CANCELLED`: within 15 s, `RESUME` every truck the
system held **for that zone**, confirmed in telemetry, unless it is now held for another zone (B8), has a
lease or a fault, or was also held by an operator. Never resumes into a zone that is not `OPEN` (L4.R5).
An operator's hold is never resumed (L4.R4).

## Link and service

**B13. Link down.** Nothing can be sent. Every zone that is not `OPEN` becomes UNSURE; "link down while
a zone is closing" interrupts. On reconnect, act on the `hello` snapshot at once against the time left.
Commands in flight are replayed by the registry.

**B14. Service restart.** The engine's holds and their reasons are persisted with the command log, so a
restart mid-blast knows which trucks it held and for which zone (L6.1).

## Every decision is logged

**B15.** Each system action is logged as the system, with the rule id, the zone, the truck's belief
(confidence, range, time left, time to clear) and the command's outcome, in the same log as the
operators' (answer 4).

## Open for review

1. **B2 (let confident trucks leave on their own).** Fewer commands and fewer unnecessary stops, but
   one more prediction that can be wrong. The alternative is `EXIT_ZONE` for every truck inside.
2. **B5 (keep evacuating a truck that can't make it in time).** I think yes; it shortens the held shot.
3. **B6's margin.** The trigger distance is 6 s plus the truck's telemetry age at its speed. I'm unsure
   whether the stop itself is instant in the simulator. The re-probe's `HOLD` timings will show it.
4. **Queuing.** The re-probe showed a queued `HOLD` dropped (one sample) and a pending command that
   `RESUME` can't recall. It could not test whether a newer queued command replaces an older one, so
   the engine never queues two different commands on one truck.
5. **B1 for a frozen truck that is really outside.** Holding it costs production until its data
   recovers; the alternative is an operator check. Holding is the safe default.
6. **B6a uses a lease as a brake.** It is the only immediate stop besides `ESTOP`, and unlike `ESTOP` it
   leaves the truck `HOLDING`, resumable by B12. The costs: it interrupts loading, the lease is visible
   to operators as held by "system", and an operator who wants to drive that truck must force-take it.
   The alternative is to accept up to ~12 m of entry and rely on the can't-clear alarm. I lean to the
   lease, but this is your call; it is the one place the system would take manual control.
